product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: one old lady's viewpoint on the fire
review_body:
first and foremost, i love my fire. i've literally worn out my first kindle and my paperwhite is showing signs of the same sorry state. yes, i read a whole lot.
pros:
* finding the back and home buttons is far, far easier than on the paperwhite.
* color. 'nuff said.
* sending documents via whispernet (i suppose that's how it's happening) is ridiculously easy with drag-and-drop.
* both front and back camera capability is a hoot!
* picture quality is almost as good as my digital camera.
* sharing pictures is very, very easy.

cons:
* what's up with the battery life? after fully charging the unit, i gave it my favorite stress test: a trashy romance novel. usually i can sit and read one in an hour or less and still have at least 70% power left (paperwhite). after my so-called test, there was just a shade under 50% power left on the fire. i guess you pay for having color by the battery being less robust.
* i'd heard that despite the advertising, dropping the unit did cause screen damage among other things. proactive choice: i bought an aftermarket screen cover and protecting case. you never know when you'll fumble and drop the unit.

all in all, my most succinct advice would be to determine up front what exactly you want from the fire: speed, capacity, or coolness.

review_headline: so i finally upgraded to an hd. what's different?
review_body:
i had to replace my original kindle -actually the second one as the first was replaced under warranty. both had the same problem with the charger port getting loose and not being able to charge. there was absolutely no other problem, too bad to lose use of something otherwise fine for a small reason like that. i'm not exactly complaining as for my original 99$ i had over 3 years of use between the two. but i do hope this problem has been addressed as i am far from the only person who had it and there were things on the old kindle i cannot recover.

so i've had the new one a week and i'm still adjusting and trying to get things as i want them. i decided to save a few bucks by getting an ad supported one. the ads are not intrusive at all, but also not relevant to me so far. it is definitely worth it to pay for 16 gb. on my last one i was almost always nearly out of memory as i have a lot of books magazines songs and video downloaded as my wifi access is intermittent.

the first thing i noticed were physical. the edges are slightly beveled and the case is all slippery plastic. i prefer the old rubbery back - much easier to hold. the on off button ad ports are now off center - good because i used to accidentally hit the power button. why oh why are the volume buttons physical buttons on the outside instead of on the screen? i rarely ever changed the volume - do people change the volume so often that there was demand for this? it annoys me as almost every way i hold it i feel those buttons.

the screen is crisper , noticeable when watching videos. the sound seems the same though the speakers now face back. to me the sound is more muffled due to that. which brings me to my first big complaint. the sound seems calibrated wrong. i have it all the way up and it is not loud. i could never set the old kindle above 75%. i cannot use the included alarm function as even at 100% i can barely hear it. i have no hearing issues.

having cameras is a nice addition and so is bluetooth. now i can attach wirelessly to my printer and speaker. location based services are now available. a microphone is now included-don't know that will use it but who knows.

it was easy if a bit consuming to redownload all my apps and media and try to remember all the passwords. i did lose some apps that aren't compatible with the new os.

the included maps app is okay. i'll probably like it more when i get used to it.

the keyboard is updated, it now includes emoji. you can sit it in half if you're a thumb typer.

some typing issues are improved - it's much easier to cut and paste and finally i do not have to type my entire email in every time. little tweaks can be big.

the battery seems to drain a little faster but charges a little faster. the included charger seems a little sturdier. my last 2 included ones didn't last long.

still discovering what's new. not the most technical review, just giving you an idea of what's changed if you have an earlier kindle.

review_body: this tablet is fast and works pretty well. for the price i paid its very hard to beat. the one thing i don't like about it is the way the ui works. there is no home button like on an apple device, so learning to use it takes some hunting around. it does have child profiles which is a bonus, but enabling that functionality further frustrates navigation. just logging off one profile and onto another is not intuitive at all. you can log off the child profiles but there is no log off from the non-child profiles, you just lock the device, wake it up and then select the profile icon for the main user and then are presented with the other profiles as options. very counter-intuitive. it would be better to have all profiles presented on the unlock screen. to amazon's credit, the device pulled my kids profiles off my firetv account with a single question/answer. besides the ui issues which one can eventually learn, the device has excellent sound (stereo too), excellent screen resolution and color and snappy performance for games, video, browsing and other functions. i streamed a movie from my prime account and it started instantly and ran smoothly and i have an older router and many wireless devices. i would give it 5 stars were it not for the clunky ui navigation issues. i suspect amazon is not done tinkering with it and will probably introduce nav improvements. even if they don't, once you get used to the way it works its a pretty good little tablet.

review_headline: ok, but i wouldn't buy it again
review_body:
this is the first tablet i ever bought. it has not been a great experience for me, but my four-year-old daughter enjoys it enough.

there are four main irritations: 1) the ever-present ads, 2) the lack of customization, 3) the slow wi-fi, and 4) the poor battery. each and every time that either i or my daughter turns on the kindle fire hd, we get an ad that is very easy to click on. this is definitely not good for a young person who might take some time understanding what to click on. users are not able to customize their interface very much. for example, i cannot put my favorite apps or videos or website on the home screen. nor can users download apps from anywhere but amazon, which really cuts down on the choices. the wi-fi is painfully slow at times. all the other wi-fi devices in our home work perfectly well, but the kindle fire hd creeps along, struggling to download apps and load webpages. lastly, the battery life is just awful. we need to charge it after just about every use. this tablet cannot handle decent-sized games or many other apps.

nevertheless, this tablet is a fun diversion for my four-year-old daughter. there are a few free games that we have found. they are age-appropriate and not filled with ads. we've bought a few apps, as well. in retrospect, i probably should have gone with a refurbished tablet that had a little more "umph" in it.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body: my review is more for the support of amazon then the product.  first i will say that the product seems to be a good product at a good price.  purchased 2 tablets for our kids with the main purpose of gaming, music and music.  pure toy for them with of course computer/tablet skills learning.  tablets seem to do everything that they claim and as an adult function great.  2 issues however.  first, both original units charging ports went bad within 2 months.  for a product that you need to constantly charge day in day out this is not something that should fail.  looking further into it this is a common issue with these units.  was replaced and received new tablets.  second, broken screen.  my son dropped his tablet and broke his screen (anybody who owns a phone or tablet knows this happens).  this is not covered by warranty (which i never asked for that btw, but was told several times by amazon support) and amazon does not offer any support for a replacement/repair.  i was simply looking for a replacement screen to purchase and either replace myself or get replaced.  this i find confusing considering that this is a common issue in todays phone/tablet world with touch screens?  they will offer you a replacement tablet at a so called "reduced rate", but do not support their product with replacement or repair.  i guess you get what you payed for and amazon believes that these things are very disposable?  nice job amazon!  so the moral is to do your research on everything before purchasing.  buy locally too so that you can actually deal with a human.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
let's get this out of the way right now: the fire hd 7 does not compare well against any of its pricier competitors, and that's mostly due to amazon's extremely limited fire os. if you're looking for a truly full featured tablet experience, you would be better served looking at an ipad or a more expensive android device running a proper version of the operating system.

this is device that's defined in many ways by what you can't do. you can't download apps from the google play store. there isn't a default youtube app. there's relatively poor support for common third-party services like dropbox, and accessing google services is either impossible or requires workarounds. you can't even use and login to chrome without going through a process that's likely to seem daunting to non-technical users. and if you are one of those technical users, don't expect to be able to root a 4th gen fire to turn it into a proper android device. it's not happening.

that said, the fire is competent in its own little niche. the device pops out of sleep quickly and fire os is a smooth and fairly seamless experience. i haven't had any crashes or other oddities that diminish the experience. unsurprisingly, it works flawlessly if you're mainly interested in making use of amazon services like prime streaming or kindle books. amazon's app store has only a fraction of the apps that are available on google play (and many popular or common ones are missing), but the selection isn't terrible and there's a good mix of software for most basic needs.

the hardware itself ranges from "pretty good" to "god awful." the quad core processor, at this price point, is a nice piece of kit. it's good enough to make the fire hd feel snappier and more responsive than a cheap budget table has any right to be. the screen is a high point as well. the pixel density on the 7" version isn't spectacular, but it looks fine and the overall quality is good. the case is cheap feeling plastic with a textured matte finish. it's not terrible, but you'll be disappointed if you're used to higher quality tablets or phones. the cameras are so terrible that they border on useless. they're acceptable (barely) if you only intend to use them for video chat, but expect photo quality that's on par with ten year old feature phones. they're that bad.

on the whole, the fire hd is decidedly unimpressive. it feels like there's a great budget device here, but the limitations mean that it never crosses over that magical line that turns it into a great value. you get exactly what you pay for, and at this price that's fine. just don't expect to be blown away or to receive a device that'll give tablets costing twice as much a run for their money.

review_body:
i love the kindle fires, and fireos -- it's simple and intuitive i think, and not bloated with settings to configure like many other android flavors. despite some negative reviews about amazons app store being less than desirable, i've been able to find 99% of the apps i needed there anyways.

i bought a kindle fire hdx 7" around december of 2013 and love it. and when i spotted the fire hd 7 on sale for $79 a few days ago i decided to pounce. we've been thinking about getting a second one for the kids anyways and $79 is fantastic. my thoughts below will be more of a comparison between the two and what i like/dis-like about each.

* the fire hd 7 is thicker, and though i don't think it weighs more than my fire hdx 7 -- it feels heavier because of the extra bulk.
* the hd 7's white plastic case it somewhat slippery from time to time as well and the tablet can slip out of your hands as you're maneuvering it. the white case also feels more like an after thought rather than part of the construction -- it feels a bit loose (not detachably loose though) maybe is a good way to put it.
* the performance of the hd 7 is comparible to the hdx 7, but feels a bit more sluggish to me. but still no complaints, it's miles ahead of other android tablets i've purchased in the past.
* the power and volume buttons are the biggest issue in my mind, and are the reason for 4 instead of 5 stars from me. on the old hdx 7 the buttons are rounded and concave'd, and inset in the design and are easy to press with a finger tip. however they are rectangular and protrude from the hd 7 and very different locations compared to the hdx 7. the power button is particularly tiny and sometimes difficult to press. sometimes i feel like i might break it. i'm not overly impressed with the volume rocker either as it's also stiff and somewhat difficult to press.
* the last slightly annoying thing about the hd 7 is the lack of auto-brightness. it's not hard to set, but is annoying to have to constantly adjust in order to save power.

overall though i give the hd 7 4/5 stars and would have no problem recommending it. especially at the $79 price-tag i paid.st in order to save power. overall though i give the hd 7 4/5 stars and would have no problem recommending it. especially at the $79 price-tag i paid.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
my fourth kindle!

i've purchased these ever since they were originally released and love this product. each generation gets better and better.... and without the corresponding leap in cost as the features have improved. i use mine every single day - both for reading and watching amazon prime videos as well as xfinity and hbogo. i have priced and considered the ipad each time but still but the kindle because for the cost and quality, it's hard to beat.

the feature i most love is the text-to-speech function. i use it everyday to and from work to keep up with my reading on the one hour drive. i just plug it into my aux outlet in the car and get to enjoy many more books and authors than i would normally have time for.

also, a note about the books: i am the very example of the customer who enjoys all of the free books available each month. i shop every couple of weeks and download a few so i have plenty to choose from. but, i have several times enjoyed the author or story so much that i have gone back and purchased the entire series - so that marketing plan is working! seriously, this is a terrific way to find new authors with very little risk, and helps keep my library stocked at all times.

i also purchase several books each month from my "usual" authors, but am really unwilling to pay more than $10 a book, so i really have to enjoy that author to spend the money. i go through probably 30 books a month? so the costs could really add up over time. my least favorite purchases are those that are over $10 and do not have text-to-speech enabled - i have to really like the author to buy that book!

i have also found great use for the ability to upload your own documents and being able to access on the unit. i have an online cookbook that contains 100s of recipes (from familycookbookproject.com) and reload this document and view on-screen often. yes, i could pull from the net on this unit, but find the actual document more helpful when i have limited cell service. i've also used this unit to view some of my pictures i've loaded to the amazon cloud - i take hundreds of pictures and use this as an online backup. so inexpensive and reliable!

i also use the device to watch my favorite shows and movies. the quality of the movies from amazon prime library is superior - they download very quickly and video quality is amazing. the selection is still a bit sparse, though improving all the time.

less amazing are the offerings from xfinity to go, but that is because of xfinity and not amazon. does it not make you crazy when all of the many, many, many commercials from xfinity stream perfectly without a glitch, yet the shows look terrible? i just keep telling myself that soon comcast and their ilk will be a thing of the past as new methods of delivery take their place. however, when xfinity works, it looks terrific.

i did not purchase wifi but that is only because cell service is terrible where i live and i didn't think i would get good value. i will probably take the plunge with the next unit. oh, and i have had 4 units personally (and given 2 as gifts), primarily due to upgrading or replacing after accidents. my first unit had a battery that stopped charging after almost 2 years and was replaced free. units 2 and 3 both met horrible ends in accidents - one a car accident and the other when i dropped squarely on its face. my current unit has both a screen protector and extended warranty. its a very durable unit, but i do walk around with it every day, throw it in my purse or backpack, etc, and drop it a lot more than is good for it. do yourself a favor - buy the warranty.

i highly recommend and will definitely keep purchasing these products

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: nowhere even close to fire tv's level of quality
review_body:
i'm a huge fan of amazon's fire tv, so i expected to be blown away by the company's tablet offerings. i mean, amazon's tablets seem to be immensely popular, while virtually no one i've spoken to locally even knows that the fire tv is, so surely these tablets are solid, right? well, while i've only had the fire hd 7 for a day, and i know that the right software update could make a ton of difference in the future, this review is based on my initial experience with the device, and that experience is anything but positive.

now, for the pluses and minuses:

+ the display, while not full hd, is actually quite nice.

- getting a movie that you downloaded over wi-fi to play offline isn't as intuitive as it should be. unless i'm doing something wrong, launching a movie offline when you've already downloaded it seems to only work from the carousel. trying to play it anywhere else just generates an error, and even launching from the carousel makes it seem like the device is locked up. (there's no indication that it's loading the movie. the ui just becomes completely unresponsive until playback begins. this isn't the case on fire tv.)
- haptic feedback would've been nice. the ui just feels lifeless and lacks sufficient feedback to your input, in my opinion.
- the carousel ui is a colossal waste of space.
- the ui generally just needs more context menus (ideally by long-pressing).
- these tablets don't have nearly enough storage for what they are. they should've had sd card support. sure, i don't *have* to download hd versions of my movies to watch offline, but i should have the option to do so, because i bought hd movies in order to watch them in hd. being able to only download three hd movies onto this thing (16 gb version - thank god i didn't settle for the 8 gb version) before it's too full for another download is just ridiculous. speaking of which, the menu for managing storage shouldn't be buried in settings. you should be able to long-press on a movie from anywhere on the ui and delete it.

yes, i understand that fire tv is plugged in and isn't relying on battery power, but there's no reason for the fire tablet experience to be this much worse than the fire tv experience. i'll update my review if things improve in the future, but i can't help but feel that the experience simply won't get that much better. while i realize that it'd be at the expense of app compatibility, i honestly wish that amazon would dump android and work with something more lightweight for the underlying os. this thing feels like an android tablet...and not an especially good one.able to long-press on a movie from anywhere on the ui and delete it.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body: update 5/7/2015: this thing is getting more frustrating by the day. it's already giving me warnings that it's nearly full. i guess that's partially my fault for getting the 8gb version....but i never imagined i'd be able to nearly fill this thing with just a few children's apps. they shouldn't even sell the thing with this low of a capacity.   it's still very dodgy performance....sometimes it's speedy, but most of the time it's slow. still take a ridiculous amount of time to download an app. this alone has cause both me and my daughter a great deal of frustration (kids aren't known to be that patient as it is).   the app selection is horrible for the child subscription service that's offered....free time unlimited?!? what a joke...it's very limited. majority of the apps are low low low quality. very few truly educational apps. and once again...they take forever to download and install.   another quirk is that some apps, even though they are child centric, still have to be installed from the adult profile. but the thing is...when you download it from the adult profile, and then add it to the kids profile, it appears that you have to redownload it. no clue what that's about. so you ultimately have to wait twice as long now before you can finally allow your child to play the app.   the sluggishness of downloading apps means you really have to plan ahead and curate apps for your child way ahead of when they're going to actually play on the thing. this is very frustrating because the apps on the children's profile literally offer no description of exactly what they are. so you have to select the app, wait for it to download...then open the app and determine if it's an app you even want or that your child will even enjoy! this is beyond frustrating and really really kills the enjoyment of the device for the parent and the child.   i really want to return this thing and purchase a table that has regular old android os on it. but despite it's many many many many flaws....mychild would have a fit if it wasn't around. hopefully i can do a switcheroo on her but i'll have to find a green bumper case so she's none the wiser....well....she'll probably be wise to it very quick once she sees how much better it is.   i feel horrible that i recommended this thing to so many parents before i even owned one myself. that was definitely irresponsible of me :( ... it might explain some of the dirty looks i've been getting.    original review below here: purchased this for the sole purpose of giving it to my toddler. kid's mode is not at all what it's billed to be. the primary problem is that the app store is still fully accessible to the child and they'll spend more time download each and every app that they see instead of playing with the apps that you've installed for them. it's frustrating that there's no way to preview and see exactly what the app is when you're in the kid's mode too. it also takes a ridiculous amount of time to download the apps! so frustrating!  the next huge deal breaker is that you have to repurchase apps you've already purchased from the google play store. the same freaking apps! i have rebuy all these child focused apps that i'd already purchased for our little one to play with on my android phone and tablet. this is beyond infuriating. amazon really needs to come up with a way for their app store to cohabitate with the google play store. no one should have to repurchase the same apps for the same platform simply because amazon doesn't want to put the google play store onto their devices. and no, i don't want to/shouldn't have to root my device just to do something that should be provided as an option.  getting out of kid's mode is not intuitive or easy. you have to push the power button off and then back on to get to the lock screen, then select the adult profile you want to use.  it's a really sluggish device overall. the fireos skin (i refuse to call it an operating system because it's simply a clunky skin on top of android) is very unintuitive and slow. so you browse apps, touch the app, and then wait....and wait....and wait....and wait....for it to finally download. oh yeah, no 5ghz wifi band use here....only 2.4ghz......  everything is so slow. i don't understand it. it shouldn't be this sluggish based on the specs.  lucky i got it on sale for seventy nine dollars.....i'd be really upset had i paid full retail. no one should pay full retail for this thing.

love it! i upgraded to the fire from the paperwhite. while the paperwhite is excellent as a straight reader (i still have mine) the fire offers so much more. i've been using it instead of my ipod to listen to music while at work, so i have one less device to carry. i love that there is a separate place for documents (pdfs, etc.) than for books. makes it easier to find and manage my documents. i love the ease and speed with which i can move things from cloud to fire and vice versa. i love the capabilities in "shopping" which allow me to access more areas of amazon than the "kindle store" on my paperwhite did. i can order physical items (rather than being limited to just digital) and track orders. very convenient!

i love love love streaming music and movies - thousands and thousands free (because i am a prime customer). prime and fire make a very a happy pair!

it would be a plus if it had more storage space. i have to be careful not to put several seasons of tv shows (like downton abbey :-d) on it or i run out of space - videos take up much more space than books and music. on the other hand, having limited storage keeps me from cluttering it up - keeping a limited number of items actually on the device makes housekeeping easier.

wonderful device - love it!

review_body:
the fire hd 7 is so much more than the original hd 7 that was released in september 2012 that there's really no comparison. this is a new fire tablet from the ground up. the quad-core 1.5 ghz cpu screams past the original fire hd's dual-core 1.2 ghz cpu. the hd 7's 1280x800 display is noticeably sharper than the original hd 7's 1024x600. and they've added a rear-facing hd camera to go with the front camera. compared to the original fire hd 7, the only loss is the hdmi port, which, with wireless devices like the fire tv stick, isn't as valuable as it once was.

the fire hd 7 is a powerful tablet that's a welcome addition to the family of kindle fires. typically, entry-level products are stripped down versions of bigger, more powerful products, but the fire hd 7 has virtually all the features of the other fires, but at a lower price.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: storage space not even close to advertised.
review_body:
initial presentation, fantastic. speed and responsiveness, spectacular. build quality, awesome. screen crispness, wunderbar.
why only two stars? i understand 8gb formatted is approximately 7.37gb usable. i understand i can expect a gig of os and bloatware. but when i first booted the device, the storage capacity showed as 0.95gb used for os and bloatware, and 4.11gb free. 4.11gb + 0.95gb = 5.06gb. where is my remaining 7.37gb-5.06gb=2.31gb worth of space? that's huge when you're only starting with "8gb." i called in to amazon who explained that the remaining 2.31gb was additional hidden system resources.

i purchased this with the understanding that i had limited space, and more than likely had room for only one 720p hd movie at a time, which would be approximately 5gb. negative.

i also purchased this during a deal promotion. i overnighted the fire to myself for a trip today. amazon would not let me purchase a 16gb version at the promotion price since the promotion was ended.

talk about false advertising. of all the things i do with amazon - buy, sell, prime, prime video, prime music, etc. this is a top 10 sore spot for me.

buyer beware - 8gb is actually 4.15gb usable.

review_body:
we ordered a kindle fire during black friday when they were on sale for $79. the original intent was to give it to the kids (5 and 3) as a tablet that they could use. it turns out that not only do the kids love it, but i do too!

physically, the kindle doesn't seem that impressive at first. it's lightweight and it's not made of the shiny metal (read, instantly scratched) material that more expensive electronics, like an ipad are made of. you wonder how it'll perform since it's so light.

it performs great. it's not the fastest tablet i've ever seen, at least not when loading an app, but once it's loaded it works just fine. reading is easy on the kindle, and you can adjust the screen brightness from within the book you are reading, which is very handy.

one thing i'll note is that it was tough to learn the controls for me. we are an apple family for the most part, and while the controls are similar, they aren't exactly the same. the transition was a little rough for me, but the kids picked it up right away. there is a ton of online support, help and forums, so if you ever get stuck, you can just search for a solution - and there's a web browser built-in, so you can even do that searching on the kindle.

my absolute favorite feature is a built-in app called freetime. you can set up profiles for your kids, so you can choose which content they have access to. we also have an ipad, but it doesn't have anything comparable to freetime, so we always wind up reaching for the kindle to give to the kids for their preschool games because they get into apps (like my email) that they shouldn't get into on the ipad. i'm so glad the kindle solves that problem!

my only criticism is that the screen is very difficult to see in bright light, like when you're outdoors. it's not really something you can grab on the way to the beach to read your favorite book while relaxing on the sand. even with the brightness turned all the way up, you're still stuck if the sun is too bright. i'm sure there are ways around that, but for me, it's easier to just grab my old kindle touch or an actual book.

review_body:
i moved from barnes & noble's nook tablet to this kindle fire, and am glad i did! i love the versatility of the kindle. one of my primary reasons for switching was the affordability of books on amazon versus the higher-priced books through b&n. i have found the same books on amazon are usually a dollar or two cheaper than on b&n. i am also very pleased with the android interface. the display is crisp and sharp.

the only downside i have found so far is the power button on the kindle. it is very small and cumbersome, on the top right of the device. this is the only negative i have encountered, however, and just takes some getting used to. i disliked how limiting the nook was and always felt like it was set up in permanent parental mode. there just is not much flexibility at all in nook's interface. the kindle has far surpassed my expectations. i am able to customize it and no longer feel as though i have a babysitter. highly recommended.

review_headline: parental controls miss the mark and make the tablet pointless for older kids
review_body:
would return this if we could. the parental controls look great. they apparently provide a degree of control and flexibility unavailable elsewhere and yet they miss the mark in unforgivable ways.

a child account is completely unable to use a web browser under any circumstances and is also unable to use email. i cannot understand why these cannot be enabled but they make the device useless for schoolwork and undermine the value of the tablet. don't think about switching your child to an adult account because amazon family accounts can only have two adults in them. grown up children at home? tough. trying to fix the shortcomings of parental controls? also tough. the only option is to create a standalone account that cannot share any content. might as well have bought a standard android tablet or a cheap kindle reader. the former would do what the fire should do while the latter will more cheaply do what the fire is actually usable for.

extremely disappointed because a small number of fundamental software design decisions completely ruin the device.

review_headline: a good tablet for a reasonable price
review_body: overall: this is a good tablet for the price.  i bought the kindle fire 16gb to take advantage of the amazon prime kindle lending library feature that comes with my prime membership. i really didn't expect much from the device having seen early versions of the kindle. i was pleasantly surprised, it has full tablet functionality. some features work well, some not so well. lets take a look...  what works well:  books: reading is a joy on the kindle fire. i was a bit leery of the 7" screen when ordering given i have bad eyesight, but once it arrived and i opened my books i was able to read them as well as i could on my 9.7" screen ipad with the kindle app. the text can be customised in many ways; font size, choice of font face, colour of text and background, margin width, line spacing, brightness and text-to-speech are all options. highlighting, note-taking, copying text and sharing excerpts straight from the page are all fast and simple. the x-ray feature lets the reader drill down into segments and terms commonly notated. a dictionary (in your choice of language) is called up with a long press on any word. searching is a snap; no more fumbling through pages looking a word or phrase. and of course pages can be bookmarked. i have my goodreads account linked with amazon and i update my progress as i read, as well as post status updates. the kindle fire is a winner in the book department.  videos: amazon prime members can enjoy the full features of amazon instant video on the kindle fire. the app store also has free apps for hulu plus and netflix. youtube can be viewed via third-party apps or the silk web browser. the speakers are good quality and rather loud at full volume. the video image quality is shockingly good for a tablet on the lower end of the price scale.  games: the app store has a good selection of free games, and paid games as well. many popular titles are available and i wasn't disappointed.  music: amazon prime members can add music from the primemusic library to their kindle for free as a feature of the membership. prime stations are also available under the music tab, so members can pick a genre and let the music play. you can also migrate your own music collection to the device via the usb cable. sound quality is quite good.  newsstand: i received 6 months of the washington post for free...not sure if that is a prime feature or a kindle feature. the newsstand has occasional discount offers on magazine subscriptions and there is a wide variety from which to choose. i haven't used this feature much, but what i have used has worked well.  docs: for a lower-end tablet, they're surprisingly good. this is where i tested the speech recognition function. in the word processor, every one of the sentences i dictated was taken down correctly, even recognising and capitalising 'rumpelstiltskin'. granted i did enunciate well as i normally would when using this feature in any device. it took some trial and error to figure out table customisation in the word processor and some of the other less used features. in the spreadsheet application i dictated some formulas, all of which were taken down correctly. (one does have to know correct terms for signs and symbols.) hand entering formulas is a bit clumsy and having 10-key option would be a big help. some of the pdfs i viewed were inconsistent but overall this feature ranks 'good' with me.  what's not so hot:  photos: the camera on the kindle fire is pretty darn bad unless you're taking close-ups. the zoom feature doesn't 'zoom' much at all in my estimation and it doesn't capture fine detail. if you're on holiday, at a party or anywhere where you're planning to take pictures, bring another camera ready device because this doesn't cut it.  battery life: very disappointing. if you're not using the device, power it off. don't just turn off the screen, fully power off the device. i'm on my kindle a few hours a day, and when i am, i'm typically reading with some occasional internet usage. if i don't fully power the device off when i'm not using it, one charge will usually last a day with a little bit left over. if it's a weekend or a day when i'm doing a lot of reading, i'll run out of power...unless i fully turn off the tablet when i'm not using it. i don't know what it's doing in the background that drains it so, but most (not all) of my settings are optimised to save power.  overall i'm very pleased with my purchase. i found my ipad to large and clumsy to tote around town when i just wanted to read my e-books, and the kindle fire is just the right size to be unobtrusive, yet is still easy to read and has all the basic functionality i need, plus much more. the charging cord has a usb connection which allows it to charge in any usb outlet, including the adapter in my car, so i can keep it charged while i'm driving and unplug it when i reach my destination. it's quite versatile and well worth the money. i did not pay extra to have the 'special offers' on the lockscreen removed and i do not find them at all bothersome.

review_headline: about time!  a tablet that thinks it's a giant.
review_body:
if you are on the fence, please, don't go by the negative reviews here. many of the reviewers are nitpicking, and did not read, before purchasing, the specs this tablet offers. familiarize yourself with what this tablet can and cannot do, and you are more than halfway to an informed decision as to whether to buy or not. then you can decide based on your needs from a well-made tablet.

this tablet is zippy! the battery life is very good (let the tablet die out, then charge and do that again for improved battery life). the speakers give a good sound to your movies and music; with headphones, this tablet rocks (i suggest buy n7 music player)!

the screen is gorgeous for such a low-end tablet, and will make movies pop, text stand clear and your overall enjoyment a pleasure. if you don't lose sight of the fact that this is an under $150 tablet (7" model), you will enjoy this well-made tablet.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: purchased for 5 year old daughter. ok for what it is, os needs definite improvement.
review_body:
i purchased this kindle fire hd for my 5 year-old daughter. as an adult who can be safely considered a tech-geek, here are the pros and cons for normal folks:

pros:

1. my daughter loves it.
2. the profile controls and amazon freetime controls to restrict usage are detailed and really exemplary.
3. it's inexpensive.
4. amazon freetime has a lot of games, videos, and apps. the monthly fee is nominal.

cons:

1. the ui for main os is so disjointed and ugly that i'd almost prefer it if it were simply command-line based.
2. the actual freetime ui is similarly disorganized, and definitely confusing for anyone who is the age of my daughter. it just throws too much right in her face that she can't figure out where everything is.
3. my wife has difficulty figuring out how to navigate through the ui, so if there's a problem finding something or doing something, i'm the one that has to figure it out. ios, this is not.
4. the tablet stutters a non-trivial amount of time. it also sometimes becomes unresponsive for short periods.

overall:

the truth is that i'm not willing to hand my daughter an ipad that costs triple the price, no matter how well protected it is. so, this is the next best thing at her age. amazon freetime is a good idea with great parental controls, but definitely needs more polish. amazon, please fix fireos. it's hideous.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: great as a tablet, less so as a reader
review_body:
the fire is excellent as a tablet. i love the games, the accessibility to the web and the clarity of the screen. the lack of apps is sad, but should improve as the fire becomes more popular. the sound is great. it is light, easily portable and fits comfortably in my hand. i am very disappointed in it as a reader though. seriously, amazon? losing features on a signature product is very bad form. not being able to access the collections i already have established on other devices, no search function for the ebooks i have, having to scroll through over 1200 ebooks to add them to collections i've already made, not allowing collections in the cloud, not being able to find if i already have a book without having to go back to the website. i am also not happy with the automatic connection with goodreads. just because an ebook accidentally opens because the screen is touch-sensitive doesn't mean i am "currently reading" it. trying to find to special offers after unlocking the screen is also a pain.
all in all, i love the fire and would never return it. i consider it a worthwhile investment and plan to enjoy it for years to come, just as i have my first gen kindle and kindle dx.

review_body: very upset about this situation. i'd rather give no stars. bought this kindle last summer to watch movies on my nightshift when i work doubles, after about 4-5 months it started turning off by itself after i unlock screen, open apps, just randomly turning off. sometimes i get an app to open and load but as soon as i touch the screen it turns off and does not restart. if i press the power button to turn it back on, it shows the kindle fire loading screen as always when you first turn it on then turns back off, can't even make it to the unlock screen. finally after a few months of dealing with that and trying to reset my kindle, the problem continued. i baby my electronics, so i never overcharged my kindle, it doesn't make sense as to why it would suddenly give me such issues. i called tech support yesterday, they said i have 85 days left on my warranty so they'll send me a refurbished version, guaranteeing i won't have any problems, and i just opened it up and already have a problem! the back is loose, the battery drains very fast and gets very hot after 2 minutes of use. about 1% of battery drain per minute. where as my old kindle i fully charged last night, played a couple games, left on all night and is still at 95%. if i pay 160+$ for a 16gb kindle, and it craps out on me only less than half a yr after i buy it, i expect my money back or a brand new kindle, not a refurbished piece of crap that seems ta be worse than my old kindle! not sure if i wanna send my old one back to them. i think i'd rather deal with my old kindle constantly turning off when it wants and only way i get it back on is if i plug it in, rather than keep a crappy refurbished one that's absolutely not worth the 160$ i had spent on my original kindle in the first place. how is that even fair?

review_headline: no repair options for the amazon fire
review_body:
amazon bills this product as being sturdier than the competition, so buying these tablets for my kids for christmas seemed like a no-brainer, but what they don't tell you is that these products cannot be repaired. my eight-year-old cracked his screen. our local repair shop doesn't deal with amazon fire's because they aren't popular enough for them to bother with. i contacted amazon about repair possibilities and they said: "it’s amazon’s policy to offer our customers a replacement device rather than repair their original device." then they say they cannot further discuss the matter via email, you must contact them by phone. i called the number provided and had to provide all sort of info only to have to be transferred to another department (a customer service pet peeve of mine. they knew the problem why didn't they provide me a phone number to speak directly to the department that would handle this?). after going through everything, the customer rep said the broken screen would not be covered under warranty and the device would need to be replaced. amazon does not provide any to repair these devices. since they knew that would be hard to hear, they provide a discount for the replacement; a discount so small that the price of a replacement was still significantly more expensive that the price of the tablet when i originally bought it. you'd have to be an idiot to rebuy an all new device knowing this would likely happen again (i feel like an idiot for buying this device the first time around).

i feel amazon is irresponsible for selling a device like this with no way to repair it. buyer beware!

review_body:
so today my kindle died. it wouldn't turn on and would only flash the opening screen. i rebooted several times then chatted with tech for a fix. they had me reboot several times and then declared it dead. they of course offered me a replacement at 150% of what i paid for this at christmas 2013 and an astronomical 14$ off of the regular price. 15 months old and. pfft . no recourse. the wont fix it, they wont prorate some sort of replacement, they basically just said you are s.o.l. so i filled out the evaluation after the chat and up popped a screen that said we would still like to talk to you about this. so i put in my number and they called and said how can i help you. well you should know since you asked me to call no? chit chat with call receiver who forwards me to tech who says your kindle is dead. i can sell you a new one for 14$ off regular price. you are kidding me.
and here's the thing. i own 2 other kindles. another one of these and a 8.9 32 gb. overall i have spent 700-800 dollars on merchandise that will probably end up being very expensive paperweights. maybe this is the future, i don't know. i have folks on my block who have had their kindles for years and handed them down to their kids. i thought it was a good buy. i thought surely amazon stands behind their homegrown products. the last tech told me the average life of electronics is 2-3 years, well then your warranty should be 2 years so i can enjoy the average not 1 year so you can keep me in a buying loop in perpetuity. i will not be buying any more kindles. i'm not sure any other product will be better and have been avoiding apple products, but i am going to try one and see if it lasts longer than 15 months. and if it does then amazon will have lost me forever as a tech consumer. was it worth the 30-40 bucks they could have discounted on a new unit? only time will tell.

review_body:
i, too, saw the advertisments for how wonderfully strong the kindle hd was, and had to have one. i received it on march 17th, and on march 28th it slipped out of my hands when i was getting into my car. i had placed it into a neoprene case to protect it, and after seeing all of the impressive falls in the commercial, i figured that everything would be a-ok. but, no, the corner that the kindle fell on was now seperated from the back!! what the ....
i called customer service who informed me that dropping the kindle was not covered, and there wsn't anything that she could do for me, her hands were tied. i then called capital one to figure out if there was anything they could help me with. i had purchased this item on a 5 payment plan and had 4 payments left to pay!! it was 2 weeks old. the credit card company lady called amazon for me, and then i got back on with the amazon representative, who informed me that there wasn't anything she could do for me. then she went away for a while and when she came back on the line, she offered that i could return the kindle for a refund, but next time, if i wanted to purchase another kindle i would have to pay full price for it!! are you kidding me? i assured her that would not be a problem, that i would never consider buying another kindle no matter how it was financed. i am supposed to be getting a return lable in my email, so we will see how this all turns out.

review_body: i got my fire hd7 with 8gb storage a little over a month ago, and i have already gotten down to 10% available storage.  i did take about 1.7gb of videos and used 1.86gb of games, but when i connected my fire to a computer, the computer indicated that there were 782mb free out of 5.05gb!  since 8gb was advertised, i expected it to say 782mb free of 8gb.  if you have your heart set on getting a fire tablet, i recommend the 16gb version, but ultimately, i recommend the samsung galaxy tab 4.  the strangest feature on the thing might be a glitch, is that when you plug it in and it's off, it automatically boots up.  the main reason i gave this a 3 star rating instead of a one or two star, is because of the handy feature that lets you drag your finger (or stylus) across the on-screen keyboard to type and despite other reviews, it has a good cpu speed.  update: if you look at the storage section of the specifications, you will notice that it says: 8 gb (4.5 gb available to user) or 16 gb (11.6 gb available to user) of internal storage.  i do not think it would have been hard for amazon to put in a memory card slot for upgradable storage.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
hello-

i have been a fire user for a year or two before this device was released to the public... and not having a phone or any piece of technology; it was greatly welcomed. let's take this review step by step starting with the build-

build (7/10)

so the device is wrapped in a layer of plastic with a strong glass for the screen. this plastic is not strong at all and is also a fingerprint magnet. this is why i took of some points. however, it claimed it could be dropped off of a car and not scratch and for the 4 months of abuse it's been through it has shown no signs of damage.

apps (4/10)

the new fire runs off of a new fire os now and that means that it has a new app store.. now this app store is already lacking some of the bigger apps already (ex instagram, clash of clans etc.) but now even less because of the new os. they said that more than 200 apps are added everyday but none really of my interests. i'm sure it will grow but for now it isn't very impressive.

performance (8/10)

okay so it has a quad core processor in the device which makes it lightning fast and i really have to give it to amazon on this one.. there is virtually no lag in regular everyday use. also it has two dolby graded speakers on the back (speakers sound amazing some of the best i've heard on a tablet) also amazon has included new "emoji" characters to the keyboard a nice upgrade if you are into "emojing"

camera (3/10)

so one of the biggest new features it has is the new rear facing camera! this practically won me over. but then i got to use it... little did i know it is only a 2 megapixel camera!!!! it sucks!! it is one of the worst i have ever seen i will tell you, do not buy this if you are looking for a tablet with a good camera! (same goes for the front facing camera as well it is no better)

now i've said enough bad things let's look at the cool features they addedthis time-

- app collections
-"emojis"
-nice crystal screen very bright and vibrant
-a little bit of customization but nothing exciting (no wallpapers etc)
-voice command
-very fast
-lots a bug fixes from the previous models
-one month free prime (at time of review)
-firefly

now for some disappointing cons-

- no mayday on these models at this time
-bad cameras
-plastic shell
-lack of customizations
- only comes with 16 gb which is fine but it can get tight.

so that is about it... would i recommend this to a friend... yeah... i probably would. just not for the camera.

(ps. not much has changed about the reading experience it is still as good as the previous models)

hope this review helps you decide!

the price is amazing, so yes i would recommend it only if you think it suits your needs!

thanks for reading
- sent from my fire hd

review_body:
this is my second kindle fire hd. i got this one a few months ago and my husband is now using my first one, from a few generations back, almost exclusively to download, then read and simultaneously listen to books.

i use this every night and very much like its versatility. i first check all my news sources, then read through twitters posts, play a few games, and read books, all the while listening to classical music via the pandora app. (the music stays on regardless of what else you're doing on the kindle, unless you deliberately stop it.) there's an exception to that: now and then the kindle -- for reasons entirely inexplicable to me -- makes the music cut out and i have to go to the app and restart it. (the sound quality, not incidentally, has improved some from my previous model as well.)

here and there other apps hang up as well, but not all that frequently. that's a defect of sorts, i guess, but it haven't been serious enough for me to contact kindle support about it.

though i don't use the camera all the time, the front and back camera on this model (as opposed to just a front camera from my previous model) is a great improvement and now allows not just for skype use but for regular picture-taking. the screen resolution is also excellent.

i deliberately don't do email on the kindle, and don't allow it to track my location. i also don't own a smartphone, and don't want one. but i'd very much miss my kindle fire hd if it were, for some reason, taken from me. besides using it every night at home, i really like being able to take it with me to appointments, etc., when/where i know i'll have to sit and wait for a while. though i'm still very much a paper-and-ink book person, it's so much easier to read a book with the kindle in such circumstances -- and/or to dip into several books -- than to take one or more actual physical books along to wherever i'm going.

that amazon is producing these sophisticated littlemachines and offering them for the relatively modest price they're asking is a boon, particularly to us non-apple users. (yes, we're "out there"!)

review_headline: great tablet but this is about the problems.
review_body:
you can read about the good stuff elsewhere. it's great tablet, but i have one os design issue and a tech completities to discuss.

i will say, before i get into the problems; the speakers are really amazing. i was able to share a youtube video with everyone around a 8' long table and everyone could here.

the kindle fire gen1 did everything i wanted it to until the battery died. replacing it was the best option. the huge issue is a security issue. you can set a strong password on the gen1. the hd 7uses a 4 digit numeric lock... completely lame. security is supposed to get better over time, not worse. when i talked to amazon to see if there why this was the case, it turns out that they had to deal with too many people who forgot their passwords. reducing helpdesk calls really isn't a good justification for reducing security.

i was able to save my data before the gen1 to my computer's hard drive. but had huge problems getting hd 7 to communicate via the usb cable with my computer, and i do not envy anyone without professional computer technician abilites figuring the computer doesn't automatically detect the unit. once i got this problem solved, moving the data over was very cool... with caveats.

books:

the kindle really wants you to push all your data out to the cloud (aka centralized server storage). it's the default. there's this little setting thing. if you moved over the entire contents of your books directory from your old device to your new device using a cable, the new kindle will remember where you were in all your books, but when it pushes your books out to cloud storage your bookmarks are lost. if your wi-fi is turned on, the default location from which the tablet will be the cloud... so if your just reading turn off yoru wi-fi.

photos

the gen1 didn't have a photo browser so i had to use a third part photo viewing app. it was pretty cool, because you could organize your photos intofolders. maybe great aunt milly wants to see the wedding photos, but you're not too keen on her checking out the bachelor/bachelorette party photos, this worked pretty well. the hd 7 has a photo view standard, but it organizes by date, even if you move photos over from a device and create subfolders in the photos directory. i haven't looked too much into this to see if this setting can be changed, but unless you're careful poor milly's going to see way more than you want her too using the default settings.

review_headline: great for all your ebooks and checking your emails!
review_body:
i absolutely love my kindle fire hd. i upgraded to the 7-inch screen because i wanted a bigger screen. i love how i can watch most youtube videos on it and i can check my emails easily. it even gives me notices when i have a new email that i have not seen yet. of course, the kindle fire is really meant for ebooks and i love that too. i have many ebooks that i have read on this kindle. i like that it remembers where you left off and i can bookmark many different pages that i might want to return to later. this is especially helpful for cookbooks.

now when i wake up in the morning and i want to check my emails, i don't have to go over to the computer. i can just grab this open it up and click on my emails, which i do every day. i love the convenience of just sitting on the couch doing stuff that i normally would have to do at my desk. if i plan to type a reply in an email than i will go to my desk because it has a keyboard and that’s a lot easier if you’re doing a lot of typing. there is actually a lot more you can do with this kindle than i thought there would be. i am still discovering new stuff. anyways, i am very excited to have this kindle and i would definitely recommend it if you’re looking for any kind of e-reader.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
3 strikes you're out amazon! sorry. i want to love this new version of the kindle fire but i absolutely cannot. i have the first version of kindle fire and loved it. it however, after 2 years is starting to die even with 50% battery life still on the charge. so my husband bought me this new one. the battery life was so bad, i returned the first one thinking it was a lemon. the second one arrived, same thing but with added speaker issues. now i have the 3rd replacement and it just died after 3 hours!!!!! amazon i expect way more from you!

in this day and age a 3 hour batter life is not even good enough for our phones, let alone a tablet. i was planning on using this on my upcoming trip with my toddler. the problem is, the kindle won't even last long enough for the flight, let alone airport waiting time. besides the battery life, the speakers are terrible! i almost have to have the volume all the way up just to understand what is being said.

another glitch that i cannot live with is, the notifications while watching a movie. if i am on netflix and a notification comes in, the volume automatically adjusts way down and does not go back up. you have to exit out of netflix completely then go back in for it to be fixed. how many notifications do you get in any give 2 hours? watch a movie on the new kindle and you will notice how many.

amazon, it seems like you had a hit with the kindle fire and in your haste to make a quick dime, you sacrificed quality to satisfy the masses. it's too bad that is going to drive away any business you could have received from very satisfied customers. you might be able to win me back with a quality product down the road, but i don't know what would make me try your kindles again.

review_body: i purchased this kindle fire 7 hd for my wife and she loves it! she is 49 years old and this is her first touch screen device ever (she's still using an antiquated flip phone that we'll be upgrading shortly). the audio and video quality is amazing. for folks not used to touch screen devices, there is definitely a learning curve. for those of you who are familiar, you will have no problem with this software. i purchased this with the understanding that this would be able to mirror the tablet to my lcd tv. i should have researched that feature further because the list of compatible devices is remarkably small. unfortunately nothing i already own is compatible. that was a let down for sure. the other let down after the fact was the limited storage space on the device itself. the default 8 gb would have been fine if the os didn't occupy about half of it. especially since there are no slots for expandable storage cards. the unlimited on line cloud storage is fantastic, but we are constantly removing older items and apps in order to make room for new items and apps. at the time i ordered this, the 16 gb model was out of stock and had a min. 30 day time line before i would receive it. so basically i settled for 8 gb and am having to deal with it. all in all it is a great little tablet and my wife is happy. she can play her games, quickly browse on line, and have quick and easy access to her facebook account. for $130 +/- what more could i ask for?

review_body:
the kindle fire is perfect for all different kinds of users. there are an abundant amount of apps designed for children on the amazon app store. these apps range from educational to simple games to occupy time on long car rides. the kindle fire has an advanced parental control center so parents can limit the ways their child is able to interact with their tablet. the parental control center can limit the time the kindle is used, it can block any option for a child to buy things online or through games, and it can block content that is deemed inappropriate by the parents. anyone who likes reading would also be interested in purchasing the kindle tablet. it has access to the amazon bookstore so books can be downloaded directly to the tablet. people who are avid shoppers would also be happy to know that the amazon tablet comes with access to the amazon store built in. frequently there are deals posted on the store only available to kindle users. i am an avid reader and a student; this tablet was perfect for me because i had an entire library at my fingertips and i could find electronic copies of my textbooks at reduced prices. the kindle also allowed me to download the adobe app so i could sort and view my reading assignments that were in pdf format.
the most prominent features on the kindle fire are the vivid 7” display, the sleek button-less appearance, and the dolby dual stereo speakers. the kindle’s size is perfect for holding with two hands. it isn’t so large that it feels like a laptop and it isn’t so small that it feels like a smartphone. the buttons for the kindle are on the back side and they are slightly indented into the back of the tablet. the button placement lends to your hands being placed in an area that amplifies the sound from the speakers directly to your ears. even if the tablet is placed on a flat surface, the dolby dual stereo sound is surprisingly loud for such a small device.
the main benefits of the fire are the access to amazon cloud, amazon prime, and the relatively low price. the amazon cloud lets the user access their purchased material from any device with an internet connection. amazon offers a service called amazon prime that offers discounts on all products and access to unlimited television and movie streaming. the kindle fire 7” is available brand new on amazon for $139. this is much cheaper than comparable tablets. the only negative side to the kindle is the eight hour battery life and limited access to android app store. compared to other e-readers, the kindle’s eight hour battery life is low. this is because the kindle fire has a much more powerful and graphics intensive screen. other e-readers use screens that use e-ink. this uses next to no power so they can have batteries that last for days of use.
overall i would recommend the kindle fire hd 7” tablet. it can be a great tool for many types of people; students, children and professionals can gain something from what the kindle fire offers. the kindle can be used to play children’s games or a graphics heavy online game, read books for school or pleasure, and has many productivity apps that can help the student or professional.

review_headline: almost to the day and my daughter hasn't even used it every day so i was very disappointed when the wifi completely stopped work
review_body:
so far we have only had this item one month, almost to the day and my daughter hasn't even used it every day so i was very disappointed when the wifi completely stopped working on it. we tried multiple soft and hard resets and even went so far as to do a factory default reset and wipe the unit but it would not connect back to the wifi. the problem was with the unit, as our other devices were connected and still working just fine. customer service was prompt and agreed to send a new one and have me send the old unit back. but this is frustrating to have had the unit such a short amount of time before having to send it back. it was in excellent shape with both a screen protector (which is now useless as it can't be reapplied) and a child proof case on it.

the tablet seems alright otherwise, when it was working. the amazon free time allows her to download a lot of child friendly materials including games, books and tv shows. i do hate the ads that appear on the screen when you first turn on the machine. there is the option to pay to not have these appear and i think that is an absurd rip off to have to pay even more money to keep my child from seeing ads for romance novels. i assume it shows the romance novels since the kindle is registered to my account and i have purchased them in the past for myself. but to have a bodice heaving chick appear on the screen of your 7 year olds device is disturbing. i think they should just remove the ads altogether because i guarantee i won't buy a single item that appears on it, if anything just out of spite for being inundated with the ads.

review_body: i have always liked,the kindle as a media device.  the processor  on this model is better than the original fire, so it's fairly decent as a web browser.  that said, i still have an ipad for serious web use and printing but i find i reach for this much more often.  the main reason i wanted this fire is the sound.  there simply is no tablet on the market where you can do dishes, clank around the kitchen, and watch a video without headphones.  however, the 8 gig is a little short on memory.  with just facebook installed, i have only 2.5 gig left for downloading.  for twenty more dollars, i'd get the 16 gig, especially if this is your  only tablet.  i also am a bit disappointed that the text to read option has gone away.  listening to articles on the web was something i liked to do while working that i cant do here.  i can on my ipad.  yes, understandably, i know they  want to sell audio books, but what about the sight impaired and why not have it available for web pages?  that's a personal perk for me but if you don't care about that,  read on.  it's a very user friendly tablet.  grandma will get it.  the keyboard is easy to use.  it's small enough to hold in one hand, though a tad heavy compared,to an ipad.  still with my small hands, i find it easier to hold than my ipad mini. a grippy back would be nice.  i'm not a case fan but there's no way you're  going to use this without, so get a light one.  the roocase i review is perfect.  durability:  seems these guys don't quite measure up to apple.  mom had an hdx die just short of a year and she treats it with kid gloves.  luckily it was just short of the warranty expiration  and got replaced.  keep in mind apple is just 30 or 90 days (forget which) and apple care is insanely high priced.  that said, my ipad mini is in its third year of heavy use and still going strong.  i just can't hear it at a distance and  it's still too big to hold in one hand.  also mega pricey.  for under 200 dollars this is a nice tablet, especially for prime members.  amazon's customer service is  impeccable. i have never had the problems others complain about in all the years i've been dealing with them.ally for prime members.  amazon's customer service is  impeccable. i have never had the problems others complain about in all the years i've been dealing with them.

review_headline: great product that could get even better
review_body:
bluf: great product that would be greatly improved with a more robust app store and a larger library of available media for video and music.definitely get something to protect it from damage if you have children.

great product; i really wish that they had used a modified version of android software as this would have helped the appstore out tremendously (currently lacking). it's mostly intuitive to use, but could use some upgrades.

i bought this for two reasons:
1: i have a young daughter who might like this on long car trips
2: i'm trying to convince my wife to get rid of the $99.97 cable (just cable; not internet) bill that we get every month

results:
1: my daughter loves it; she is currently 6 months old. yes, she sits in a rear-facing car seat, but we used one of her headbands to secure the fire to the rear seat headrest that is above her car seat. she doesn't mind that there is a headband through the middle of the screen. she is absolutely enamored with it; we hear nothing but small "coos" from her (unless she's hungry or she has delivered a huge "present" for us") as she watches "despicable me" over and over. i haven't figured out how to play a video on repeat so when it's over my wife leans and reaches over from the passenger seat to re-start the video.

2. we have an older tv: 2007 plasma (pioneer if you're wondering). it still has a great picture, yadda yadda. it does not have a plug-in for usb power so i have to run a charger from the wall to the hdmi adapter to the tv. first world problems, i know. the picture is great and the sound is fine when running from amazon prime programs. the problem is that my wife can't do without her f****ing housewife programs which are not offered by amazon prime nor any other service that i know of (hulu, netflix, etc).

conclusion: this is a great product that is somewhat lacking in the apps department. it has good battery life, good picture, decent durability, and a wide range of uses. it does not get 5 stars because it needs a more robust app store and because the amazon library is lacking in some areas.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
pros:
absolutely love it! always wanted a tablet and for the price i thought that this would be the best choice to get me started. as a college student my main reason for getting it was to take it to class with me for ebooks and note taking, which works great for this. games are a huge plus as well, they look great, and are responsive. its fast for browsing the web as long as my internet cooperates. (its sluggish sometimes because there is over 7 devices on it at any given time) the screen is nice and clear, and the tablet is small enough to fit in your hand but still large enough where you can see everything. i love the color, and while many people complain about the plastic back, i kind of like it. better that they save costs there and use plastic rather than cut performance or image quality and use a metal case. it feels solid enough to me as well, and has some weight behind it, its heavier than my moms 2012 hd 7 and comes with a lot more features.

cons:
the only issues that i have with it thus far is the lack of apps in the amazon app store. you don't get the same apps as the google play store, or apples app store. for example the amazon app store does not have clash of clans or snapchat. they do offer alternatives though such as snapgrab or castle clash. i just wish they offered a little more selection. they do offer a number of books though, so if you are into reading thats a plus. another downside to this tablet is the camera quality. the rear facing camera has a 2mp camera, which is worse than nearly all smart phones today, and not much better than my basic phone that i had a while ago. shooting video is okay at best, but taking pictures with the rear facing camera is just god awful. the pictures come out grainy and if the object you are taking a picture of has any sort of movement it comes out very blurry. the front facing camera is alright if you plan on using it a skype call. camera quality could deffinitely use an improvement, however the cameras do get better as you move higher up in the price range and begin looking at the hdx. the final issue is storage. i got the 8gb and that only leaves 4gb for the user. which really limits you on what you can put on it. they do give you unlimited cloud storage, but some apps can take up a large amount of space, including ebooks.

overall:
so the bottom line is that this tablet is great. if you can look past the camera then i would look into getting this tablet. storage is not that great, but surprisingly i havent filled it up yet, and i have a number (about 13 or so) of games and apps installed right now, the largest being 1.26gb. it hasnt been slow or sluggish yet, and the screen is amazing to look at, all the webpages come in clear and crisp. the app store is a bit of a downside but you can enable the option to install third party apps from another market place if you would like.

review_headline: meh, okay but a little hobbled update- get something else
review_body: i got this for my wife to watch netflix and amazon videos. certainly better price than a full tablet. she ended up not liking it so i inherited it. i think amazon is trying to replicate the walled garden approach used so successfully by apple. however, with those products one is able to at least be productive. forget any google apps- there are none in the amazon app store. there isn't even my top-rated password manager. on the plus side the screen is crisp and the os solid. if you want to shop amazon and watch videos and not much else, this is a great tablet to do just those things. if amazon would allow those major apps, i suspect they would sell a lot more of these without having to discount the price to move them off the shelves.  update- after having used this almost daily for several months, i have to take off another star. we buy *a lot* of stuff from amazon and this tablet excels at that and not much else. if something pops into my head and i need to email, text or edit a 'to do' list, i have to set this down and go to a computer or my phone to accomplish it. what an inconvenience in this day and age. it's okay for watching amazon prime movies or netflix (i'm surprised they even support this app!), but several other free movie apps are missing. if i had to do it over again i wouldn't buy this (even though there are some pluses listed above), but would spend the few extra dollars to have a fully operational tablet. they made the same mistake with the fire phone (from what i read) and sales are dismal. i imagine people aren't waiting in line for these either. spend the money and get something with the apps that 95% us use.

review_headline: okay for tight budgets and kids, otherwise consider something else
review_body: bought two of these for my kids to save money versus ipads.  and while i won't say i regret it completely, the kindles leave a lot to be desired in both functionality and ease of use relative to an ipad.  one of the two devices crashes routinely or freezes and has to be completely rebooted.  the device menu and help pages tend to be non-intuitive and not pleasant to use.  supposedly, you can also drag and drop music and movie files on the devices but i can't get them to play with sound on either device in various encoding formats..  i also have experienced significant trouble connecting to certain wifi networks - especially on airplanes, which is when i really needed them to function properly the most.  lastly, the online help available is less than helpful - if the topic you're searching for even exists in the first place.  i generally find better help by googling third party message boards.  conclusion: if you're on a tight budget like i was when i bought them, or you're seeking devices for younger kids/children, then they're passable.  however, if you have the money or you need to be a serious tablet user, i'd opt for considering the substantially more expensive ipad.

just one regret: i should have coughed up the extra $15 to avoid all the special offers that pop up when i'm using the thing with wi-fi. the good news about that is that i can still pay $15 to put a stop to it, and plan to do so as soon as i remember how.

yeah, there's a learning curve for a dino like me, but i'm mostly enjoying the process. it's supposed to be good for older brains to learn whole new skills, so it's all good.

review_headline: i think that the home screen is an easy access way to get around
review_body:
dear amazon,

i have had my kindle for awhile now and i am a big fan of it. i think that the home screen is an easy access way to get around. there are an abundance of neat features. however i have come up with a list of features which i think would be really cool to have and frankly i think they are a necessity.

first off, wallpapers! please make it to where you can at least have a home screen wallpaper! the gray, bleak default is quite boring. so please amazon make this an option. i believe that this would male your customers very happy. i personally would love to have a wallpaper. and if you can also make it to where the non adult versions of the kindle to have a lock screen wallpaper.

a second thing that i would like to see is more animations. make the os more appealing to the eye. create animations for opening folders and opening apps.

amazon stop being apple and allow more customazation.

reach out to more app developers and make the app store more wide in variety. if you want, even consider adding the google play store to the device.

here is a suggestion for a new multitasking interface. when you slide up from the bar at the bottom, instead of just the apps showing, show pictures of what you were last doing in that app. the name off the app would be on top of the image with the app icon next to it. have it to where when you tap the app, it enlarges from that point and fills up your screen.

now lastly i would like to see a new notification bar. let users customize the color of it. make it similar to android lollipop where if you swype on the left, you get notifications and on the right quick settings.

also in the settings add a search feature and a recently used feature

thank you for reading,

kelby's bricker
