review_headline: all this would've been fine and dandy if not for their tv ads implying ...
review_body: i bought this for my daughter for christmas.  recently she dropped it from about 3 feet (she's 3' 11" tall) onto it's display flat onto grass.  the screen shattered.  i find out about it after my daughter slices her finger on the crazed but still functioning display.  "hmm... these things happen", i say to myself.  but then i watch the latest tv commercial on this fire hd 7 and it show a hapless mom forgetting her fire 7 she left on top of her van and watch as her fire 7 flies off and hits the concrete right on the display screen but lo and behold!  not a scratch!!  what gives?!  i called kindle fire customer support and refer to their implications in the tv commercial ad.  they refuse to acknowledge it and tell me that i'm now out of warranty and that i should've plunked down an additional $29.99 in accident protection.  additionally, they offer to sell me a refurbished fire hd 7 for $105 (new is $139.99).  well, all this would've been fine and dandy if not for their tv ads implying non existent product toughness.  shame on amazon for their deceptive advertising!  i think from now on i will look elsewhere for a sturdier tablet.

review_headline: it's a kiindle fire!  means it's great.
review_body:
when i call my kindle fire a life changing item, i really mean it. i no longer buy books made of paper. the void left by the lack of book clutter has not gone empty - oh no. that void has been filled nicely with stuff. but i digress. this version of kindle fire places the buttons back in a more intuitive spot. the power and volume buttons are on the edge instead of the back. to me, this makes sense but i can't explain why. the speakers are on the back. tiny little things that point away from the user. it's fine i guess since a lot of people use ear buds. the screen resolution is beautiful, the interface is simple. set up is fast and easy too. probably the only thing i don't like is the alarm feature volume is so quiet. i didn't hear this alarm go off and it was 4 feet away from me. don't expect to wake up with this alarm. i do like the option to add a user. now my hubby can borrow my kindle fire and not have his settings replace my own.

i love my kindle fire. my hubby benefits since he gets my older one. my mother-in law got his older one. since i'm likely to keep buying the next greatest thing i just wish the cases were universal so i wouldn't have to buy new ones. but i guess that's part of the genius that is amazon, i keep buying.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: satisfied with our upgrade from kindle fire g1
review_body:
overall this is a great upgrade from the kindle fire g1 that my wife and i were previously using.

we have been using the new g4 version for about a week and the performance is much improved over the original g1. the interface has had some pretty substantial features added to it (better management of app shortcuts, ability to create groups, support for new features and apps, etc.), but still will still be familiar to someone accustomed to the original one.

inclusion of the rear camera and a few new apps is particularly nice. especially the new default install of a maps application. although the unit does not have a gps and cannot be use for routing, the lack of an out-of-the-box map application on the original fire was a feature i felt was missing. although the included app does not compare with maps from the google play store, its nice to have basic location-based stuff (food, stores, addresses, etc.)

this unit is much lighter than the original. in a way, this is a double edged sword though. while the reduction in weight is nice, the unit does not feel as solid as the first generation. this and the overall low quality of the rear facing camera are probably the main reasons for the 4/5.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: adequate but not great. unfortunately, i went back to other devices.
review_body:
i wanted to try a dedicated fire tablet again, to replace my ipad mini for reading and light gaming. i still have two old fires in storage and i absolutely loved those, i just needed to move on. i don't have any truly serious complaints about the new kindle hd 7. it's just that it didn't grow on me like other models did. there really isn't anything great about the current model. the screen colors are washed out compared to my other devices and the design is bland. i also had a problem with the page number feature. when tapping the lower left corner to get the page number or progress, it often wouldn't register at all. i had to keep backing out of the book then tap the bottom left corner again, then it would register. until making a note or highlight, then it wouldn't register again. that was very annoying since i rely on this feature.

other than that, the sound was decent. and i could use it as a kindle e-reader and audiobook device. i don't mind the ads and limited app store. i knew what i was getting into. i just didn't love it, it's so lackluster. i went back to the kindle apps on the ipad mini and nexus 7. and i sometimes use the kindle voyage(voyage is a+ so far).

i have a feeling the hdx would serve my needs and wants better. but i'm just going to keep what other devices i have and wait for the 2015 releases.

review_body: bought this for working trip to australia.  wide range of functions for very reasonable price.  you can spend more for a higher-def display, but at this size i can't really see the difference.  video playback is also crisp.  huge range of functions, both built in and downloadable android apps; haven't had any of the latter fail despite what i understand to be enhancement amazon made to the os.  the size is the most persuasive feature--fits in coat pocket (not in jeans, however), and i was able to shlep it and the keyboard all over australia without difficulty (the keyboard, which i got separately, is adequate for email, and possibly for more extended work once you get used to the placement of things like semicolons, which are not where your fingers expect them to be; it's a significantly bigger form factor than the fire itself, but thin and lightweight.  spending more for the 16 gb made sense for me--i was able to download 4 feature films for those long air flights and still have plenty of room for music, books, etc.  one odd note considering the fire's heritage--i still prefer my paperwhite for plain old reading.  but i don't think anyone will be dissatisfied with the fire on that count either.  so it's basically a home run.

review_headline: find a better, less restrictive option
review_body:
honestly, this device is too restrictive. most videos won't play because there's no real way to get the plugins to play them without going out of your way to instal an old fire browser called dolphin which then gives you the fun of every single website you visit from that point on asking which browser you want to open it in, even though you set your default browser to dolphin. the app store is pretty limited, most useful apps are not available, but you have your choice of games if that's what you like.

restrictions aside, the device doesn't hold up over time. recently my device has started to shut itself off every time i connect to wifi unless my device is plugged into a wall, which defeats the "mobile device" purpose. i was lucky to finish a college course because i had rented a digital textbook from amazon (also not recommended) when my device started acting up and it took me awhile to figure out that i could run it as long as i was plugged in. being barely at the year mark for owning it didn't help and my only option from amazon was to purchase a discounted refurbished device, like i'd trust another tablet from them after my current experience. i'm not putting another penny towards an amazon tablet.

frankly, i won't be buying another amazon tablet. i love my paperwhite but have more hate towards kindle fire than is probably rational at this point. i've never felt so much dislike or disappointment from a device from amazon and i will not be trusting another tablet in the future.

i now have a very shiny, no surface damage, still charges device that i can't take anywhere or do anything with because the wifi doesn't let me keep the device on which is kind of the point of using a tablet: wifi and function.

- many little bugs (opening url links from apps sometimes does not work, embeded youtube videos don't go fullscreen, and the list goes on.. you'll find them all over the system). fireos is new compared to ios and android and has lots of bugs.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: not worth the "hassle free" box it came in.
review_body:
don't get unless you expect very little from a tablet. regrettable purchase. before i sent it back i kept it for about two, three weeks, to see if there were any redeeming features, and by the time i was done, i wanted to use the kindle fire as actual kindling for a campfire.

it was well below expectations as a full-fledged "tablet". for one, no versions of the device allow you to add a wallpaper. but if you don't pay more, amazon programs the device to display random ads on your lockscreen and homescreen. but in neither case can users add their own pictures??? k. the whole built-in-ads thing kinda works as a cost cutter for apps and websites, but if users choose between two *physically existent* devices and can't afford the artificially more expensive one, how's it make sense to put in ads to buy more stuff?

also: setting up the pre-installed mail app is impossible to figure out. watching video in browser is interrupted by stupid address bar and tabs at the top -- even in fullscreen. it's an android device with zero customizability, and no access to the google play store. support for google apps is basically nonexistent -- humongous problem since i use them all for school: google drive/docs/sheets, gmail, calendar, everything.

i was hoping to use it at least as an ebook reader for schoolbooks i bought digitally. still failed. if you count the fact that there were words on the screen and i can read, i guess its kind of okay. it's cool that this one small device can hold thousands of books, but then again, i never really wanted to carry around thousands of books at once anyway. i would rather endure carrying around the three or four books i'm reading at the time and putting the rest on a shelf that than spend over a hundred dollars for an ability i already have. without a second thought, i long ago would only have bought paper books if i knew what i was getting into with amazon. they have ruined my experience with them completely, and i would actively discourage friends and relatives from using their digital products.

review_headline: love, love, love my kindle fire!
review_body:
absolutely love my new kindle fire! i had never used one before and bought one for my myself with christmas money during a cyber monday deal on amazon. great looking, lightweight, easy to use. i have already read 16 novels in my first 12 weeks of having it so it has definitely helped me step up my reading.

note that most libraries have "overdrive" accounts where you can download e-books for free. there's also sites like project guttenberg with tons of older books for free as well. i had tried the "kindle unlimited" on here for a month but found is ironically quite limited on the selection of books. my library has all the current books i want to read not just obscure titles like "kindle unlimited".

i also love the pink and keep mine in a pink leather case i found at staples. note that there's several generations of kindles and not all sellers of cases on here are clear which kindles theirs fit. i returned one that didn't fit mine and was really cheap looking and the m-edge one i found at staples is a nice hot pink leather with black suede inside and fits perfectly, feels great in my hands. in my opinion far better to buy the case in person or at least see the case you want in person then buy it on here if amazon sells it for a better price.

review_headline: kindle fire hd 7 after a couple days use
review_body:
it's made very well. sturdy and feels like it will last and not break in 2 weeks. i can watch netflix with no glitches or buffering. it goes right to my wifi after initial set up with no problems. it arrived quickly and was packaged well. i had the 1st generation kindle for several years and even dropped it while sleeping and stepped on it when waking up without breaking it. this seems to have the same quality construction. my first book order came through quickly. what i needed was quickly being able to order from the amazon site, get books, watch netflix and fluff around on facebook and read email. that's really all i need. the camera turn out to be quite nice. i was pleasantly surprised since i use a dslr for my camera needs. a quick shot from the device isn't bad at all. video is crisp and clear, sound is wonderful through my ear phones and without. the price for the quality you get is top notch and it works wonderfully every time it's turned on. all in all what the heck else could you ask for? except............

my question now is.........what the heck happened to the battery life? i used to be able to charge my 1st generation kindle once a week. this is more like a phone battery. yes, it last longer than a phone but i have to charge every single day now.

ads? you really need to give me ads? my opening screen has an ad on it? you give me "suggestions" that i didn't ask for? my son is 29 years old, what in the world do you think i need with a bottle nipple ad? at least let these ads pertain to my shopping over the years.

kindle (phone) support went down. sorry boys and girls but outsourced support is always a bad idea. i can't understand them, they can not understand me and the connection is never good. considering all other amazon support is the best i've ever experienced and why i am such a loyal amazon supporter, this is sad indeed.

please please i can not stress enough, amazon please do not go the route everyone else goes. you have a great product, you have what we want with better quality than would be expected at the price you give. some of us are serious readers and would stand on a box and scream your support to all those other tablets out there. don't turn this into a venture. we are loyal customers here to the very end. don't go down that road and ad us to death. don't take away from the greatest product at the greatest price.

i'd of given 5 stars even with the battery draining faster than the first kindle i owned but those ads, man those ads have got to go. i'll be looking into that as soon as i finish my review.

review_headline: great hardware; now, about those apps...
review_body:
screen resolution is very good. picture is crisp, sharp, balanced, and pleasing. sound is very good for a unit this size. speed is also quite acceptable.

the only thing that keeps this from a solid, no-brainer 5-star rating is the difficulty that amazon imposes on the user to load and use any app that didn't come from the amazon app store. after being a long-time kindle, blackberry phone and blackberry tablet user (yes, they make/made a tablet), i decided to make the switch to android. i did, and haven't looked back. i assumed (i still think reasonably so) that my android apps used on my phone would work on my android fire tablet. well, there's the rub. some of them, more than a few, simply can't be found on the amazon app store. and the google play store says their apps won't work on my device (this isn't true, but that is what it says.) bottom line, i can still do some things on my phone i can't do on my fire tablet, besides making calls. that isn't cool with me. there are ways to get around it, but "work arounds" found on the internet which may or may not work with varying effectiveness is a particular joy i thought i'd left behind when i left blackberry. not entirely.

amazon: i get that you want us to use your app store and yours alone. you're a jealous lover and we get that. but that kind of (very) old-school fidelity doesn't work today. sure, make your hardware work incredibly well with your content, but don't shut out other android apps. android hardware and apps are what make it #1 in the world. don't mess with this.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
this is a kindle. it is a really wonderful kindle with the capability to watch a video, but it is a kindle in my opinion not a tablet. this is not a tablet to be compared with any of the other leading tablets on the market. it's a great electronic device. but it is far more cumbersome to just browse the web (could just be because i am used to the ios interface...) it is perfect for magazine subscriptions. it is far superior to other tablets in that realm. and i love it as just a kindle as well.

my use for this is that i have a large number of work-related pdf's that i need to have handy and searchable at any given time. i travel constantly for work. i was keeping these items on my other tablet. but, it was soaking up space and i didn't have space for all my work docs, pics, music, apps, etc. i had to branch out and find another, more cost effective way to manage my professional documents electronically. this is the perfect solution. it is wonderful for my work documents, even better than my other tablet! i keep all my documents on there and it's portable. so portable i can slide it into a pocket and head out anywhere for work with every pub/document/instruction/etc i need. and it's freed up tons of space on my web browsing tablet to have fun on that one. sometimes i use the kindle for things that are not professionally based and it's not as wonderful, but for its price, it is not bad.

reading
-books: backlit, syncs to your kindle, my husband complained once that it synched in the wrong spot, but we've had just that one issue. i prefer to read on just a kindle, vice the fire, because the backlight and screen is less harsh on my eyes.
-magazines: best magazine reading medium, orgnaize your subscriptions, flip through like a magazine
-documents: good for pdfs and docs that you may have, searchable and with the ability to take notes/highlight

browsing:
-works well for browsing, although the screen is a bit small to have it as your only item. you could not abandon the computer and just browse on this.

apps:
-so far the apps i have looked at have been disappointing. however, i've only looked at a small number of apps.

shopping:
-shops on amazon like a dream. i do a ton of amazon shopping and this is really wonderful.
-shops on other websites like most other tablets, doable, but not easy
-app based shopping: i have not used any shopping apps to shop on the fire.

battery:
-my biggest complaint, my battery does not last nearly as long as other tablets or kindle's.

review_headline: love my kindle, but please, amazon, help me with organizing and finding books!
review_body: i have had my kindle fire for just over one year.  i had held off buying a tablet because i really like books and the satisfaction of turning a page and physically interacting with the book.  however, my family gave this to me for a christmas gift and i am really glad they did!    there is so much to like about my kindle fire hd, 16 gb.  while i primarily use it for reading, i must admit to being hooked on many games and apps, many of which i got free through the amazon store.  i like the easy backup to the cloud as i keep most of my games, apps and books on it and download when i am ready to read it.  since i read to fall asleep, i had difficulty at first, being stimulated by the light, but now i turn the brightness down to its lowest point and often fall asleep with it.  luckily it turns off by itself.    i also want to thank you for the design of the usb connector.  i sometimes forget i have it plugged in and accidentally yank on the cord when moving the device and no matter how many times i have done this, the usb port is still securely fastened and not loose.  i can't tell you how many laptops i have had to have serviced or replaced because the power connection loosens over time.    the main reason i am leaving a review is that i want amazon to improve some things so that when i buy the next generation it fulfills my needs even better.  so while these may be viewed as criticisms, they are really a request for improvements.    management of books  i am a prolific reader.  sometimes i am in the mood for a literary, mystery, romance, or a cookbook, however, kindle has no way of organizing books by genre, only by title, author or date purchased.  with well over a hundred books in my library, this can take forever to find the book i would like to read at the time of reading.  also, sometimes, i'd like a novella due to time constraints so i'd like to know how many pages as well.  the only way to do this is to go back to the store to get this information and i can't scroll the library and the store at the same time.    secondly, i'd like to delete a book right after i read it without having to go the manage my kindle app.  as it is, every week or two i go to the manage the kindle app to delete all books i have read and this can take a long time.  its especially frustrating when the alpha order in manage my kindle does not match the alpha order on my kindle, so i have resorted to typing each book in manually, making the process even longer.  sometimes its an issue with the word the at the beginning of the title, but sometimes the title doesn't match and i have to go searching by author instead.    thirdly, the scrolling function is not there for games.  there is one for apps and books but not for games. i surprised myself with how many games i have on my kindle with many downloaded for my nephew when he comes to visit.    i really like the favorites section in which i can add a book that i want to read and/or purchase in the future.  i would amazon to expand on this and add favorite authors and not just titles.  so often, i read a kindle book that i like and want to read more by the author.  while i could go in and add each of the author's books individually this is time consuming especially if the author is prolific.  even worse, if the author comes out with a new book, it won't be on my list.    like others, i don't like the delay between when apps and games are published for android and for when i want to get them on my kindle.  there are some great android apps that i would like to have on my kindle but can't download to it from a non-amazon store.  likewise i have some compatibility issues even after they have been received from the amazon store.    overall, i love my kindle fire, but with the aforementioned features and a couple other tweaks (not mentioned) i would be even happier.  to be honest, a more robust way of organizing and deleting novels would have me jumping quickly to upgrade to the next version.

review_headline: works great - very easy to use, but destroyed by constant amazon advertising!!
review_body:
the fire tablet works very well. it pretty much does everything that an ipad will do, at a fraction of the cost. i purchased two of them (one for my wife and one for myself). the battery life is very good, wifi connection is very easy, good signal, amazing camera, great various other features.

now, for the bad part. there is no background option, unlike all other electronic devices. no, you cannot have a picture of your dog, wife, or loved one as your background. here's why: each time you return from any period of inactivity, there is a big stupid ad for one of the absurd games that amazon is constantly peddling. these games actually start out free, but then cost as much as 99 cents per level. i don't play games on my fire, so this is a big problem for me. i don't want games -- and i don't want ads for games.

next, you will find that google play and the android market place are unavailable, because amazon wants you to only buy the items that they are peddling. another big problem. i've researched and found that high-tech users can go through various hoops to 'root and install" the other market places and apps. this is something that should not be required. amazon did not tell me that the fire would be able to only install amazon products.

review_body:
initially we were skeptical of the tablet scene with all the typical questions and comments. "i could just use my laptop for browsing or online shopping", or "i could use my phone for quick references or take out orders". after purchasing our first kindle fire 3 years ago we became instant fans and eventually added 2 more to the house due to high demand, from the kids (wink wink). i found myself using the kindle everyday for tasks that i had used my phone for in the past such as for a portable netflix/youttube viewer when doing dishes or house chores and quick general browsing for recipes, etc. we also found that we use the kindle the most when traveling for entertaining the children in the car or hotel room and as a reference when looking or booking places to eat or visit.

comparatively, the kindle fire stacks up very well to the competition. we all know ipads are nice but not everyone wants to spend $300 on a tablet that gets carried around a lot and used often by the kids. additionally, i really like the 7" screen as it is plenty big for general use without being so bulky that you cant bring it wherever you would need it.

pros:
-great overall quality and finish to the product
-intuitive interface that is sure to be a breeze to learn
-size
-price
-accessories

cons:
-you have to pay to remove advertisements
-variation between generations requires new cases (but not power cords which is very nice)

in conclusion, if you are looking for a great tablet for the entire family, look no further. i have no problem endorsing this product (which i shouldn't considering we have 3 in the house now) and fully believe that you will love it too.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: much, much better choice than the kids version
review_body: better than the kids version, good enough for a basic everyday tablet for sure. i do want to say that we've only had this a few weeks so my opinion could change over time but i think barring a.anything major my star rating wood remain the same. i originally purchased my 3 yr old the 6" 8gb kids fire and it was truly awful (no memory, slow processing) but returned for the adult version in a larger screen size and with more memory for apps, movies and pics. the extra inch of viewing space makes it more useable and he hasn't used up all the memory in a wk like he did with the other version. he finds this mostly easier to navigate than my ipad but it took him about a week to get used to it and sometimes still steals my ipad from me. i find this to be useful for using the internet and watching movies, probably playing games if i did that (when my son takes my ipad) but the small screen still frustrates me even at 7" when trying to do any serious shopping since you can barely view one item on the pg tho the small size makes it easy to carry about with you during the day. this version moves fast enough for basic purposes, screen resolution is decent and so is the camera. i will say that it doesn't hold a charge very well, it seriously sucks up energy (it's gone from 84% charge during the time that i've written this to 60%). 3 hours tops if watching movies straight thru so i don't know if mine is just lemon but i'm not going to hold it against them too much since i can ways get one of those lil portable chargers and i don't imagine it's made to hold a longer charge. i love amazon, they as a general rule make my life easier and i'm inclined to purchase their products over others because of that but i don't love these fires (i do like them tho). i had two of the earlier fire versions along with the original kindle reader ones and liked them quite a bit but that was before i had an ipad. i think for the price you get a solid, useable tablet and it'll work best for people who aren't sophisticated with tech, children for whom one doesn't want to shell out hundreds more or as a cheapie tablet for traveling or running about. i can't imagine getting any serious work done on this thing due to the size even tho 16 gb is decent enough memory, it's lack of charge time and it's generally a lil slower than nicer tablets. i love that it's so easy to purchase anything, the separation of family members ( or that my husband and my credit card info can be stored jointly) and that the parental controls are so customizable and that i can prevent my child from not only doing certain activities but also control exactly when and how his time is used. i haven't been an amazon prime member since they last raised the price but i would assume that works great in addition to this tablet. let's face it, a kindle fire is essentially a giant amazon store which is great for anyone who uses amazon a lot, it makes everything easy. i've been using amazon since the early 2000's as a college student, thru my early career and now as a sahm in my mid-30's so i've built up a huge collection of books, music, games and movies in cloud that now my son can access as they become appropriate to his age (i doubt he's gonna be reading proust any time soon but he enjoys my puzzles) but this essentially gives him a decent sized library to choose from as he grows and i've been able to add age appropriate materials to the selection for now. this along with the ease of use and purchasing power makes me inclined to continue with fires for him as he gets older and i think for most kids these tablets would be acceptable up until college provided they had a secondary device for homework. let's face it, for the price tag you can't really beat this model but as someone whose used fancier tablets it doesn't quite compare. now i haven't tried the next step up on the fires given that for the price one can get an ipad mini and i do think for most people if amazon wants to capture the market they need to consider why anyone would buy a fire for $300 or more when they can get something faster, sleeker and more useful for a similar pricetag elsewhere but if the tech improves and the price adjusts then the next step up of fires might be a better choice for school age children but this one will do for now. i'm so relieved that this product turned out so well after the last disappointment with the kids fire and some other minor amazon frustrations, i don't know what i would do without amazon in my families life lol. fyi, the advertisements are barely noticeable so i couldn't imagine paying for one without, they just run on the screen when it's locked, not during active use. oh but i find the keyboard kind of awkward, the way it's laid out and moves doesn't work well for my small hands but that could just be me. in any case my son loves his "pad" and it's a great educational tool as well as babysitting device when mommy's running errands or on the phone, just make sure you have enough things physically downloaded for use out and about or you could have a frustrated kiddo on your hands.

review_body:
problem: i bought my kindle fire hd 7 in june of 2013. in the summer of 2014 i started having trouble with it booting up and keeping its battery life. because it was "out of the warranty" time frame (1 year) i had to put up with it hoping it would get better. i took the few apps i had on it (facebook, twitter, and flipboard) off the kindle. i also disconnected my email and reset it. i hardly ever turned on the wi-fi because of loss of battery. my kindle fire would not get past the start up kindlefire logo screen.

review: amazon kindle has the worst customer service. i have had grace, patience and mercy for over one year as i have time and time again called customer service to work out the issue with my ‪#‎kindlefire‬ hd 7. their solution is to buy another one (50% off). i could understand that if the problem was because of my error (like dropping it, water, etc). but it is a manufacturers error.

any time i called their customer service they treated me like i was stupid and repeated the same steps each time - even though they can track my customer service calls. i would patiently explain that they had done what they were asking me to do each time i called and it did not fix/change the situation. they scheduled for their supervisor to call me - and they never did. they did reach out by email three weeks later to see if the situation changed. the customer service reps (in a foreign country) were following a prescribed list of questions and did not actually listen to the customer.
i highly doubt that i will ever buy one of their products again. if they had good customer service i would stick with them. but with a bad product and bad customer service - they have lost me.

my personal review - go with apple and then get the kindle app if you want to purchase kindle ebooks. apple store has the best customer service and i have learned from this long and painful experience that their price is worth it - even for their customer service alone.er service alone.

review_headline: i would love to write a good review about the kindle fire
review_body:
i would love to write a good review about the kindle fire, but i can't. it's an amazing piece of technology, until it stops working, which coincidentally happened soon after the 1 year warrant expired. now it's a piece of junk. it rarely starts when you hit the power button, and when it does start (about 1 of out 5 tries) it often just shuts down or freezes up. i am very, very disappointed in this product. amazon usually stands by the things it sells, and this is their product, and they won't stand by it. once the warranty is up, you're out of luck.

bottom line is this: if you want a table that will work for one year, it's great. if you expect your electronics to last longer than that, don't waste your money on the kindle fire.

review_headline: give me interface or set it on fire
review_body: item came as promised, which was a good price and a bit ahead of the backlog that was originally forecasted. i do like the reading interface, not as annoyingly digitized and fluorescent as most pads, laptops, phones. i am not finding the kindle as user friendly as i would have liked. i feel the os probably has a lot more to offer but is laid out in a proprietary manner to push sales. the user info was extremely basic, how  to set up log on accounts for multi family members etc.- but no real info or overview on utilizing the device itself. great - i can connect and receive dead end guis for amazon products i don't want or other applets  i can purchase; its loaded with more commercials and sales pitch than a super bowl sunday! i bought it for a user friendly interface for tween, teen, myself- instead of using our phones- a bit more screen, reading, interface options. so far that hasn't happened. i will pursue some online avenues on my laptop to see if we can make this a bit more user friendly for all, but that's already wading into the "don't bother" area for most people. i did purchase the extended warranty since it was bought with tween/teens in mind, i received an email weeks before the item was delivered that i now have a "warranty" from the third party company. not getting warm fuzzies on that front either- more work to chase down how to, when to, who to, list the item serial number with...etc. at this point i feel i probably should have purchased a mini laptop for the teen and let the tween have my old one. that or updated to the larger screen smartphone; just not big on that auto tracking mechanism in the phones, but the ads on the kindle have geo-tracking all over them!

review_headline: not for kids to read with.  buy something else!!!!
review_body: parents beware!!! i bought the 7 hd for my grandson so he could effortlessly read books. i handed it to him, not realizing that parental control had to be installed at the outset and if he set it up, i would have to erase the entire system to re-do it.  then he began playing games. the device was on my account (do they tell you to set up a separate account?  no) he charged $900 on game enhancements, an amazon gimmick.  it took more or less an hour to wrestle amazon to rescind the charges, and i was warned never again would they credit me back. i did not want another game device to monitor.  i did not want him on my account.  i did not want his device reviewing my books ordered.  i did not want to have to actively monitor his use.  today, with an hour or more invested talking to ms bangladesh, i was able to get most of this reset, maybe??  if you want your kid to read, do not buy this.  buy a simple paperwhite or something like it.  this is just a badly designed, clumsy, distracting, money sucking game device.  i think i may have gotten this da@#$ed thing under control, but why make it so hard?  and do not count on amazon to give you decent parental control options up front (or even later without lots of questions and patience).  most kids have too much gaming access.  this is not one you will want to buy to make it maddeningly worse.

review_body:
before i begin i must say i bought this tablet for someone else for christmas. they did not want it so i decided to keep it for myself. this is my honest take on the device.

overall the tablet does an ok job for reading books, playing games, and watching movies. the biggest problem is that the battery is rather faulty. the tablet can be charged at 100% with the screen brightness turned all the way down; no music or video playing and yet within an hour the battery level is at 89%. all i've done within that hour was read articles on the internet and checked my mail, that's it. watch a video or play a game, obviously the battery will suffer a lot more. i fount myself charging this thing twice a day. maybe its just my tablet but overall the battery is bad. i will request another tablet to see if it really is just my device.

second, the build quality is decent. the back of the tablet however feels really cheap. so cheap that if you were to put a little pressure on it by just holding it up it would give off a plastic squeaky sound. the tablet is also slightly heavy compared to other 7\\" tablets on the market. nothing that will make your arm tired but you'll definitely notice a difference if you've played with other small tablets before.

lastly, the os at times is frustrating to use and the amazon app store is lacking a lot of quality apps. i say the os is frustrating because even though it does a good job of making things simple, there is no way for you to customize the interface to your liking. the tablet is too simple for its own good! you can't even change the wallpaper. it's also frustrating when an app has a youtube video ready for you to view and it fails to load every time (also the youtube app just directs you to the mobile youtube website. you wont get the same youtube app experience as the one on android phones or tablets).

a couple of positives though. the sound coming from this tablet is fantastic. really good quality. second, if you are a prime member you will most likely enjoy the tablet a lot more with \\"free\\" movies, books, and music. without prime i'd honestly say that this would be a paperweight, meaning nothing special. prime helps this tablet out a lot!

with all of this said the tablet in my opinion hasn't been worth the price i paid for over a month ago. although i never intended to use it to begin with,i wanted to see what all the hype was about and i just don't feel the tablet does a good job at competing with other tablets out there. the battery is really a killer and for a tablet i shouldn't have to charge it twice a day nowadays.ber you will most likely enjoy the tablet a lot more with \\"free\\" movies, books, and music. without prime i'd honestly say that this would be a paperweight, meaning nothing special. prime helps this tablet out a lot! with all of this said the tablet in my opinion hasn't been worth the price i paid for over a month ago. although i never intended to use it to begin with,i wanted to see what all the hype was about and i just don't feel the tablet does a good job at competing with other tablets out there. the battery is really a killer and for a tablet i shouldn't have to charge it twice a day nowadays.

review_headline: great device, but app store needs work
review_body: the screen definition is excellent and the device is heavy enough but not too heavy  recommend a case and screen protector, as the screen collects fingerprints and dust, and is very reflective.  the protector cuts down on the glare.  it does a great job as a kindle reader for books and it is wonderful to read a book, see another book mentioned, look it up on amazon and then download it.  books, apps and website bookmarks pop up very quickly.  the interface for apps and web bookmarks is very good, making it easy to switch between apps or from an app to a bookmark and back.  the silk web browser works very well.  my only complaint, and others have complained about it as well, is that many apps are not available that are on either an apple or android device.  maybe amazon sells kindles at a loss and can't devote money to developing apps, or does not want people to spend time using apps so they will spend more time shopping for books, apparel, etc.  apple refuses to enter any arrangement with adobe for flash player, which allows the user to see videos and hear audio streams, but this device also does not have flash player capability and there are other (e.g., warp radio) audio streaming sites it is not compatible with.  if amazon focused on its app store, they could charge more for the tablets and bring in more amazon shoppers.  feb. 14, 2015

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body: i am the proud owner of a kindle paperwhite, an ipad 2, and now my kindle fire hd7.  i use each for different purposes.  my paperwhite has the built in wifi, and i take it with me everywhere.  i keep my current reading on it and it's great in doctors offices and anywhere else i have a desire to read.  my ipad is great too, but i do fear that one day it will die, and i use it primarily for emails, web browsing, and a couple of games.  my fire hd7 is the first step for my buying a flat screen tv, and fire stick as i live in a situation where i can only stream shows from netflix and hulu.  my reasoning at the time was that the fire was going to be the easiest way to stream on to a tv using the fire stick.  i am probably a couple months away from that, but in the meantime, i have absolutely fallen in love with the fire.  the screen is so clear and the built in speakers are awesome.  i now consider this one of my favorite possessions, i take the paperwhite where i can read for longer periods of time as the battery life is longer than the fire.  if i knew how much i would fall in love with the fire, i might not have purchased the paperwhite at all.  i am an amazon prime member as well as a kindle unlimited member, so i have decided that my unlimited books - those i only keep long enough to read - are only read on my fire while my purchased books are on my paperwhite.  since i am on a relatively limited income, the payment plan for the fire has made it extremely affordable.  prior to my paperwhite, i had owned several different kindles - the kindle keyboard and the basic kindle.  with the severe arthritis in my hands, i cannot hold large books any more and the kindle allows me to easily hold a book and read it.  my ipad is too heavy for me to easily read with while holding it in one hand.  this year i am facing numerous surgeries and reading is my sanity while i'm in recovery mode.  i cannot say enough good things about the kindle line of products and i do not regret any of my purchases.

i first wrote the following in early february, and gave it 3 stars. then, downgraded my rating to 2 stars, because *when* the device works, i enjoyed it, despite some of its huge flaws. that was before it stopped working altogether. for over two days i was unable to get this thing out of the "boot loop". after spending two hours talking to five different amazon customer service representatives, they told me they wouldn't ship me a replacement at my current destination, which is in peru. so i'd stuck with an expensive paper weight. i was bitterly disappointed to have wasted my money on this, because like i said in my original review below, i mostly bought it due to the price. i should have known to save a little more for an actual tablet, and not just a "reading tablet". never going to make this mistake with amazon again.

i checked and researched before going to customer service this time just in case there's some trouble-shooting tip i would feel like an idiot for not having tried, and to no surprise, it's quite easy to find a lot of people who are just as disappointed in the same problem with this device. but according to the last individual i talked to at amazon, supposedly it's a fluke that mine is behaving this way and there's a low probability that my replacement will have the same problems.

then, it finally randomly powered itself back on while talking to him, so i went ahead and did a factory reset while i finally had it working just in case it powered off again before i could. couldn't hurt, right? i thought maybe something is all screwy in my settings or i downloaded a bad app that deleting it might fix. once i got my tablet to reboot and re-installed all my apps, the instant i went ahead and touched one (it was netflix, incidentally), it froze, shut itself off and went through the exact same routine all over again.

since they can't/won't replace it for me (they would if i were in the usa), i'm basically out of luck. i've been so happy with all the other amazon devices i'd bought in the past (they should basically pay me a commission for ali the persuasive advertising i've done for them!) i never even imagined it was possible to have a problem, but sure enough, mine won't work properly. i give up on it, and the next time i buy a tablet it will be real one.

original product review below:
----------------------------------

first, it needs to be noted i've been a huge amazon fan for about four years, and had never been disappointed previously with any of their products i've purchased over the years. i have gone through three kindles (i'm currently on a kindle paperwhite), and i read voraciously, and about a year ago bought my wife a samsung galaxy tablet for more than double what the kindle fire hd7 cost.

i finally decided **based on the price alone** to take the jump and get a kindle fire. i had accumulated enough money on my gift card balance from sharing affiliate links on facebook to buy one, and this last black friday i ordered one without any real loss to my bank account.

first, the good:
-as far as price goes, you are hard pressed to find a tablet of this quality, this inexpensive. so i am taking that into consideration when giving this device the rating i'm giving it. however, see below.
-i have been using it for all sorts of things, specifically surfing the web, using a few apps that are just easier to use on a tablet than a phone, and really enjoy using this device. i am now a huge evernote fan thanks to having my own tablet and find it much easier to write on my laptop and sync my notes to the fire tablet.
-great customer service when i had a problem with the device turning itself off and not coming back on, and getting stuck in a perpetual "boot loop" while charging. but that says more about amazon than the device, per se.

overall it needs tobe admitted that all these "good" qualities are not exclusive to the kindle fire tablet, but can be obtained on any tablet, per se.

the bad:
-when it came, i showed it to my wife, who has been using an samsung galaxy tablet for the past year, and she said to me "it looks old". this thing is *thick* and clunky looking, or at least that's the expectation i've gotten used to after having a slick android tablet.
-the brightness. seriously? i can't even look at the screen if i'm trying to read in the dark! even on the *lowest* screen setting. i had to download a blue light filter app, and it works like a charm, but if you open the silk browser (another point of frustration) the filter turns off and you're stuck with an incredibly bright screen again. i don't know whether the app is to blame (which i shouldn't need in the first place if this had a reasonable level of low-brightness) or the tablet's manufacturer design.
-the silk browser is just garbage. absolute garbage. nevermind that amazon makes it incredibly difficult to load other browser apps and you need to side load anything from google play, which also seems to cause problems with the tablet's functionality if you do. ok, so i get that amazon and google are competition and don't play nice. however, whenever i click on a link from inside any of the apps, whether it be email (native), or third-party social media app, silk opens, and then... nothing happens. i wait like twenty seconds or however long one needs in order to realize the link ain't opening. one out of three times a tab will open and provide the link i had clicked on, but the other two times nothing.
-while writing this review, my tablet has turned itself off twice while trying to download a podcast mp3 i was hoping to listen to (which needed to be done using silk, incidentally). since i have never yet successfully download a large file from the internet onto the tablet directly, i always have to do it on my laptop, and then plug in my device via usb to move the files over. i don't understand why i have to even do this, instead of skipping this unnecessary step and downloading it directly using the tablet? this problem has sort of solved itself when i downloaded podcast addict and can sometimes successfully download mp3s using that app.
-it frequently turns itself off and won't come back on. thankfully customer service was really helpful when it wouldn't turn back on for a prolonged amount of time (like a day or two), as i mentioned in the "good" section above.
-scratch what i just a bullet point ago. i stopped trying to download the mp3, and went straight to spotify and after two songs, the device shut off again and won't turn on unless i plug it in. sometimes a window pops up asking if i am sure i want to power it down, and i hit cancel. other times it just goes ahead and turns itself off. is there a reason for this?
-when listening to music, whether the native music player app, spotify, podcast addict, or any streaming service, it just randomly shuts off the app for no apparent reason. strange brew? if i wanted to randomly turn my music off, i would do it myself since, um, i'm listening to it because i want to.
-sometimes it takes forever to charge the tablet, other times it randomly charges super fast. is there a reason it can't just charge in few hours on a consistent basis or must i really wait like 10 hours some days before i can unplug and um, use it?
-and the real bugger: you don't actually get 8gb of hard drive space like they advertise! i have more space on my outdated samsung phone than i do on this tablet, which truly only comes with less than 4gb of hd space. why amazon? this part is probably the most inexcusable because it's not even a design flaw, but misleading advertising. although i didn't intend on loading it up with videos or photos or a lot of music files, i couldn't anyway if i wanted to! in fact, i don't have anover abundance of apps loaded on this thing, but i'm constantly getting a notification that i need to free up space or that i'm 90% full. what a major disappointment.

so yeah, beware: you get your money's worth if you buy one of these things. put aside a few more coins in the bank and get yourself a real tablet if you need one.

maybe i shouldn't write a review for a product while i'm trying to use it unsuccessfully and with frustration, but that's precisely why i'm going ahead and posting this. while i can't rate this one star since it has many features i like (when the device is actually working properly) i likewise cannot in good conscience or as a satisfied customer give this thing a 5 star rating either as this is much more mediocre of a product than i was expecting from amazon. they had made a good impression on me with with their dedicated reading devices (i really love my paperwhite), but this is truly disappointing.

all in all, i'm surprised to find an amazon product is this mediocre. i'd come to expect good quality from them.

review_headline: imagine my delight, when the day i decided to order

i received an amazon gift card a few months ago, for my birthday, and finally decided to use it toward a fire hd 6. imagine my delight, when the day i decided to order, the fires were on sale! i had planned to add $50.00 to my gift card in order to purchase the $99.00 item, but for a mere $14.00 more, i was able to purchase the hd 7.

the tablet is very user friendly, so even the most technically challenged person can use it. the graphics are crisp and clear, stereo speakers so it doesn't sound like a tin can. i've been using it for everything i would normally use a computer for. i recently purchased a new printer for my home, and am able to print wirelessly from the tablet.

i love that there is a variety of color choices, and best of all, after placing my order on a tuesday evening, i received a conformation informing me of a delivery date for the following monday, and was quite surprised and pleased when it was delivered on a sunday

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
i can see why many people have found themselves happy with this device, it is very responsive, allows you to do most things you can do with any other tablet, and is clearly made of quality parts.

though there are few downsides, they were significant enough for me to warrant 2 stars. at this point, i simply find the device disappointing. my issues are as follows:
1) there is so little content. seriously, aside from the kindle reading app and adobe, i doubt i've spent more than an hour (in total) on any available app.
2) most recently i learned that pdf files cannot be downloaded from epub. i'm a graduates student who frequently uses research databases for multiple purposes. this is seriously the issue that sent me over the edge with this device. it's usefulness has since reduced to simply reading pdf files that i've downloaded on separate devices.

for not much more you can purchase a quality device that can accomplish much of what the kindle fire can, and more.

i have been a loyal customer of amazon's and i truly hope they give me a reason to keep this device before i can manage to upgrade to something better.

review_headline: kindle free time is great--but use teen setting for older kids
review_body: we got two fire hd 7 tablets for our twin sons' 8th birthday and they are going to be blown away.  my customer review has to do with kindle free time for kids and some advice to other parents...the kid's version is described as great for kids 8 and under, while the teen version is described as great for kids 9 and up.  i initially set it to the kid's version because of the age recommendation, but quickly realized 8 years old is plenty old enough for the teen version as it looks exactly like the adult version but with the same parental controls.  bottom line, an 8-year-old is going to think the kid's version of free time is for "little kids" and i know mine will love being in the teen version.  i recommend amazon change the age recommendations to literacy-based: if your kid can't read yet, use free time, if he can read (k or 1st grade and up) then use the teen setting. either way, both options are fabulous!

review_headline: good budget tablet, but still has a lot of kinks to work out.
review_body: first of all, i just want to say that i love my fire hd 7. i'm glad that i went with the 7\\" because it's the perfect size, any smaller for me would be too small. i love that it comes in a variety of colors, namely pink. i think that is a great way to customize and personalize the kindle for the user's specific tastes.  it's a very durable little tablet. the back of the kindle is a harder plastic, which acts as a case in my opinion. i have yet to scratch the screen and think that it too is pretty durable. the kindle fire hd 7 is definitely a budget tablet. don't expect to be getting ipad quality here guys. it's not the same os and it will not perform the same way, trust me. i have an ipad as well. there aren't nearly as many well-tested apps for the kindle fire, so there are many issues with bugs and apps. if you aren't careful with browsing the web, your cache is going to build up and really slow this thing down. i clear mine out regularly, and clear my history regularly too, so speed has not been as much of a problem now as when i first got it. overall, i think it's a decent budget tablet, but still has a lot of kinks to work out.

review_headline: the hd7 does an excellent job in terms of speed and easy navigation
review_body:
i decided to buy this tablet for school so i would have something i could quickly check emails and documents on. in this context, the hd7 does an excellent job in terms of speed and easy navigation.

the screen is large enough to allow for typing on the touch keyboard without any problems and the keys on the keyboard are large enough to prevent hitting the wrong key when typing. you can shift from vertical to horizontal display as well which offers some freedom to change perspective for viewing as needed. the resolution is also high quality (i watched a few actions movies and was pleased with the quality).

programs for viewing and editing microsoft word and excel docs are available for purchase in the apps marketplace - $10 is a little steep for a mobile app but it helps with school and could be easily applied to a work scenario where viewing word docs or spreadsheets is required. there are also apps for quickly checking emails and youtube or podcasts. ebooks for school are also available which can cut the cost of books in half if you like that sort of thing.

internet access is good on campus and i haven't had any connectivity issues yet. the streaming speed is great. so far all the sites i use for school can be viewed on the tablet without any issues.

overall, the hd7 does an excellent job at providing quick access to content required for my education: word processing, spreadsheets, videos, websites, etc are all available. the device is also much easier to carry around than a laptop. other than these features, the hd7 can also run popular games without much lag so if you need a distraction every once in a while this will do a fine job there as well.

review_headline: great for the price, but not quite apple-caliber
review_body:
i would prefer to have an apple ipad, as we have a macbook pro and two iphones in the family already. i bought this because it seemed to be spec'd quite well for the price. the display is wonderful. the interface is ok, but not quite apple-caliber. it locks up and crashes much more than an apple though. not enough that i want to give up on it, just don't buy this thinking it is going to do everything fluidly. for example, i tried to go to youtube on the built-in web browser, and that was a flippin' disaster. it either crashed or locked up 100% of the time. i looked and saw they have a youtube app; so i installed that, and it works great. would i buy it again? i think so. samsung and apple devices are much higher in price, so high that i couldn't justify buying one and letting kids use it. probably not myself either, as a laptop is still loads more capable and an iphone is still loads more portable. but this is 1/3 the price of an equivalent ipad, which even though it is not as good as an ipad, it is still a good buy. it is like comparing a well-equipped camry hybrid at $35k (ipad) to an entry level kia rios at $12k. they both get the job done, and the camry (ipad) is certainly nicer, but nice enough that it is worth triple the price? i guess that depends on your budget. for me? this will do nicely.

in addition to my 2 year old daughter playing starfall, my 11 year old son plays minecraft on it. this constitutes about 95% of the use it gets. it is great for reading in bed. no lights to keep on that will disturb my wife's sleep. i choose the white text on black background, as this draws the least power and also bombards the eyes with the least light. it was almost as pleasant as reading an e-ink kindle in daylight.

this device is also great for checking email.

the most limiting factor at this time is the amount of apps available to its kindle-proprietary operating system. for example, i would have loved to install wechat and qq chat for my wife to chat with her chinese friends. those apps are easily available on droid or ios. i like the tapatalk app for browsing internet fora, but it isn't yet available here. i'm sure amazon will get them eventually. i think the result will be that it is not quite as "open source" as droid, so it'll have fewer virus and malware issues, but also not ios, so they can keep the price down.

the colored plastic case provides a little bit of scratch and impact protection, and is more easy to hold than apple's smooth and rounded aluminum. still, i went ahead and grabbed my ankles and bought the freetime kid-proof case for it. product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: she absolutely loves it and has it with her pretty much 24/7
review_body:
bought this for my wife since i was hogging the ipad. she absolutely loves it and has it with her pretty much 24/7. after playing with it for a bit, i'd kind of like to swap the ipad for one myself. the fire is a better size and weight for holding -- you can comfortably hold and operate it with one hand. if you've ever tried reading for any prolonged period of time on an ipad, you know that it's not ideal for that. the fire has great speakers. the ipad we always plug into external speakers or headphones if we're trying to watch something. the fire has better settings for reading so you don't get the eye fatigue you do on the ipad (yes, you can invert the display on an ipad to give you light text on a dark background but it also inverts pictures). the pros to the ipad are the ability to have multiple apps open at once and hop between them, and, if you're an apple user generally, the tight integration with other apple devices (like airplay to stream to an apple tv). but bang for the buck there's no beating the fire, especially if you're a prime subscriber which gets you access to tons of movies, original shows, music and more. definitely recommended.

one extra star to amazon for their amazing customer service. i originally bought it in yellow because they were sold out of just about every other color at the time. we sent it back to exchange for a black one. the return box was mailed out on a monday morning. that night i got an email at 11:30 pm saying it had been received, processed and my card had been credited back the purchase price!

review_headline: it's a nice tablet for the price yet leaves a lot to be desired
review_body:
i like this tablet. it's fast operating, looks good, has good touchscreen precision, and easy to figure out navigation. also seems to be safe from hacking or prying eyes. the sound volume and quality is nice.

the downsides:
- "special offers", i have found no way to remove these offers that are always on my lockscreen. it makes me feel this tablet was designed exclusively for shopping on amazon. (i do love amazon btw)
- amazon app store, has very limited app selections. and it requires a credit card to download free apps. that doesn't sit well with me.
- no customizations: backgrounds, lockscreens, tones cannot be changed... or so i haven't been able to do so.

it's a nice tablet for the price yet leaves a lot to be desired. i am content with this tablet and just purchased a case for it.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
there are so many great, detailed reviews of the fire hd 7 - i'm just going to add my voice and try to distill it into a small bite:

i'm extremely pleased with my fire hd 7. i purchased it to replace my fire hdx - which i gave to my mother because she has a lot more free time and loves playing games and watching prime video in bed on her tablet (she also loves using the x-ray capabilities while she's watching shows on the big screen with her fire tv).

back to the hd 7 - it does everything i could want, and at a great price. i use my fire hd 7 mostly for video - prime movies and tv, amazon original content, hbo go and xfinity apps. my internet connection is strong and fast, and i often listen on my bluetooth stereo headset (the same one i use with my phone). it's perfect for trips (downloaded content), private viewing when others are sleeping or reading or using the tv for games. it's great for watching something on break or in a waiting room or waiting in a car (wifi or download). it's fast, sharp and the speakers provide good sound.

it's far more capable than i expected! as for the other functions - reading is great, and the games are everything you would expect from a more expensive tablet. facebook and goodreads integrate perfectly, along with other social media. for entertainment - this is perfect, and it "does the web" just fine too! if you don't need "the biggest, fastest so & so device" - this will be perfect for you too!

review_headline: (my wife & i both like to read
review_body:
i'm not "tablet" savvy at least not enough to write a blank overall review. i can tell you this is the second one in the family, (my wife & i both like to read.) i have had a stroke and reading line by line in a book or newspaper is out of the question for me. i opted for the audible books and was pleasantly surprised when the word being read was highlighted seamlessly on the page! made reading and following along a joy again.
now i have found out i can control the spaces between lines and of course the size of the text. with this feature i can turn the narration on and off at will. when my stroke problems start to act up i simply touch the sound bar and go right back into narration where i left off.

after 8 years i can finally read once more!
i love technology!
ed (dv) combs

review_body: i had previously given the kindle 4 stars, but i'm changing that down to three due to quality issues.  my new kindle simply stopped working after just 5 months; after sitting for a day and a half it refused to turn on, even plugged in.  it wasn't dropped, handled roughly, or anything. amazon replaced it with a refurbished one, but that one had a malfunctioning screen right out of the box.  i'm going to be asking for another (new) replacement, but my faith in the quality is in doubt.  there are only two function (rather than quality) annoyances i've noticed - the ads on the lock screen are a little annoying (i got it as a gift so i shouldn't complain, but if it were me i'd have paid a little more for no ads), and the device occasionally freezes with certain apps ("bonza" word puzzle).    however, other than those two small annoyances, i love the kindle (when it's actually working).  it's a far better size for web surfing than my iphone, and i can actually print to my wireless printer from the kindle (revolutionary i know...).  i had initially snubbed e-readers in favor of paper books, but after giving it a try, i'm definitely a convert.  anyone who says paper books are better should have to lug two 800 page novels around through airport security and spend two seven hour flights holding them.  on top of that, with the ease of borrowing library e-books right from the device, i'm already reading far more than i would otherwise, without the expense and clutter of paper books, or having to run back and forth from the library.  definitely one of the best gifts i've gotten, and would be completely worth the cost if it hadn't been a gift.

review_body: i received my kindle as a christmas gift. truthfully i wasn't sure if i really wanted or not. however, i have come to love my kindle. i used to think my laptop was convenient. but my kindle is the definition of convenient. if i want to google something real quick, shop on amazon, oh and thing is made for amazon prime; i take advantage of my prime membership way more now than i used to. i have watched movies on here and the picture is so crisp. i wasn't expecting such hd quality. i can lay in bed at night and read a book without the bedside lamp on so it doesn't bother my husband. i can adjust the brightness of the screen so it's not so bright. you have the option to change the background color while reading a book. i changed my background to black and the words are written in white so it's much easier on my eyes. i figured out that when your typing out, like writing a review, you don't even have to lift your finger off the screen. all you have to do is move your finger across the screen to all the letters and it knows what you're trying to type out. my kindle has made it very easy to keep up with facebook. and i have become obsessed with pinterest. there are fun games you can download and play. some of my favorites are the slots. you can download all kinds of apps and books and keep them in your cloud instead of on your kindle so it doesn't slow down your device. the only reason i didn't give my kindle a five star rating it's because sometimes it freezes up. i have a feeling this my have more to do with some of the apps rather than the performance of the kindle but i'm not sure. now that i have a kindle i'm not sure what i would do without it. i'm so glad i got this as a gift and i highly recommend everybody have one, especially if you have amazon prime.

review_body: i debated about getting a kindle fire hd or a nexus 7 to replace my failing four year old samsung galaxy tab 7 plus.  my wife got me this for christmas.  i thought i might find the carousel a bit backward after the samsung.  i also have a samsung phone and love using folders on the home screen.    i found the carousel very easy to get used to.  it is an easy interface.  i also like the speed and love the screen resolution.  the screen is slightly wider than the samsung or nexus.  this way out-performs my wife's 2012 vintage nexus 7.  the sound is much stronger than any tablet i have used.  it is clear and its volume will fill a room.  the screen has a type of glass on it that wipes off easily.  it does not collect finger marks.    this is built for video and reading.  it streams well throughout the house whereas we have problems with the nexus.  it does well with netflix, youtube (via the browser) and other video on the internet.  i downloaded the spirit clips app and side-loaded the vudu app.  all work well.    not all the apps in the amazon app store are available on the fire hd.  some are not compatible.  i downloaded an apk extractor app and got the vudu and some other apps off my old tablet.  i was disappointed that swiftkey is not compatible.  i got it loaded but it took up too much screen.  i found another keyboard i am just as happy with.    i read and heard negative information on the browser.  i have found it to be as good as any other tablet browser.    overall, this is a really good product.  we will get one for my wife when her nexus wears out.

review_headline: false advertisement-8gb is really under 4.5gb free space
review_body: i'm on the phone with amazon as i write this.  i bought two of these for my children at christmas. my son has been getting low storage errors since he started using it, and he only loads simple apps as a 7-year-old. i finally looked at the storage to find that the device only had a little over 4gb of storage.  the second one i bought has the same problem.  i just factory reset one device and ran through some tap here, tap there, force stop this, force stop that with tech support.  the device says 0.92gb used and 4.11gb free.  it's supposed to have 8gb of storage according to the product description.  tech just got back on the phone with me and said that the pre-installed apps (that i can't delete) take up over 4gb, and this kindle really only has 4.5gb of free space.  i'm sorry amazon, but you failed on this one.  it really feels like false advertisement when i'm getting half of what you claimed i would get.  i own an original kindle fire and 3 other kindle readers, and i've been happy until now.  i have a prime account and do a lot of shopping with amazon, so more than anything, i am just truly disappointed in an inferior product.

review_headline: great tablet, great price. highly recommend
review_body:
this is a great device. bought it as a x-mas present for my 4yr old. we chose this regular version rather than the model specifically for children because it is more customizable. this is our first kindle device. my favorite feature is how you can download the kindle app on other android or iphone devices, and read any book downloaded on the kindle. the parental controls and user profile settings are great. the main admin profile has full control over each user profile settings. i have restricted all app purchases under my son's account, so i never have to worry about any unauthorized purchases. any application i download can either be shared or restricted from user on any other selected profiles.
the speed and processing of the device are great, and rival other tablets at much higher price points. battery life and picture is great as well.
the only bad part about kindle is that the "wake-up screen" shows advertisements. i'm not sure how or if you are able to remove these. its just a little annoying, but doesn't take away from usability.
this tablet is definitely worth what we paid.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: pretty little tablet: great for reading & listening to audiobooks
review_body: i've been an ipad user for a few years, but i am also a loyal kindle e-ink reader. i have had almost every e-ink model, but i had also always wanted to try a kindle fire as well. i chose this one, because the price was low, but it still had room for some books and apps. it's not an ipad (which i use mostly for productivity stuff and web surfing), but it's lovely for reading or listening to audiobooks. the speaker is pretty good for listening, but it sounds better when i connect it to my bluetooth speaker for a louder volume. the book covers look so pretty on the screen, audiobooks are easy to find, and i can play games on it as well. it's very nice for reading. i don't intend to give up my e-ink kindles or my ipad, but this is a really nice tablet. it's not entirely intuitive, but once you get used to it and figure a few things out, it's very easy to use.  even though i put a cover on it, i chose the blue one and it's very pretty.

review_headline: must read if you are going to buy a kindle, must read!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
review_body: returning this kindle. i bought 2 of these kindle fire hd7 8gb and my boys' storage was critically low and wifi automatically kept turning off by the first week. i called amazon to get clarification on what is taking up so much space, since nothing within the settings for storage came close to even 1g. then i started questioning why the space was considered 'critically low' when only 4.3g was showing as being used.... what happened to the other 3.8g? sure, no device actually has the full storage capacity for your own personal use, but wow almost 1/2 of the entire space of the kindle fire hd 7 is used just to run/operate the kindle? had i known this i would have just purchased the 16g from the start. when i stated i wanted to do return these 8g kindles and buy 2 new 16g kindles, (but i had initially purchased on sale with $25.00 discount) the amazon customer service rep told me that she could give me a $25.00 credit for each kindle to return them and purchase the 16g. i asked a 2nd time to be sure that she was able to apply the $25.00 credit twice (1 for each kindle) and she replied with 'yes, the $25.00 credit will be applied for each kindle, so $50.00 total.' ... unfortunately this never happened! i was told they could only apply the $25.00 credit once after i was just told two times that it would be no problem to credit for both. now mind you, i am known for being a amazon spokesperson. i am constantly raving about how great amazon is and i have told hundreds and hundreds of people to sign up for amazon prime. i have >6 amazon devices and spend thousands of dollars with amazon each year... yet they won't follow through with giving me what they originally told me (twice) which was $25.00 credit to my account for each device. this was escalated to 2 supervisors and the answer was still no. wow!!! my mind has vastly changed about you amazon!!! i would have spent more than the $25.00 by buying 2 more expensive kindles. but now i'm about to just return both kindlesand go someplace else for a tablet and after all of this i plan not spend another dime at amazon.... just another giant conglomerate company who has lost sight of values and how to have good customer service and is only concerned about greed and profiting. best of luck to you amazon, you just lost a customer. and remember how many people i talked to about how great you were!!! i'll keep talking, but my comments won't be positive.

review_body: i debated between a ipad, samsung tablet, and kindle fire for a long time. i did a lot of research and decided that i was going to go the economical route of getting a fire. i needed a tablet to access recipes (tired of lugging my laptop to the kitchen to cook), wanted it to fit in my purse, or easily stowed for traveling, and i love to read so it had to have a reading app. i am very happy with what i got. i initially got the 6hd and a week later the 7hd dropped to the price i paid. amazon gladly exchanged my device so i upgraded to the 7. i use it all the time in the kitchen, have taken it with me on trips, and use it to read. i also realized that i could use it for music and movies! i am a prime member and it is so awesome to have all of these features. sometimes i get annoyed because i have to have wifi to utilize a lot of the features, but that would be the same problem if i were to get an ipad or samsung tablet. i love my kindle and am happy i didn't pay an arm and a leg for it. silk web browser works great and doesn't glitch as other users have said. i use my kindle more than my laptop but sometimes i do have to use the laptop to access certain sites that format funny on the fire, but it is rare.
