we bought this for my son (11 years old) mainly because amazon markets the freetime function as a way to control screen time for your kid. well, it can technically do that, problem is that's all it can do. when you set up a child's user profile, you can choose a younger child (8 and under) or older child (9 and over). then you have to select specifically what apps/books/videos the user can access. this is fine for a toddler but for any child older than 9 is a major pain. here's why:
1- the child's profile has no access to the app store. so either you always sit with them to browse the app store or you have to give them full access without any control over what they can see(on ios you can restrict the type of content on the app store to age appropriate only).
2- once you download an app, you have to go into the user profile and select that app to give it access to the child's profile. every time.
3- because the kindle is tied to your amazon account, your credit card info is already stored into the kindle. which means if you give them access to the amazon store, they can see what you have been looking at. this was almost disastrous during xmas as he could see everything we were looking at and some of the things were for him.
4- also because the kindle is tied to your amazon account, when my son renamed his device to his name amazon decided to rename my account as well.
the kindle is fine if you are buying for yourself or as a glorified reader. otherwise i found the settings difficult to configure and interface confusing to navigate. could be that i'm just too used to my ipad.
anyway, this device ended up on ebay (where it sold for 30% less) and he's saving up to get an ipad mini.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
this is an amazing device. ok, may not seem that way to an iphone user, but for someone like me who's never had a "smart phone", this little tablet is really cool! i find myself using the kindle more than i used to use my laptop pc. checking email is dead easy, it's easier to read my digital rc magazine on the kindle than it is on the laptop, and typing on the kindle is really easy thanks to the on-screen keyboard. the "word suggestions" that are displayed across the top of the "keyboard" are context sensitive, and it makes typing even easier. i can lay the tablet on my knees, in landscape mode, and type almost as easily as i can on the laptop. the learning curve on this device is pretty easy.

what was really surprising was that i found all the cds i've bought from amazon over the last few years in the "cloud". as long as i have a wifi connection, i have access to all these cds! woah! wifi sensitivity is very good, better than my laptop. it's essentially a smart phone without the phone, and without the monthly charges of a smartphone. (we'd looked into getting a smart phone so my wife could use an isquare card reader at some art shows she participates in, and the cheapest plan was $60/mo.) of course, having access to amazon on the kindle and being able to buy anything at the drop of a hat is another story. 8^) i have to watch myself. but i did find a couple cds i've been looking for for like twenty years!

so, now i feel like i'm truly in the 21st century, i have a "smart device" like most other people in the world now, but on my terms, no monthly charges, and it's, like, totally star trek-cool!!

review_headline: sound quality great, but screen too bright to read books
review_body:
pluses and minuses. glad i bought it but i will also continue to use the original kindle fire that came out in 2011 for reading books because the screen is easier on the eyes (with the tan screen that i call up). when i call up the tan screen on the fire hd 7, the screen is still too bright for comfort - at least to my eyes. the dual speakers give a better sound quality to the fire hd 7 so i can listen to audiobooks and streamed films without turning off the nearby fan, which i have to do with the original kindle fire where you have to turn off the fan or any other distraction to be able to hear the films.

about audiobooks, another drawback to the fire hd 7 is the fact there's so much extra stuff on it, that it stops downloading audiobooks from audiobooks.com and gives you a message that it can't download due to too much content on your device.

and when it does download, it takes a half hour to download (as with my most recent download of a book that wasn't overly long). on the original kindle fire, the downloads are much faster and i've never been told there's too much content on my device. i didn't think i had too much content on the fire hd 7, just all the items packed on the device plus a few extra things i downloaded to the carousel (a few magazines, books, a one-minute video taken by the fire hd 7 camera). so to get my audiobook to open, i had to delete other additions to the carousel.

if my message seems convoluted, i apologize, but what i've been talking about is a big deal to me and i don't like being annoyed by having so much crap on the fire hd 7 from programs i have no intention of using. in short, i have to retain the three year old original kindle fire in conjunction with the new fire hd 7 to get all my entertainment needs met. still, the fire hd 7 is much faster in downloads for facebook posts and opening yahoo email and in browsing news sites than the original kindle fire. how could the developers of the fire hd 7 make it more difficult to use in some ways and better in others? in short, don't throw away the old device, it's still good for many things.use in some ways and better in others? in short, don't throw away the old device, it's still good for many things.

review_headline: stay away from fire. very disappointed about the way amazon deals with a faulty device. worst purchase ever.
review_body:
i'm very disappointed with the fire. i've already went through three different devices and all have the same problems: after some weeks it is very difficult to charge them. at some point, i just stop using them. i have never had this problem with apple products, including the ipad, no matter how old they are.
i've been an amazon client for 15 years, i have prime and consume a lot of its content. after contacting customer support to see if there was some way to solve the annoying problems to charge the battery, they recognized that the fire has this known problem but since it seems that they do not have a solution or the device cannot be fixed they offered to sell me a discontinued refurbished model at a small discount from the price offered online. i'm now more disappointed about the whole experience. you can judge by yourself, this is a copy of the chat i had with customer support (btw, to add insult to injury, amazon never sent me the copy of the chat as they should and it is confirmed in the chat, i took the precaution of copying it, i obviously changed the names):

support: my name is support and i am from amazon kindle support. you’ve reached the right place and i will be happy to assist you today.
are you referring to "customer's fire"?
me: yes
support: are you unable to turn on your kindle device?
me: yes, when it is charged...the problem is to charge it. but sometimes it takesa lot of time (5 mins or more) to turn on, in the meantime i see the "fire" message
i mean, i'm able to turn it on when it is charged
support: how long did you charged the kindle device previously?
me: i do not know i leave it at night, some hours i guess
but this is not once in a time occurrence
this has been going for several months, in fact, i'm almost not using this device because of the charging issues
support:have you tried charging the device using a power fast charger?
me: i've tried with all types of chargers
the latest amazon power fast charger did not last more than a couple of months
support:i'm sorry about that, customer?
are you unable to use the kindle device properly now?
me: now i'm charging it, after 40 mins of fighting with it, i was able to get the "red" light
support:it looks like there is a problem with your kindle device.
i'm sorry, in this case, replacing the kindle device is the best option.
me: but i guess this is a common issue with this device, right?
support: yes, customer.
it looks like the one-year limited warranty for your kindle device has been expired. normally, we'll create replacement for the out of warranty kindle at a reduced price. in this case i can provide the options of the devices which we are offering at a reduced price and if you are not interested in any of these offers and if you prefer to purchase anew device i can offer a special discount on your new purchase.
me: ok, let me see, but i'm giving up with the fire
support: here are the available kindle model at the reduced price:
--certified refurbished kindle fire hd 7", hd display, wi-fi, 16 gb - includes special offers costs $129.00 and we are offering at $98.00.
--certified refurbished kindle fire hd 7", hd display, wi-fi, 8 gb - includes special offers costs $99.00 and we are offering at $79.00.
me:r efurbished??
support: every certified refurbished kindle device includes the same one-year limited warranty you receive with a new kindle device, and is subject to the same return policy as any new kindle device.
me: i have had so far two "new" devices, one worst than the other, i can only imagine how a refurbished one may work
support: a certified refurbished kindle is a pre-owned kindle that has been tested and certified to look and work like new.
in this case if you prefer to purchase anew kindle device i can offer $25.00 discount on your new purchase now.
me: i do not think i can give you more money for these failed devices, i already spend a lot on your site/devices/content, as you can check i've been a good customer for 15 years, but i've been really disappointed with the fire
but i see you agree with me, you are basically offering usd20-25 for my device
support: i'm sorry about that, customer.
me: device
that is probably what it is worth
support: in this case if there is a problem with these devices once it is replaced, you can return the device for a full refund.
me: what is the year of making of these refurbished devices?
support: i'm sorry. i don't have an exact year of making of these refurbished devices.
are we still connected?
me: yes
but it is the latest version or a previous one?
support: are you referring to a software version?
me: the software i guess can be updated, right? i refer to the device, is it the same model i can buy new now?
support: currently the same model kindle device is not available in our website.
we have more options which we are offering at a reduced price.
me: so, is it an old one?
please be specific
support: no, customer.
me: i understand it is a refurbished one, that is fine. but i want to understand of which model, could you tell me what is the processor?
support: unless otherwise noted on the product detail page, a certified refurbishedkindle is eligible for the optional two-year extended warranty offered by our third party partners.
i can also offer you the latest model devices at a reduced price now.
--fire hd 7, 7" hd display, wi-fi, 8 gb - includes special offers, black costs $139.00 and we are offering at $125.00.
me: jajajajaj
so basically you take off a 10%
i'm sorry i laugh
but at this point i cannot do otherwise
support: if you prefer to purchase any new kindle device i can offer $25.00 discount for your order now.
me: so the refurbished one you are offering correspond to an old/discontinued model? please tell me if this is not correct
support:yes, customer.
me: ja, ja, so basically you want to dump on me something that you are not going to sell anyway
refurbished for 100 bucks!!!
i was disappointed before, now i'm beyond disappointed
i guess you are sending a copy of this chat to my email as i asked
this goes exactly as it is to your reviews of the fire

chat*

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: a great tablet if you know what to expect.
review_body:
i have to say that overall it is a solid tablet. but know what you are getting and what you are getting in to. i like the tablet,even knowing full well that it was going to be somewhat limited in comparison to a galaxy tab or a nexus tablet. there are some apps that are unavailable and some apps that are just behind the main android release version. with that expectations set, here is my 2 cents.

the good:
the tablet feels really solidly made.
the fire fits in my hand easily and is easy to hold on to.
the screen quality and responsiveness is great.
the speakers are really good all things considered.
the ability to set up a child profile is great. especially since i can control what my kids see.
the amazon instant video and prime music work really well on this.
it integrates perfectly with the fire tv stick for watching something cast to my tv or if i wanted to start on tablet and then lay down and watch on tv.

the not great:
i feel the battery life is not very good. my wife's ipad easily outlasts this thing 4x as long. even my phone doing the same things would be 2x as long.
the limited app store feels lackluster in comparison to the google play store.
amazon instant video selection is unclear what is free and what you have to buy in some of the menus.
pushing an app to the device from the amazon website, while usually works well, sometimes is clunky and delayed for no apparent reason. (thereby forcing a refresh of purchased apps from my settings menu.)

i think the tablet itself is outstanding for the price, but i knew what to expect going in. a solid tablet that can carry out fairly basic functions and while limited, has an integrated app store.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: if this wasn't a gift i'd return it
review_body:
for a tablet "designed for entertainment" i find myself only using it for just books, as it lacks the qualities and features to be used for any other entertaining purposes.

reasons why
-amazon app store; its extremely lacking in good apps and its the only store you can use to download apps officially, sure you can side load apps but a lot of .apk are hard to find. there is no youtube app, because it like a lot of other app is associated with google. which is a big grievance of mine. if apple and android has it so should amazon. i have counted 12 apps that i have one my android phone, as well as my mothers ipad that can't even be downloaded and installed on this "tablet"

-sound quality: there is one speaker and it quieter than my smart phone.
-immersion reading with audible- it really suck, i enjoyed it a lot on my phone and really looked forward to it on my kindle,but i will not be using it. the one speaker that comes with this kindle plays the audible books at such a very low level it has to be close to my face to hear making it hard to read. i talked with both amazon and audible about this and they said nothing can be done because the kindle is made that way.

-lack of customization: you can not change the background or lock screen at all. i know it's petty but with the price i pay for this i should be able to do such a simple thing like that. if the knock off brands of tablets and phones can do it i expect a name brand product like one from a company as big as amazon to be able to do it as well.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
awesome product thus far! i purchased this for my stepson for christmas and he absolutely loves it!
pros: everything was pretty easy to set up, added my kid's preferences and apps fairly easy. i am not as pleased with free time as i thought i would be, but the functions that only allow your child on during certain times and only allow them to play for certain amounts of time are great :)

cons: the biggest ding i see is the fact that in freetime there is no option to have books read aloud! this is the biggest reason for 4 stars vs 5. i can do it in the regular (non-freetime) portion of kindle, but this is lacking in freetime. i found a book or two that will do this, however, there is no way of knowing until you have waited the ridiculous amount of time for it to download. my stepson is 5, so he can only read very easy level 1 books, but he loves ninja turtles and other books that are far above his reading level, so not being able to listen in freetime is a big bummer. also, we download alot of library books, and not only will it not read them to him in freetime, but everytime we get new books from library i have to go into apps for free time and add the books. honestly, i purchased this product over an ipad mini because of the "free time" portion for kids. however, it is not as amazing as i would like it to be. the "learning apps" are pretty mediocre at best. i found much better ones in the app store. also, apps and books take forever to download vs app store apps for some reason. also, for some reason audiobooks i have downloaded in overdrive app do not show up in free time, but this could just be a precaution so kids aren't reading inappropriate material, so technically a pro.

overall, the tablet is wonderful!! i would definitely recommend this over the kid's version tablet that is all in free time.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
i have mixed feeling about this version. i have the 2nd kindle fire and it's so much better, and built sturdier. i thought this would be a great upgrade, not so. it's not all bad, though. i love the sidebar slider when reading a book that gives you the table of contents and book details, such as description, etc. i do love the fact that i get my book collections now on this device. old fire didn't have that feature (which i have on my ipad kindle app). the bookmarks/notes access is better and i love that. i edit my own books on it, and it's easier to get to my notes and bookmarks. i love the prime music app...so far it works flawless. the screen resolution is great. the email app is equivalent. no complaints there and works well for my yahoo and gmail accounts. i haven't yet used it for video. the speakers are decent for a small device.

the bad:
the browser is just as slow as my old 3 year old fire. i was hoping to get a faster browser. nope. if i'm in my facebook app and i click on a link, i'll be lucky to get anything on the browser page, half the time it's just a blank page.

battery: worst ever. my old fire hasn't been charged in 2 weeks and its in standby mode and still has a 75% charge. this thing barely lasts 4 days in standby mode. it'll last a little longer in airplane mode, but not much. just reading a couple hours on the device and occasionally checking facebook and email, i have to charge it every other day. and it takes over 4 hours for a full charge from about 10%...way longer than the old fire.

books don't always download properly, i.e. i click and click on it and it doesn't do anything. when i delete a book, i sometimes have to power off completely for the book to remove itself from the device.

and why do random app icons keep showing up on my home page slider? i like to keep my slider clean with only the apps i'm using. but every day, there are random kindle and funny little screen apps showing up. i delete them and they come right back. so irritating.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: great device but a step backward in software
review_body:
i love my new fire--mechanically, anyway. i’m amazed at how great the sound is. i’m a heavy kindle user with over 2,000 books, and the fire hd 7 replaces a fire hd (3rd gen). most of my irritations stem from the most recent software update:

1. many of the things i often do on my kindle fire now take two or three clicks instead of one click. really unhappy about this--why would amazon make the fire less convenient to use?

2. since i use my kindle mostly as a reader, it's a big problem when books won't open. some books take longer to open or start to open then close again multiple times. this never happened before the latest upgrade.

3. another annoyance within the kindle app is the new response when text is selected. wikipedia/translation/dictionary seems to be the same, but the line of symbols above the selected text has been changed: "search in book" and "search the web" have been buried in a dot pile. perhaps i'm an anomaly, but i use both of those a lot, so it's an extra click each time--not a lot of extra work, but annoying just the same when it takes two clicks to do what you're used to doing with one click.

something i wish the program had is a sound for battery-low and battery-charged. i use it primarily as a reader, although i look up a lot of info online as well. when i'm reading, the battery icon doesn't show, so i have to leave the story to find out whether the battery level is low. since it now dings when it starts or stops charging, how about adding sounds that will really help readers keep using the product without interruptions? when my phone battery gets to 5%, i get a noise to remind me to charge the phone; when the battery gets to 100%, the phone makes a little rumble so i know it's time to unplug it. i wish the kindle did something similar.

the biggest annoyance is actually on the amazon site: the floating menu on "manage my content and devices" floats down so low,hardly any of the list can be seen on a kindle held horizontally. and it jumps in fits and starts which makes it even harder to see what's there or to click on an item. i use my kindle horizontally most of the time, and this page looks like it really wasn't designed with the user in mind. somebody wanted to do something slick, but it doesn't work for the consumer; the dropdown takes half the screen but sadly contributes almost nothing to page utility since it's mostly unused space. this really should be better.

i’ve written to customer service about these issues and get a response that indicated either they didn’t really read what i wrote or they didn’t understand the words i used. if amazon really wants to be “earth's most customer-centric company,” customer service needs to do a better job.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: fell far short of what i expected.....
review_body:
i am hoping to come back and have a change of heart. i asked for the fire tablet as a christmas present since i have the fire tv and the fire stick and both are wonderful. i figured this would work out great. i was sorely mistaken.

i will first talk about what i do like about the tablet. it is small, easy to use, and works well with prime. it also makes a great remote for both the fire tv and fire stick. the picture on it is pretty decent. i have been able to load and play music and videos that i love to use. the camera works pretty good - better than my phone for sure. lightweight, and not a whole lot to it... as i said before, easy to use.

now for the problems. first, there needs to be some updates. i thought at first that it just wasn't updating, but as it turns out it had, and was up to date. and with that i mean most of the apps that i use, for instance gmail. this is a common and popular app that should be updated. yes, i realize that the app maker is the one who has to release an update, but if they don't feel like it is worth their time, then they wont. it still doesn't change the fact that the app is out of date and it is better to use my phone, computer, ipad, or other tablet in the house instead. one of the biggest issues is the battery life. i am not sure if there is just something wrong with my battery, but it doesn't last for anything. i get about 4 hours at best-and i don't mean with a constant video playing either. i bought for my kids - 2 sero tablets, and a half defunct vizio tablet. all three of them have a battery life of about 6-8 hours. i thought maybe i was overdoing the tiny tablet, so i charged it all night, it said a 100%, i left for work after putting it to sleep, i came home and it said 10%. not sure why it would drain all day while in sleep/standby mode. i have looked up multiple answers and none of them work.

now, one of the greatest things about the fire tablet is the remote control... only it really takes some getting use to. it is very touchy and finicky. i have since purchased 1 random episode of sponge bob square pants that i did not want. also, when i use the fire tv remote app on the tablet, for some reason the screen will revert to the small upper corner preview video while in netflix. at first i didn't thing that was possible, it had to be with the tv. however, trying to diagnose how and why that happens, i could definitively say that it only happens when i use the tablet as a remote.

when i contacted technical support, i got simple answers - yes, that is normal. or, no, we haven't heard of that, i will get back to you and i was not contacted back. i have never had to deal with support since everything else i have gotten was awesome. not really sure if i want to bother.

these issues make this a very hard sell. i am glad it was a present and i didn't spend the money on it. it is definitely over priced for what you get. compared to all the other tablets i have (minus the ipad because it's on a different tier with price and hardware) that have a comparable price, i would not purchase this again, nor would i recommend it to any of my family or friends.

amazon really missed the mark. i was so happy with everything else i have gotten from then, i just didn't think this could be that far off. not to mention, when my brother ordered it, it was supposed to be here by christmas, but i didn't get it until after.

at time of purchase, was supposed to be here december 17. then was back ordered to january 17. came in early january, but was shipped to my brother's address instead of mine. yes we double checked that my address was on the where it was supposed to go address. we freaked out because he called me and let me know that it was left on my porch. but it wasn't on my porch. he looked up on amazon and it was supposed to go to my address, but then on the ups it showed amazon had hisaddress. we thought it was stolen, but was sitting on his porch (he parks and enters his place through his garage).

the whole ordeal was not one i would want anyone to go through. i would wait and see if they are going to make any changes that will improve multiple issues, and some common place issues that you would think customers would want taken care of from the get go.

review_body:

review_headline: good starter tablet, bad battery life.
review_body:
i had no idea what the "special offers" thing meant. we bought ours at best buy and when i set it up i couldn't figure out why there were ads every time i turned it out. after googling, i realized if you bought it "with special offers" it means that you were paying $15 less to have ads on your screen. not worth it. i paid the extra $15 by logging on to my amazon account and it was worth it.

the battery life on the fire is horrible. really really bad. doesn't compare even a little to iphone or ipad. it's a great little device, but if you're looking for something for a long road trip, be sure you have a charger.

the freetime for kids is a great option to have access to kids apps, books and shows for free (for amazon prime members) or paid for those who aren't. definitely than paying a la carte. if you read a lot, it's worth paying for kindle unlimited so you have access to as many books as you can read.

it's definitely been a learning curve since we're an ifamily, but she likes it a lot. it's can't be customized, i.e. screen savers, but it does the job and is a great starter for a kid.

review_body:
i am a kindle fire fan. yes, i think the ipads are cooler and more powerful, but this is the perfect tablet for my young children. plus, it isn't so expensive that if they drop it, break it, or damage it in some way i will go into cardiac arrest. i let them watch three to four cartoon episodes on it at a time (we have prime), so i can have time to myself during the day. the kindle fire has saved my sanity, honestly.

for those of you considering free time, i would suggest that you pass on it. you can easily customize settings on the fire and in your amazon account. so, for example, you can prevent your kids from downloading media or from watching tv shows above a g rating. it's really easy to do and doesn't take up a lot of space on the hard drive. i don't have any problems with my kids sneaking mature shows (not that they would want to at this age, but still).

overall, we are so happy with our kindles. it was money well spent.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: much more than a kindle reader
review_body:
first of all, some disclaimers. i have been a full sized laptop (15.6" screen) and net-book user for over a decade, so this is my first device that uses a touch screen/tablet format. i have also been a fan of windows and have written hundreds of apps using windows api. i have been considering a kindle for a long time, especially since some of my co-workers use them at work.

after i ordered this device from amazon i read many negative reviews from the 2012 period and was concerned i had made a mistake. i justified my purchase by thinking that this only had to be a reader with wifi and a usb port. after a few weeks of use i could not be more amazed at the capability of this device. i use it mainly as a reader and it was easy to move my pdf files from my laptop to this device with the usb connection. i use the adobe app for reading my pdf books and it works great. the only drawback i can see is that i need to re-size the page each time i start a new page, but it is a small issue. this is not necessary with kindle format books. kindle format books are very easy and intuitive to use.

i was also concerned with getting a device with "offers included". again, this is a non-issue. i only see an offer when i first turn on the device. when i sweep the screen to unlock it, i never see another offer. every offer i have seen so far has been geared towards gamers, which does not interest me at all. i fact i would be interested in seeing offers of technical (mathematics, engineering, science) books with the kindle format. amazon could make some money off me it they would catch on to this.

the screen keyboard instantly comes up when needed and is sufficiently useful for entering small amounts of data to an excel spreadsheet or for a small document. i cannot touch type with the screen keyboard, it is just too small, so that work is done on my full size laptop. i plan on creating apps for my device so there is a bluetoothkeyboard purchase imminent.

i watch a lot of youtube videos, and this device is excellent for that purpose. i also like the map app that came on the device. it includes a satellite view which comes in handy. the cameras are easy to use and come in handy at times.

an important (good) attribute of this device is its small size and weight. the net-book i used to carry is now a back up lap-top. my fire is all i ever need to carry and it fits in every pocket of my backpack.

as a windows fan, i found adapting to the android operating system, extremely easy. the email app works great.

i have never tried loading a full movie on this device since i have the 8gb model. i have watched several movies by streaming and that process works fine. if you want to load more than one movie you may want to get the 16gb version or buy a different device. i suspect watching more than a couple of movies would run down the battery on this device, so for overseas air travel, you may want to stick to just reading books.

overall, for $138, this device is a good value.

review_headline: i'm glad i bought the kindle fire.
review_body: i'm happy with this product and wish i had more free time to enjoy it more often. it works well as a book reader and when playing android games. i've downloaded a number of quality free games. the availability of quality free games is a great bonus. however, i have two complaints that amazon could work on to improve the product over time. the charger, charges the battery a bit slow, so they need a faster charger. luckily, i have one that i use for other devices. i listened to internet radio for 1 and 1/2 hours and the battery was 85% gone. wow, they could improve the life of the battery to be more appropriate for wireless tasks such as internet radio listening and internet video viewing. currently, if i'm going to watch videos or listen to internet radio, i do so with the kindle plugged in so that the battery will not get depleted of power. also, the kindle fire speakers could use a little improvement, the sound is not crisp when you turn up the volume. without headphones in use, this speaker system struggles a bit with the sound quality. i was weird because the speaker issue was most noticeable while i was using the speakers for text-to-speech listening of books, but was less of an issue when playing games and listening to internet radio. so maybe the speakers can be better suited for speech. lastly, amazon should disclose up-front that with a kindle unlimited membership you can only take out a maximum of ten books at a time. once you've checked out or downloaded 10 books, you have to return a books for each additional book that you want to add. i'm not disappointed with the ten book maximum, but why does it seem like a secret fact until you are using the membership. currently, i'm still in the trial period, but yes there will be months when i order the kindle unlimited membership, but probably not every month because i'll be buying some books to keep and some months i will have very limited free time. also, it's true that kindle unlimited doesn't included new releases but it does contain a good number of top books written years ago and classics, stuff written decades ago. for example, one could download any of the harry potter books; one just has search kindle unlimited to see if the monthly subscription would be of interest to them. amazon should make it easier to get the search box into that restricted search that will only return search results for kindle unlimited books. i personally, keep having to try this and that to get get amazon to perform a kindle unlimited only search. lastly, i would advise that people download the free lookout internet protection because the kindle does have internet access and it does hold personal info, and you will likely type in person info and passwords as you sign in for access to stuff.

review_headline: i consider myself smart enough to learn the basics of a device such ...
review_body: first, i ordered the kindle and once received had trouble connecting it to the wifi.  my internet provider asked that i return the modem/wifi to the store an get another one.  the second one had the same problems.  so, they stated it was not a problem with the wifi, but the kindle itself.  it simply would not connect.  they asked that i return the kindle, which i did.  amazon provided me with a new kindle and i was immediately able to get it connected to the wifi.  the kindle was as i expected.  apparently, i didn't read far enough that i could only "borrow" one book a month from their library.  i read at least 4-6 books a month.  so, i have to purchase any thing beyond that?  another added expense that i did not anticipate, after i had purchased amazon prime to get all the "frills"....video streaming, cheap books, etc.  it suddenly appeared to me this could be a real money pit.  additionally, i am 72 y.o. and though i'm not a techie, i consider myself smart enough to learn the basics of a device such as this.  however, i found it almost impossible.  if i pulled up a tutorial, it was absolutely hopeless.  i have 4 friends who swear by the kindle.  but, i should have listened to them more intently.  i recall in conversations with them that they were often calling kindle support folks for help with one thing and another. ...on a regular basis.  i have enough stress in my life, and i didn't need to add anymore.  i have netflix streaming, plus a couple of netflix dvds a week, plus 5 televisions, and a library about a mile away.  i just couldn't see any reason to keep the kindle, so i sent it back.  i mainly purchased the kindle because my wife has cancer and she was going to have chemo/radiation treatments 5x a week for 7-8 weeks at 2 hours at a time.  i thought the kindle would be something to help me pass the time while awaiting her treatments.  turns out, she declined the treatments, so even if i wanted to keep the kindle, i really had no reason to doso.  i really don't think this device is for everyone.

review_headline: nice product, but amazon still has work to do when it comes to apps they provide
review_body: the kindle fire hd 7" is a nice tablet and for the price it somewhat forces you into trying it out.  unfortunately there are just too many issues to give it more of a rating than 3 stars.  dont get me wrong, its a well built, nice feeling tablet.  the os is pretty nice and fairly user friendly but so are many other options out there.  one issue with this is that you don't get amazon's incredible service unless you buy the hdx version. they really should provide this with all of their newer devices.  my biggest issue is that not all software works on a kindle. my phone can run several well put together applications designed for the android os that amazon doesn't even provide, even though they work flawlessly on several other android devices. but why not kindle?  even if i look past that and shop for the apps that amazon does allow and deem compatible for kindle, literally half of what i've downloaded for my kindle from amazon wont work. why? you'd think if they go through some crazy process to allow only certain products on the kindle that they'd make sure those products actually work with their kindles.  crazy how that is.  several apps crash and freeze the tablet to the point where you have to hard power off the device just so you can use it.  crazy!  lastly, the profiles are a very nice feature except that they still have a lot of work.  its very time consuming to have the admin download and install software then make it usable for each profile but understandable. but some things only work under the main admin account, not under profiles.  i want my son to be able to watch amazon prime when he's on it but in his profile it isnt available.  i can download movies we've purchased and make only the downloaded movies available to him but not the streaming prime movies or shows.  its pretty crazy... maybe i'm missing something but i've looked all over for a setting and nothing can be found... this points back to my first issue too, it would be better if amazon's service would help me out without buying the hdx.  anyway, we are keeping it and will use it for now but we most likely won't be buying another kindle in the future.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
i started looking into the kindle fire around christmas when the rca tablet that i had purchased kept crashing. i had only had it about 3 months and it was the second off-brand tablet i had purchased- trying to save a few bucks- that i had been disappointed with. i decided to look into the kindle fire because i love my original kindle and shop with amazon all the time so i know i can trust product i buy on the site.

i am a mom who likes to volunteer so using this as a tablet is perfect for me seeing as i don't use it every day in a professional capacity but when the need arises it really can function the way i need it to. i have a bluetooth keyboard i can take with me to school and church meetings-- i downloaded the word app-- making it super easy to take notes. the battery life is not for all day use (i had a 8 hour planning meeting the other day) but was able to plug it into the usb on someone else's computer to keep it going. i also love that it's amazon so all of my purchases from other devices are synced. just like any other business if you keep it in the family it makes things easier.
i also like that it's still a kindle with a wide variety of books. i still have my paper white but love that on my fire hd the covers and pictures are in color and that the table of contents are easier to navigate with a touch screen.
i am so glad that i spent the extra money and got the bigger screen and memory. my friends got their daughters the smaller fire hds and after comparing the feel and usability of the smaller screen i am happy with my choice-- if i want a small screen i'll switch to my phone ;) but it is still small enough to fit comfortably in my purse.

of course there is a learning curve with the layout, especially if you're used to working on other tablets but nothing that is too difficult, it just takes some getting used to.
i do have some issues with app availability. there are several apps that are available in the itunes store or google play that simply aren't available in the amazon app store, and if they are, they aren't the same version (cut the rope for example).

all in all i would recommend this product to others.

review_headline: still getting to know the fire
review_body:
i purchased two of these for my children intending initially to use free time to control their access. i quickly discovered some limitations. first, i chose the fire over the e ink because i wanted the whispersync technology for my son, but then i learned that free time will not allow whispersync to work, which meant he had to access my account, which pretty much defeated the purpose of free time, which, let's face it, was really too juvenile for him anyway.

i should add, however, that free time is a great option for my daughter who prefers to read rather than listen. we tried out a month of free unlimited, but we calculated that the small number of apps she enjoyed would be cheaper to purchase.

most disturbing, however, is the frequency of "freezing" on my daughter's fire. my son's works fine, but my daughter's kindle freezes daily, and we have to power it down and start it up again before the touch screen will work.

i still have high hopes for the devices once i learn to use them more effectively, but my favorite kindle is still the old e-ink kindle i have from years ago.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: excellent tablet. accessories could use more variety.
review_body:
been wanting a tablet that i could read books on and keep with me for work in situations where a laptop simply wouldn't be practical, and the fire hd7 delivers.
pros: easy to use, yet powerful enough to run some serious software (for a tablet). great sound and a screen packed with pixels. the claims of an 8 hour battery life will depend on usage, but i've gotten 15 hours out of it even watching a movie. i imagine that, in airplane mode (essentially turns off wireless, bluetooth, etc..) i could easily net 20 hours of use before recharging. it's also fairly durable. not a tank, but it will survive normal everyday use without issue.

cons: for the tablet itself? none so far. however, there do not seem to be a great presence of tablet cases "designed" for the fire series, and virtually every universal 7" tablet case has a camera hole for the right side of the tablet. (the fire's forward camera is top left), and there are no tablet cases i've found so far that incorporate a keyboard that are universal and/or for the fire. if amazon were to produce such a case, i (and many others, i'm sure) would be very pleased.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: quirky device or user error?  either way...this is not a user friendly device!
review_body:
there seem to be so many quirks with this device. the screen was constantly going partially black the first week and my kids were getting very frustrated. i think i figured out what was going on. a couple of the apps had not fully loaded so i removed them and reload them onto the device. it seems to be running a little better but is still running pretty slow.

i set the tablet up so that the kids would each have their own profile and i would have my own profile as the main account. it was laborious setting it up. once i loaded all the apps onto the tablet through my account, i then had to approve which child could play with each app. that was not a problem and relatively easy to do. but, when they go on the first time to use them it then has to load those same apps into their profiles. the app is already on the device. why does it need to load that app into 4 different profiles??? does that mean it is taking up 4x the space?

i also decided to take advantage of the free month of amazon free time for the kids. free time changes their profile screen and adds all the items they can load from free time based on their age. it is overwhelming for them. their home page should only have the items that they have currently loaded on their profile. maybe it is user error and i'm just not doing it right. not sure.

i cannot load a lot of the apps that my kids like because they are not in the amazon store. i didn't realize that was going to be the case. there are even some apps that i use that i cannot get. very frustrating.

i am seriously considering returning the device because i feel like there is some internal glitch in it that causing it to run slow and for apps to sit in limbo and not load. any advice from other fire hd owners would be welcome in comments under this post. i am gonna give it another week. if it is user error i would love to figure out the quirks of this device. i think i am used to the user friendly apple products so this one is throwing me for a loop ;)

- it takes a while to charge. i had it on airplane mode and it took about 7 hours to charge from 0-100%

i would recommend this for older people and children. for those that are trying to sync business and pleasure in one tablet, this is not for you.

review_headline: warranty doesn't outweigh all the bad...
review_body: our family purchased two of these for our 5 & 6 year old children.  i read through some of the very well written reviews and from everything i read, the price point and the 2 year warranty, we were happy with our decision.  that's until we've had the chance to use these on a daily basis since christmas.    everyday, yes, everyday the wifi is turned off (an automatic feature) because there isn't enough space.  daily, i have to go through & delete everything so the wifi can be turned back on and the kids can play. how many apps could my kids download that would cause this daily?  that's a great question since they aren't able to download apps, they are just playing the already available games on it. is it pictures by chance?  not necessarily.  however, if they do have a selfie session as kids love to do, you'll be having a storage issue multiple times during their daily allotted time.  why wouldn't my kids be able to play without wifi?  i can still play games and access things on my ipad w/out wifi. zoodles (an app similar to \\"freetime\\") will still work w/out wifi, of course some apps won't play but, many still will.  well, freetime, (the app that keeps them locked into the \\"safe\\" area) will not work without wifi at all, at all!!!! so my children initially kept getting frustrated thinking they had broken it or it had gone bad and i have to fix the storage again and turn the wifi back on again.    also, i didn't realize how much i would want to \\"push\\" certain apps into the educational category.  of course it makes good business sense to only have \\"book\\" (good call kindle/amazon.  good call. i bet your stockholders are happy with that one.) apps count as education however, we are working on phonics, writing, math, letter recognition all of which i should be able to indicate that i want these apps to be accessed during the \\"education only\\" time allotment.  my six year old needs beginner base level reading books, her age selection evidently puts her at more advanced booksand education time only lets her read.... she quickly gets bored and frustrated and wants to do something else.    we also had the first kindle freeze w/in a few hours and after two ts calls (the first promised a return call & never called back!) discovered it was a system hardware issue and ts refused to comment if this was a high occurring issue (integrity issue/red flag!).  of course they issued a replacement kindle however, whether or not it's new or a refurbished, i can't be sure, i haven't researched that.    we've had these for nineteen days so far and the android \\"lag\\" is already evident and showing.  also, many popular apps aren't kindle friendly.  google play also isn't an option.  play nice amazon, nobody likes haters.    the positives: that warranty.  however, with the frustrations make it totally not worth it, imo.    lesson: returning these for a full refund and paying an extra $79 for ipad minis plus the cost of a case because the fluidity, the memory, the camera, high selection of quality kid apps loaded to apple platform first just make it a better choice for me and my family.  plus osmo is only available with ipads, my kids love that app.

review_body:
my boyfriend bought this for me at a bricks-and-mortar store, so i can't tell you anything about shipping. what i can say is that i have an android os phone, and i'm able to use the same apps and games that i have on the phone on this device. reading on this device is great with lots of options that allow almost anyone to be able to read easily. i also use the "my cookbook" app, and use this device in the kitchen when i'm cooking something that i need a recipe for. videos from youtube and hulu plus are also very clear on this device.

the camera isn't the best; however, it's better than the camera on my phone, and you can edit the pictures using the program on the device to make pictures look better. the device is wi-fi capable, but it sometimes isn't a very stable connection. for instance, if i tilt the device, i'm apt to lose a bar on my "connection meter," or it drops the signal altogether. sometimes it can take a while to load up web pages, even though the amazon appstore loads up pretty quickly.

if you are a reader who likes to have some games, a few handy apps on your device, something to check your email from time to time with, and the occasional picture; this tablet is for you. if you plan on using the camera for a document scanner app, and need documents to be pretty clear; you might want to pick a different tablet. however, it does do what i need it to do, so it works for me!

review_headline: great upgrade from a second-generation fire
review_body:
we have a second-generation fire, so i was a little hesitant to order this because i wasn't sure it would be much different. however, the sales around christmas were too good to pass up, and as much as we use our fire, i knew we would appreciate having a second.

the processor in this fire is much faster than the other one we have. the silk browser has crashed a couple of times, but not nearly as frequently as in the second generation version. apps also respond more quickly (for example, i never used the pinterest app on our other kindle because it was a pain, but it works great on this fire). the keyboard spacing is also much improved, and i'm not constantly hitting the wrong letter because they're placed so close together.

one other thing worth noting is that the buttons and speakers have moved around since the second generation. i prefer the new placement with the exception of the speakers. they are now located on the bottom (long edge) of the device, so when we set it on a flat surface to watch movies, the sound is muffled. overall, though, this device is a big improvement over the second generation, and we're going to get a ton of enjoyment out of it!

review_body: i got a kindle fire hd as a gift. it was affordable, fairly fast, and of fairly high quality. however, my personal freedoms outweigh amazon's obsession with their walled-garden appstore service that has none of the applications that actually serveany purpose to me. with the recent update, amazon appears to have done nothing but unroot my device, delete most of my applications and important data, and give me some free music, presumably in an attempt to satiate my undoubted rage that whenceforth ensued. i understand that rooting your device is against amazon's terms of service involving the device, but going out of one's way to take away the customer's rights involving their own piece of hardware, and in turn taking away one of the most important traits of any linux system: freedom, is simply and undeniably horrible business practice. i am one whose philosophies involving software are that above all else, the ability to have the freedom to do whatever one must to achieve their goals is absolutely essential. this is why i use linux. it has become clear to me that amazon does not care for the only reasons android exists, through managing to not make their system open, and also managing to make the software you install on it locked as well. i will cease using amazon products completely once i procure enough money to buy a new tablet. in the meantime, i will attempt to order a factory cable from which to load cyanogenmod onto my device, an action i was going to do anyways, but seems to have been rushed in amazon's removal of my personal digital liberties. i hope this serves as a warning to those few who realize the importance of these types of things that i, for one, cannot stand for any longer.

review_body: we purchased two of these for christmas for our son and daughter, and purchased an apple ipod and ipad for our older son and daughter at the same time.  this has given me the chance to have all 4 devices in use for the past 4 weeks.  i\\"m on the verge of returning the kindles at this point and swapping them out.  my main complaint is how limited a \\"child\\" or \\"teen\\" profile is.  out of the box the only thing that works for a child or teen is the camera.  kid wants to use the calculator for homework?  sorry.  want to have an email account.  no go.  i called amazon tech support and the only way around this is to buy a 3rd party app for the calculator or email, as you can't get the default kindle apps to work in the child / teen profiles.  the other alternative was to create an adult profile for the kids, but that requires me to create separate amazon accounts for them.  another complaint is the time limit settings per day.  the time limits differentiate between reading, video and apps.  unfortunately, all apps are the same so even if they're using a \\"good\\" app like a math program, that uses their time.  once they run out of time there's no way for me to add say another 30 minutes for the day.  my only option is to either increase their time allowance overall, or disable it altogether.  i called amazon tech support and shared these concerns with them, but there was very little they could do other than share my feedback (understandably).  maybe we just have unique use cases, but for us, these devices don't work, and i think it's time to swap out for a more functional but albeit more expensive idevice.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: cheap, but not worth it.  software is confusing but doesn't give you any actual control.
review_body:
we bought these for our kids for christmas because they had nexus 7's before from relatives, and they were great. these however are horrible. the hardware seems sufficient, but the software is a mess. their lauded child management option "freetime" is of course subscription based, but even if you have the subscription managing what the kids do and do not have access to is a nightmare.

you have to log into your adult profile, turn off parental controls (which requires two password entries, one to get to the screen, and another to turn it off), then you buy the app and install it, but the install only goes to your adult profile, you then need to associate it to the child profile, turn the parental controls back on (two more password entries), log out of the adult profile, log into the child profile, then go to the apps tab, and install it all over again on the child profile.

only after all of that can your kid play the game, app, whatever.

my wife and i use this little tablet games as reward for chores, and they can also save up money to buy in game stuff, but with the fire tablet you cannot make any ingame purchases with a child profile. there is no way around this, no setting to type in your parent password twice to let them make the purchase.

i saw that amazon had this amazon coins that could be used for in game purchases. i thought great, this must be the way to allow your kids to buy stuff in apps, assign some coins to their profile, and they cant' ever spend more than you give them. perfect.

nope, can't do that either, child profiles cannot make any purchase whatsoever. i just spent 15 minutes walking my wife through trying to add a spelling game to my daughters tablet, it's ridiculous.

google's ecosystem and tablets were much easier to manage, and gave me full control of what my kids could and couldn't do.

the amazon fire is a mess. i definitely won't be buying one again.

review_body:
i gave this kindles fire several chances to change my mind about giving this one-star review. the reason for the one-star is not for it's actual performance -- which, unfortunately, i never really was able to enjoy -- but instead is for the fact this kindle fire is just a dud. perhaps that's the reason they were practically given away this past holiday season.

the battery never fully charges (and there was also no way to know if it was charging -- it certainly never popped up stating it was fully charged. but i have no way of knowing if that is even something this kindle does, because there is not a user guide)

after charging, the kindle would operate for less than one day. it would then take two days to re-charge!! two days! was it the charger?
hmmm... the charger was generic in nature, no way to tell if was oem. it wasn't wrapped in the package. i tried different charger. a message would pop up with each charger stating charger was "low flow" and indicating the kindle couldn't be used while attached to the charger. not sure how much longer a "low flow" charger would take than the kindle charger because i didn't want to take a chance it would harm the device.

i am sorry to say this but, i am pretty sure this was re-conditioned and not new. the box was not sealed. there were no directions, user guide or anything accompanying the item but it's unwrapped, unsealed charger.

my bad, i threw out the packaging. it is doubtful there would be a successful return because of this. did i even try. no. first to admit, i didn't even make the effort. why: lately, my returns w/ amazon have been less than satisfactory, and my contribution to the return of this item will most likely cost me more time than i am willing to give.

so that's my review. doubtful i will ever buy another amazon electronic.

review_body:
the 4th generation kindle fire hd7 is a great tablet, plenty fast, and browses the internet with ease. however, the way amazon has made their os, does not allow for much customization and only most 3rd party applications will work in this tablet.

unfortunately for the latest kindle, there are no means of rooting your device, so google play is not an option to have directly on your kindle fire tablet.

one last thing. the "special offers" are entirely not appreciated and are a bit of a nuisance to see on my lock screen, yes i know you can pay amazon $15 to take the adds off, still don't like how amazon does that.

so to wrap things up i like the hardware of the tablet, its a pretty slick thing, i just don't like software loaded on the device, which for another $50 i can find an equal competitors tablet running the latest version of android, featuring equally performing hardware and overall is more capable of a tablet

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: amazon could do a better job - usability and stability issues.
review_body:
as a book reader, it does it job for most part, and it serves purpose as occasional entertainment device,

pros: price, display, audio

cons: the looks are somewhat flimsy, but comparing price with other devices it's steal. amazon is trying to provide good options, but they are confusing e.g., i can't figure out what's part for freetime subscription vs prime. even prime time content is hard to explore. skill browser crashes at times and slow to load content at other times. camera is very low resolution, so even though you get unlimited storage, you can get better quality with smart phones.
i have run into few challenges with usage and support is unable to help. e.g, i created a word doc, spent and week of hard work, and by accidental swipe, doc vanished. tech support mentioned point blank - you lost it, no way to recover, next time back it up to cloud. on asking how to backup a doc to cloud, answer was feature does not exist, so email every time you update a doc. second option given was to restore from backup, on going to backup/restore page, there was no restore option. i was told the feature is not implemented yet, so best way is to reset fire to factory default. so using it to create docs/excels is a no no, unless you figure out easy backup option. other unfriendly thing is switching user profiles - you need to hit power button, and then back again and then choose different user profile.
also you would expect fire would make shipping on amazon easier, but that's not quite easy as said.
overall, i guess we are spoiled by higher standards set by iphone/ipads.

review_headline: better battery life would be nice. but let's compare....
review_body:
i am a long time apple user - and happy to be one. but i constantly get asked how to fix something on a kindle fire and got tired of saying "i don't know" so i decided to buy this model. i have to admit, i wanted to see if it matched up to all the hype i hear - and i have to admit, it's got some nice features. in fact, it can do almost the same things as my ipad, even with it's funky navigation.

once i got used to the carousel, and after observing several children while using the kindle fire 7, i'm not as mad about the carousel as i was at first. overall the kindle fire 7 is nice, and once you know how to find what you want, it's not so frustrating on the surface. i do have minor complaints, , such as, having no physical home button, which i find almost necessary, especially for a young child old who can't manipulate the screen well enough to get the home button to appear.

my main complaint though, is the battery life - and as i said, i have things to compare to: i have 3 other kindles, plus two ipads for starters. not one of those units - not even my older ipad 2 nor my kindle 2, has such a poor battery as this unit does. i can play on my (year old) ipad mini all day long and still have half the battery left. and i use such taxing games as school of dragons or rise of berk as well as keep my email running all the time on the ipad. yes, these games require sound and motion. when i play these games on the kindle i'm lucky to get 3 hours on the unit before that icon turns red - and i do not even run any email on my kindle at all. i charge it over night, and the next day by noon it's already drained. i do the same thing with my ipad mini and use it with the same programs for the same amount of time and i can go 3 or more days without a charge.

my settings on the kindle and ipad mini are the same; brightness set at about 40%: wifi on. no headphones. i start the day with a full charge. one game is open at a time (the exception here is that i do use email on my ipad). the games i play require both wifi and sound and i prefer not to use headphones - never have used them on my ipad and don't want to start now just because i'm using a kindle.

video and audio is why i wanted this unit - and when i read suggestions on how to "improve battery life by using headphones instead of the speakers" or "turn off the wifi" i can't help think -- what!!? that's why people buy this thing! many of our games require sound and i do not recommend headphones for children. and what if i'm streaming a movie from amazon prime? i have to use wifi for that. and if more than one person is watching the movie, what does amazon want me to do, plug it in? tether it? then i lose the portability of the thing.

review_body: i work at home and use a regular tower computer so this is the first \\"portable\\" device i have ever owned therefore i don't have anything to compare it to.  a small learning curve for me was required such as the visual rotary tray.....every time i looked at something, fire seemed to throw it on tray (carousel)and i may have not wanted it there.  it took my son to show me a long press on the item in the tray enables you to get rid of it from the carousel, very easy, but i didn't know.  res is very high (watched a movie from netflix and was very clean looking) and hooking up to my home wifi was very easy.  checking email, surfing the web, downloading a book, which i did right away, was all easy to learn, just had to play with it a bit. was a bit surprised to see how many gigs of the eight gigs the operational system gobbles up but if you are cloud storing things i suppose it does matter too much.  very quick operating system (you indicate an item and it comes right up).  all in all for me it is a great tool and would buy again.  four stars simply because i immediately saw some areas that could be possibly improved.  for example why can't they figure out a way to put the speakers in the front, after all everybody knows the tiny speakers are going to suck pretty bad but putting them in the back is worse.  can't do that? how bout little ears that pop out and direct the sound forward?  a simple tasteful white dot on the front where the corner of the on and off switch is would keep me from having to flip the thing around every-time i pick it up  to use it. probably will purchase a case/stand so i can read without having to hold it constantly, i better get one soon cause i am sure to drop this thing.

i've owned a original fire since they were first released. in fact, i pre-ordered it. i can honestly say that it is the only device i have, besides my phone, that i use every single day. this new hd kindle has a slightly better screen but where it really shines is the sound. it's almost amazing how good it sounds. i was also quite surprised that, after shooting a photo with the built in camera, i could print that photo to my network printer. no discovery, no set-up, just press print and there is was. i'm a google user and after downloading the send to my kindle app for chrome i can now send any web-page directly to my kindle for reading later-on at my leisure.

review_headline: they're good, just a few qualifications on that
review_body: we've bought several of the fire's.  one i bought for reading and mail.  the others for our kids.    i like the way fire works for reading but prefer the additional flexibility of our samsung tab for getting apps from google play store.  that being said, the fire works great and is really good about saving battery power.  i would highly recommend if your needs include reading, mail, maps, surfing the web etc.  if you're a nut about specialty apps such as gps tools or satellite dish alignment tools you probably won't be so happy.    the kids love their fire's because of the content provided by amazon free time.  i also love it since we have good control over what they do on their tabs.    another drawback, i can't see how to add more storage and the 8 gb we got fills up quick.  not a big deal if you don't mind deleting stuff every week or two.  and there is a built in tool for doing that.  but i think they should put a slot for memory cards in them since most folks have plenty of memory cards laying around.  i imagine they didn't give that option for something to do with copyright protection etc.  so make sure you get one with plenty of memory, i wouldn't go under 16 gb.  i didn't notice this til it was too late.    and price for the fire's can't be beat (we bought cheaper regular hd models).    overall, good tabs if they meet your needs.

review_headline: an improved kindle in color no less
review_body: i got this as a gift and it was a replacement for my two year old kindle fire. this one finds a wi-fi network, you don't have to find it, it's lighter and thinner, and receiving email is more reliable. the link on the carousel tells you if you have new messages and how many. my old one would occasionally refuse to update until i lucked upon the refresh icon, which i never knew was there. i did have a major problem to begin with. my books and other apps transferred from my old kindle but the books would not open and when i first tried to read one, the screen went black and shut down the entire kindle. i could not start up again without hooking it to a charger even though it was charged. however a very nice customer service rep called me and walked me through a hard shutdown and told me if that didn't fix the problem they would send me a new device. it worked and he sent me some instructions to keep for future reference. because of the customer service i will give it five stars, rather than rating it lower because of the initial problem. if i want to read a book it does load more slowly than the old one. the battery life is quite short. one other thing, amazon really ought to include some basic, written instructions with these devices. this one did come with a diagram, but it would be nice to have something to start with, rather than searching on the screen for what you need. for example, there are two camera lenses, there is lots of info in the on screen guide about storing photos, but no where does it tell you how to take a photo. i finally figured it out, but it should not have been so hard.

review_body: my husband bought this for me for christmas, and i like it, but it's not as great as my nook color. (why didn't i just stay with my nook? well, it was pretty old, and for whatever reason i could never get it to connect to my wi-fi. it would connect everywhere else, just not to mine. so i thought it was time for an upgrade.) i would have given the kindle fire hd 7 5 stars, but i can't customize it the way i want; i can't change the background or lockscreen images on it, and i think it's pretty sad that you have to pay extra to get it without the advertisements on it. also, the camera is pretty terrible on it. i didn't want this for the camera as i've got a pretty nice camera already, but still. it's pretty bad. if you ever had the original motorola razor phone and took pictures with it, that's about how bad the camera on this is. so, if you're wanting an e-reader that you can customize, change background and lock screen images, not have to pay extra to not have advertisements on it, and have a decent camera then this is not for you. but, if you want an e-reader that allows you to surf the internet, download certain apps, and listen to music on without all those other things and you don't care if it has ads on it, then i'd get this one as long as it's on sale. otherwise, you can find e-readers of the same quality without ads that you can customize for less money.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: i was quite disappointed to realize that freetime is designed for much younger ...
review_body:
this was my 8 year old's big christmas gift/surprise. the factors that prompted me to buy a fire hd7 over another tablet were the price ($119) and the kids freetime account allowing me to prohibit access to mature content. i immediately signed up for the additional $3/month for unlimited freetime, which gave her extra apps and books. however, i was quite disappointed to realize that freetime is designed for much younger kids, as the programs are all very juvenile and one cannot access the internet via freetime at all.

i ended up cancelling the unlimited content and not utilizing the freetime option at all. instead, i set the parental controls to prevent downloading any apps or making purchases without me entering a password. she can't watch rated pg-13 or r movies, either. however, i've not found a good way to limit internet surfing (to prevent accidental redirection to porn or chat rooms, that kind of thing). that's a major flaw, imho. i also can't find a way to not share my library from my ipad/iphone with the fire, so at present, i'm having to trust her to only read her own books and not mine. this is not the scenario i envisioned when i purchased this device.

my daughter is ecstatic with her fire, but i'm deducting a star for not having the ability to customize restrictions based on the age/maturity of the child.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: fire hd or hd kids 6"/7" 8gb is not for children.
review_body:
intro:
we originally bought these for our 3 (5, 6, & 8yrs) boys instead of the kindle kids. kindle kids are just a pre-packaged kindle fire hd 6 or 7" 8gb device with 2 year warranty, kindle case and 1 year free time. at the time we bought this the hd 7" they were $79 after some discounts ($237 for all 3). with the 6.99 family free time, 3 kindle kids case (74.97), 3 2 yr kindle hd 7 warranty (89.97) it was about $40 dollars cheaper than the kids hd 6 and $158 cheaper for the kids hd 7".

con: (tltr)
my biggest gripe about the whole thing is the storage capacity. i should have realized the 8gb probably would not be sufficient and on top i had forgotten that kindle devices stated storage size is actually less. 8 gb (4.5 gb available to user) or 16 gb (11.6 gb available to user) of internal storage http://www.amazon.com/dp/b00ikpykwg/ref=nav_shopall_k_hd7#tech
additionally, if the device reaches around 10-15% it gets laggy, games freeze up.

con: (detailed)
so after loading up the initial profile (w/out downloading content) and then loading up a child's free time account already starts taking up space. you have 2 accounts now with default data. so after about 3-4 hrs of my kids playing with their new devices i already had to remove content to re-enable wifi access (yes once device reaches a certain amount it disables wifi). childs free time storage is not accessible from the parents account side or thru the child's account unless its reached a limit/wifi was disabled. when limit is reached it prompts to clear storage or enabling wifi prompts to clear. don't make the mistake i did and exited out of it after deleting one thing because you cannot go back in. i have had these for almost 2 weeks and every day i have had to clear storage at least once and re-enable wifi 2-3 times. after looking through storage it was clear that 8 gb is not enough (well 4.5). they says 4.5 for user storage but i noticed that even some of that still had system related items and the amazon appstore would take up anywhere from 500-1.5gb itself if not careful. my one son had downloaded logo batman (1.4gb~) and a few of their kids book that will read to them (each takes about 100-300mb). there was also a nuance app that was not being used that i could tell that kept re-populating with 50mb. some of the regular apps can take up to 50mb each. these things can add up.

pro:
if you were to use this device solely for watching netflix, amazon videos, anything that streams or reading standard ebooks it is a great device. the pro but not really related to the device but kids free time does allow for allot of parental control. time of day it can be accessed, how long it can be accessed during that time, and they must do certain things first before using it for more entertainment purposes.

summary
so for any device developer to think an 8gb tablet (not including e-readers) should be in the product line needs to think again or more clear upfront of its limitations not all the way down at the bottom in the technical notes which only geeks typically read. for users i honestly cannot see how kindle hd/kids hd 6"/7" 8gb is suitable by anyone unless it is strictly for streaming or reading standard books.

review_headline: managing kids devices via amazon site is great!
review_body:
bought three of these for my children to get them off of my phone and tablet ;-)

very sturdy unit, quick boot time, and good battery life. found a lot of the games the kids love from the ios world.

two main points about these units:

1 - if the storage gets low on the device, it turns off wifi. this seems to happen fairly regularly, but some device management gets around it.
2 - and this is cool. you can manage all these devices off of the amazon website. as i said, i have three of them for the kids. i can login to my account, choose my purchases, and send them to individual fires. if they are lost, login to the site, click on their fire, and send an alarm to the unit. very useful. the administration via the website is great.

additionally, they have free time. this is a paid service where you can configure the content you will allow your children to view. way cool. not sure if i will stick with it for the older kids, but sure helps with the younger ones.

there's also a cloud storage space of source that you will have tied to your account so you can still have your apps or books even if they aren't directly downloaded onto your kindle. then you just uninstall an app from your device and it stays on your cloud to be re downloaded and or installed at a later date.

i also would say go for the ad free version if you want a more personal touch.

review_headline: ... was looking forward to my citron kindle and now enjoy it fully
review_body:
i was looking forward to my citron kindle and now enjoy it fully. i'm only giving this 4 stars as i found setting up the wi-fi to be one of the most frustrating experiences ever with a device. i initially had the wi-fi security set to wpa2/wpa and the wi-fi never worked eventhough the kindle said it was connected. i would have to shut down, power up, and then re-enter the wi-fi. very frustrating as i ordered the fire hd 7 to be more than a vessel for kindlebooks. after googling and reading that others had the same problems, i changed the wi-fi security to wep (annoying that you have to enter a long passcode), but the wi-fi finally stuck and i haven't had issues with the wi-fi since.

the picture quality is good and the speed is fairly decent as well. and it is nicer to read on a larger screen than a phone screen.

amazon should have a fix for the wpa/wpa2 wi-fi problem especially if they know this is an issue.
