review_headline: i would not recommend this device to anyone
review_body:
within 2 days of receiving our fire hd 7, it ran out of storage space. we had not downloaded anything and had only subscribed to the freetime unlimited. i called their support line and spoke to a representative who was extremely helpful. he walked me through the process of reseting it to its factory settings and took a lot of time answering my questions. he called me back 24 hours later to check on the device and it was working properly. he told me that if the problem happened again, they would replace it because it could be a problem with the device. it happened again 2 weeks later, again after no downloads. we still only have the freetime unlimited subscription and the storage space is so critically low, we cannot connect to wifi. we also don't have pictures or videos on the device.i called customer support again and was told to reset to factory settings again. this technician said that low storage problems would not be a valid reason to replace the device because it is not broken and that i was given misinformation the first time i called regarding reasons to replace a device.
i am hopeful that we will work this out one way or the other, but for now, i would not recommend this device to anyone. it should not need to be reset twice within the first few weeks of ownership especially since we haven't downloaded anything!

review_body:
while christmas shopping on amazon, i noticed that the new hd7 fire was only $99 so i decided to upgrade my old hd fire to the newer version. i loved my hd fire and i was eager to play with the new one. however, i was really disappointed with the new one. while i like the interface better than the old one, i find the new one very slow with loading apps and books. copying to the new device is also slow. even while reading a book, sometimes you see a busy cursor when you are trying to change pages.

running the new and old side by side, you can see the noticeably slow new kindle versus the speedy old kindle. i was expecting the reverse. i am not sure how amazon managed to move backwards with product usability but i feel like that is what they accomplished with the newer version. i bought a kids kindle for christmas too and it appears to be the new hd7 fire problem, since that is also slow too.

i am hoping that they can fix this with a software update and that it doesn't require a hardware change to make the improvements.

review_body: i originally purchased this for myself then i decided to gift it to my mother. this it top quality for a 7" and it feels solid. the screen is tough but tends to feels slippery but i'm hoping the screen protector will reduce that. this item is exactly as described by other purchasers and while i knew of the google play issue, i still was not prepared for the severe restrictions amazon has placed on accessing google play versus the amazon apps. amazon apps does have many of the same apps but, if you decided to purchase a google play app, you will not be able to download it on your amazon fire hd even though it is the same app. i could not figure out how to get the device recognized as an android app so that i could download my existing apps but apparently the amazon restrictions for google play prevented it. if you love, love google play then do not get this item. if you downloaded only the free apps then get this item. thankfully, my mother will be using just a few apps but mainly she needed to be able to read her bible and not have to carry around the hefty one she has been with the words getting tinier and tinier. :) the rest of us can use her tablet to view movies from amazon or play other app games with it. it's clear and high res and works very, very well on a wireless connection. for myself, i will not be purchasing another amazon tablet because i really like google play and i have purchased some apps that i want to be able to use and not have to purchase them again. i gave it only 4 stars simply because of the amazon restrictions to downloading google play. i just could not find an easy method to get it to work with this tablet, even with the user guide.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: it's a kindle fire hd... of course it's good
review_body:
my girlfriend's mother wanted to give one to two of her grandsons (ages 16 and 6) to share - good luck with that one!! haha. but seriously, the 6-year-old already has a nabi to play with, so the 16-year-old will be the one using this most of the time. it's a kindle hd... what more is there to say? my mom got the same one, but an older version, from me for christmas last year and this seems like more of the same. graphics are great, picture is clear, and this supposedly has faster wi-fi speeds than the old one, but i don't know how noticeable it is, as my mother has no complaints with her older kindle. a great, simple interface that is responsive and easy to use. i'm not sure about the sound quality or anything on it, as i didn't get to see it used much, but i'm sure it's similar to other tablets/phones - unless you're an audiophile, i'm sure it'll be sufficient - headphones are also always an option.
personally, i'm a fan of a pure android experience, but being tied into the amazon ui and marketplace isn't all bad. if you've got a prime account, this is perfect because of the amazon prime instant video, music, etc., along with easy shopping and free 2-day shipping.

this is starting to sound like an advertisement for amazon, but seriously, it's a good tablet that will handle almost any task. i'm a little concerned about only having 16gb of storage, but i wasn't about to talk my girlfriend's mom into handing over so much more money for another 16gb of space - her grandson will just have to learn how to conserve memory the best that he can. i guess that'll be the "struggle" for his generation, as opposed to the "trying to find privacy when talking on a corded phone that was anchored to the wall in the kitchen", or "hoping no one picked up the phone while you were online so that you didn't get kicked off and have to listen to that stupid dial-up sound again" that my generation had. :)

review_body:
i've never had a device like this before, so i figured i'd start with the kindle, since my mother uses one and loves it quite a bit. i didn't really know what to really look out for when it came to these devices, but i primarily wanted to use it to read books and occasionally watch videos on, and for both of those purposes, the device works absolutely wonderfully. if that's all you want from a tablet, then go for this, since it's a fairly cheap device, and it works quickly, i never had to wait for it to load anything.

however, there are a few downsides that really bring down the overall product rating for me. personally, i love to customize my computer and phone - i like to use my own wallpapers, sound effects, and so on, and astonishingly the kindle doesn't allow any sort of customization whatsoever. i thought using your own wallpaper was a pretty standard thing in the industry, so imagine my surprise when i upload the pictures i want to use as my wallpaper and i'm incapable of using them in that way. it's only after i went online to try and figure out where the options were that i learned that it wasn't possible. it's not only wallpapers though, the fact that i can't customize the main menu in any way, and i can'r choose which tabs i want available at the top are all little things that i like to do to personalize the product, and i just can'r understand why even the most basic form of customization is unavailable for use.

my second issue is with the ads. in addition to being unable to customize the wallpapers, occasionally an ad will show up instead. if i want to remove this, it costs fifteen dollars. i find this to be a deplorable practice, since i wasn't given any options to buy a model that didn't come with ads in the first place, so in addition to the 150~ i paid for the kindle, i ended up paying an additional 15 dollars just to remove the annoying ads. granted, they don't interfere when you're reading (otherwise i would be marking this at one star), but i just hate how the device had an entire section of it exclusive to ads.

the final thing i'm disappointed about is that there no way to use an sd card to add more space. if you want more space for these, you either have to buy a model that contains more, or buy a wireless usb card that can hold the data, which aren't cheap. it makes no sense not to have something that - again - i thought was standard for most devices nowadays. the only reason i can think of as to why they don't include it is greed, since i suppose without sd card support, some people may be more inclined to pay more for a version with more internal memory.

overall, for a first tablet, it works fine, but from now on, i'll be sure to really put forth an attempt at actual research into these things when i want to buy a new one. a lot of things i had assumed to be standard are apparently not, and i can say with certainty that - while the kindle works fine and does its intended purposes well enough - i will not being buying another kindle in the future due to the drawbacks listed above.

review_headline: excellent device but has a freezing issue.
review_body:
i received the fire as a christmas present and was impressed by the simplicity of start up out of the box. it is truly like they advertise. the device was 75% charged out of the box and walked me through set up in a mere few minutes. i was reading a book within 15 minutes. i connected to all my stuff in my cloud storage effortlessly. and being an amazon prime member, i am impressed by the ease of watching videos as well.
the only problem i am having is after 10 days of using the device it has started freezing and would not turn on this morning. finding support for the device was a little tricky on the amazon website. i finally resorted to try to return the device since i could not get it to turn on and only then was directed to an area that gave me support on the device. i learned that if the device froze up, that i should hold down the power button for 20 seconds (it takes the full 20 seconds). i tried this and it worked!! unfortunately i have had to do this several times already. not sure if this is a wide-spread problem with this device or if it is just mine. if this problem continues, i would definitely try a replacement as i absolutely love the fire hd. the only reason i gave it 4 stars instead of 5 is because of the freezing issue. i would definitely recommend this product.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body: i received this as a gift.  i'm glad to have it but i'm disappointed that you can't customize it.  you can't set a background/wallpaper - which really bothers me.  you can't set a lock screen wallpaper.  you can't organize tabs/icons.  you can't even set what comes up on the carousel for everyone who picks it up to see (you can delete items, if you think of it, but not say just don't show \\"x\\").  you are limited to kindle; no google play.  you can't set an adult guest profile & are only allowed two adult log ins - both parties needing to have amazon log ins.  (why only two!?)  the battery life is disappointing & not intuitive to extend.  it really has terrible glare in daylight (nearly unusable) - much worse than my smartphone & it shows finger prints the second you touch it. basically, i think i would be happier with an android tablet.    it's also so new that the selection of cases is very limited & apparently the front camera is new so many old edition cases say they won't work & most screen protectors look like they'd cover the front camera.    still, despite the frustrations, i'm happy to have it & enjoy the apps i do have on it.  i appreciate the large viewing area for the e-reader functions.  i'm relieved that it defaults to a finger-swipe keyboard.  i love reading kindle books & local pubic library books on it (indoors).  it's a good size for watching netflix with subtitles (indoors).  i like the short cut to the amazon wish list. the built in child lock app seems decent & the built in parental controls are nicely customizable. the ads don't bother me - i get that that is why it was cheaper & they aren't that intrusive.  plus, i've read i can get rid of them for $20 if i'm so inclined which is nice to know.    all in all, i like it; i'm having fun with it.  for the price it's great, but i'm not planning to get another kindle when the time comes to replace it.    update: on the plus side: keeping the kindle in airplane mode & the brightness turned low really extends the battery life.  on the downside, the built-in kids lock app requires active wi-fi.  also, while i found a case i like, i'm still having trouble finding screen protectors that accommodate the new front facing camera.

review_headline: great product, but still prefer others.
review_body:
this product suits me fine. i've been an apple user for a long time and like the diversity the ipad has always had. the kindle fire hd7 isn't as versatile as i'd expected. nonetheless, it is great for kids and for shopping easily on amazon.

the only 3 negative things i discovered were the ad removals having to be $15 (which i understand), the lack of support for a lot of great apps, (youtube for one) and the inability to store pdf e-books in my "books" folder, rather than them be in the "docs" folder.

three things i love are the sound! has a very audible range from somewhere in the low 40hz to a good range in the 12-15khz, which blows my mind. the other being able to shop easily on amazon! who doesn't love that. last is the size and build of this thing, which is great for kids to watch netflix and some apps.

review_headline: reliable and easy to use, even better if you have prime.
review_body:
received this as a gift for christmas, and am very happy with it. the device is fast to respond and makes it easy to find things, once you get used to using the home screen. i have owned 1 tablet before this one, which was plagued with problems. the fire has had none of these, and so far has never run slow and has crashed only once since i've had it. the cameras are good too.

personally i find the ability to manage your music through amazon convenient, as you don't need a cable just to add some music from your computer, and you can have more space by keeping your music in the cloud. prime music stations are a nice alternative to pandora.

the only things missing from the device are an sd card slot and mini-hdmi output. an sd card isn't a big deal since you can use the cloud, and mini-hdmi is a rare feature anyway.

as long as you want to use cloud storage or streaming, this is a great device for it. amazon prime gives you unlimited videos and music to watch, and borrow 1 book a month; while kindle unlimited lends you 10 free books at a time for a monthly charge. together they would be pricey at $200 a year.

i personally use sugarsync to share files besides music easily, and plan to use kindle unlimited, but prime on top of that is a bit much.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
even though i'm giving this product 5 stars, i still found a couple of things worth mentioning. overall, it's great. fast touch response on the screen, easily connects to wi-fi at a new location, fairly decent battery life (depending on amount of usage), takes nice photos (not photographer quality, but still good), and keeps an 11 year from constantly bickering with her sister. i have not connected to any social networks or email addresses with this, so i cannot comment on those at this time.

the only downfalls i have experienced with this are: sometimes (not every time) it will freeze up after taking a picture, the built in microphone isn't very sensitive (have to speak a bit louder than normal), and the included charging cable isn't very long (2ft long, maybe).

other than that, a great, solid tablet that fits the needs of an 11 year old girl (mostly gaming, pictures, and reading), and capable of doing more if i ever ask it to.

review_body: i originally had a kindle fire hd (2013) running fire os 3 and then it upgraded to os 4. then i got this thing as a christmas gift. i used it mire than my old one but for $150 at the time, i'd say it worth less. originally, you were stuck with their ugly home screen where you spin the carousel to find an app. you were also stuck with their app store, which is far more worse than windows store. the camera quality is 2mp but it could do better. the front facing camera has more quality than the rear. i got 16gb since my last has 8 but amazon has lots of bloatware. even with 16gb, i had like 10 left.   when the tablet updated to fire os 5, i was happy the carousel was gone but the nee home screen has double the ads then it did before. you can't side load another home screen since the default launcher would reject it. you'd have to root the thing to disable the fire launcher, which voids warranty. the one good thing was having google play and services without root. i also liked how they tried to stick to android looks by having the original back, home and recent button. i'm glad they added the recent apps though to clear out some ram. over all, for those who like android, just get an android tablet.

review_body:
i recieved this (kindle fire hd 7, gen. 4) as a gift, and have been very pleased with it so far. it works well and is well designed. i was pleased to find that there is now a way to make book collections built into the device, that was a common complaint i saw about the previous generations of kindle fires. i've download a few different games and songs, and been pleased with the speed things load at, and the quality of the sound and graphics.
the settings are well categorized so it is easy to pick and choose what you do or don't want your device to do. the only thing i really had to look up to figure out how to turn off was the 'popular highlights' in books. everything else was pretty straight forward.
the battery seems to drain quicker than i expected sometimes, but i think that has to do with whether i'm playing a complex, energy hungry game or just reading a book.
all in all, i am quite happy with it.

review_body:
i'm pretty disappointed in this tablet. i received this as a christmas gift and was pretty excited to have a tablet of my own (i have an iphone that my kids have pretty much taken control over lol!). what a disappointment it turned out to be :( the screen is nice and clear and colorful. it is easy to use. i was able to watch shows on it very nicely using the "shop amazon" app. but sadly, that is all the positive i can say about it. the camera is horrible. the audio is fair. my first complaint was that the app selection was really lame. coming from apple, i was disappointed to see that many of my favorite apps/games were not available for the fire. next disappointment was that the apps that were available on both apple and amazon were double the price than they are on apple. the biggest disappointment of all, no memory. i received the 8gb and within 5 days, my memory is completely full. i downloaded facebook, messenger, netflix, pandora, and about 4-5 games (low end games that don't eat up memory) for myself and kids. since none of the games i enjoy are available in the amazon appstore, i was going to pass this down to my kids. i then made the mistaken of signing up for the free trial of amazon freetime (a service for kids that allows unlimited access to all children's apps for one flat monthly fee) and downloaded 3, three games there. i then got the message that my memory was full. i was shocked. i have about 8 games on this thing and the memory is already full? i have no pictures, no video, no music on it and cannot add any because the memory is gone. when i checked to see what was eating up all the memory (since i hardly downloaded anything!), i was shocked to see that about 40% of the memory was already used by the system's own applications. things that i cannot delete or else the tablet will not work properly. i deleted facebook messenger, and canceled all the games i was trying to download for my kids via the freetime (which is completely worthless if your fire tablet has no memory to support it!). another problem i'm having is that there is no password required to download games from freetime, so my kids are constantly trying to download games and there is no room for them on the fire. so it's jamming up everything. i'm not able to run apps smoothly because they are constantly locking up and freezing. i'm assuming it's because there isn't enough memory to run them and the downloading is interrupting as well. i have to keep switching to their profile and cancel all the downloads, which is frustrating because sometimes even when you try to cancel the downloads, it doesn't work. i'm going to have to remove freetime completely which will be disappointing for my daughter.

so bottom line, i would recommend spending a little bit more and getting an apple. much more selection from the appstore, cheaper apps, and much more memory. what's the point of having a tablet or device if you can't do much on it? i'm not sure what to do with this now. i guess i can use it to check facebook and do the occasional internet shopping. it's useless for my kids, so i can't give it to them. again, i'm really disappointed. amazon could do better than this.our fire tablet has no memory to support it!). another problem i'm having is that there is no password required to download games from freetime, so my kids are constantly trying to download games and there is no room for them on the fire. so it's jamming up everything. i'm not able to run apps smoothly because they are constantly locking up and freezing. i'm assuming it's because there isn't enough memory to run them and the downloading is interrupting as well. i have to keep switching to their profile and cancel all the downloads, which is frustrating because sometimes even when you try to cancel the downloads, it doesn't work. i'm going to have to remove freetime completely which will be disappointing for my daughter.

so bottom line, i would recommend spending a little bit more and getting an apple. much more selection from the appstore, cheaper apps, and much more memory. what's the point of having a tablet or device if you can't do much on it? i'm not sure what to do with this now. i guess i can use it to check facebook and do the occasional internet shopping. it's useless for my kids, so i can't give it to them. again, i'm really disappointed. amazon could do better than this.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
i bought 2 of these for my children, ages 10 & 8, thinking the freetime would be good. i'm not so impressed.

the physical kindle hd 7: the actual kindle i love for them. it's just the right size and it's just right for them. i have the kindle hdx 7" and i love it (except they have one more camera than i do. boo! lol) so i knew they would love theirs. and they do. they even received a $15 amazon gift card each from my brother to buy books and apps. they were so excited.

kindle freetime: i hate it. it works, don't get me wrong, but there is no way around some things. for example, my 8 yr old found the "escape the titanic" game. it's just a bunch of puzzles you have to figure out to escape the different levels. well, it was free so i downloaded it for him. he got through the first few puzzles really fast, but to continue you had to buy it. well, any app purchases in freetime are restricted. ok, i can see why. i don't want them buying things all willy nilly anyway. so i went in, purchased the game thinking he could play it. nope! ***all in app purchases are blocked in freetime.*** there is no way around this. i found this out after 2 calls and almost an hour later with kindle support. however, if an app originally cost $, but it's free in the app store, it counts as the full version and they can play the whole thing. a lot of free games aren't the full version. but this also applies to games like candy crush or whatever. they can play the whole game, but no in app purchases.

now, kindles have parental controls. but, in order to use pc's they have to have their own amazon account? i'm still confused on this, because the pc's don't override ft. there are 2 different types of child profiles in ft. one for 8 an under and one for 9 and older. so when my kid is 16 she still wouldn't be able to do any in app purchases even if i give her permission if she is still under a ft profile. but then what's the point of pc's? also, i've beenhaving trouble getting the reading/educational goals to work on their ft profiles, so i have to hover over them anyway.

overall i love the kindle fire tablets. the hd7s were just right for the kids and i love my hdx. i'm on it all the time. i do, however, think that kindle freetime and the parental controls need to be rethought. i love that i can control their content and screen time, but i figured i'd have a little more say in everything else too. even the guy i talked to at the app store support agreed with me. if i want him to be able to make an in app purchase, i should be able to do that through freetime. i certainly wouldn't buy anything in an app they are playing. and if you do and they use all your power ups or whatever, then you're stupid.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: the picture and sound are great. it's fast
review_body: got it for our teenage son for christmas.  wasn't sure he'd be thrilled since his school loans ipads to every student during the school year and he's always on it, but he loves this kindle. he's thanked us several times for getting it.  the picture and sound are great. it's fast!  he likes the size of it when he's hunkered down in his favorite chair.  he found several free apps that were must haves. i don't feel so guilty borrowing his paperwhite all the time now. i also have my own basic kindle e-reader with page turn buttons and sometimes i really prefer it to a touch screen when i don't need the extra light.  amazon doesn't go into the advantages of owning more than one kindle, but there are some.  you can share books, purchased or on loan, on kindles registered to the same account.  this means if the battery runs out, you can keep reading on your other kindle if you won't be near an outlet.  or you can use one kindle to hold onto a library e-book (if you can't renew it) until you're done with it as long as you don't exit the book. (i usually just need an extra day. i try to be considerate about getting books back for others who are waiting for it.)  if you misplace one (i truly need a brighter case), you have a backup until you find it.  you and another person can read the same book independently while you have it on loan. we get e-books from our library a lot and there is high demand for the popular titles.  as a devoted kindle fan, i'd say you can't go wrong with any of the kindles.  just know what you want to do with it and go from there.  of course, i'd like a fire tablet of my own, but i know this guy who loans me things...

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
pros.... good speed...good operating system, good resolution. battery lasts longer than my older kindle, especially if you turn the brightness down halfway. like the camera and all the little bells and whistles that you find as you use it. has some sorta of new streaming technology for vids and such. great for books and video watching.

cons.... * gigs doesn't men 8 gigs of usable memory. you only get 5 or so gigs of usable memory. the other three is supposedly taken up by the operating system and included apps and such. the camera isn't a great one. good enough to not jerk and such when recording so you basically get a decent frame rate. only records in maybe 480p. unless you get a special case for it you will not be able to use the rear camera while it is in a cover. power button and charge port are up on the top right corner where they either get covered up or rendered unable to be used/charged unless you remove that corner of the cover. no light on the power button that lets you see when the battery is charged without turning on the kindle and looking.

over all and good tablet for someone needing something to read on or someone wanting a tablet for watching vids on or play light games or use as a pda. i haven't tried office programs on it and maybe never will. if you want a tablet for these things but don't want to shell out hundreds of dollars for the apple one i would say get it.

review_body:
first things first: i only got this as a deal-sweetener being paired with the rosetta stone pack.

this device is meant strictly for those who want to consume amazon's media. the games were slow compared to other android-based devices. however, the content works swell.

for those of you who want to enjoy your amazon prime membership, this is your tablet. for those of you who want a functional tablet, try google, samsung, or apple.

pros:
widescreen format
100% compatibility with all things amazon (obviously)
shared profiles

cons:
poor standby battery life (compared to other well-known tablets)
a little on the heavy side
low storage capacity makes it difficult to use as a main device

review_headline: new kindle fire hd not compatible with apps
review_body:
we purchased a kindle fire hd a couple years ago, which is no longer functional, so we replaced it with the latest version, which appeared to be fundamentally the same device. our granddaughter (3 years old) loved a lot of the apps that we had downloaded for the original kindle, so we were trying to load the same apps on the new kindle.

much to our dismay, we find that the new kindle fire hd 7 is not compatible with a number of the apps that we had on the original version. this would seem to be bad execution for the new device, to make it so that the replacement of a very similar device would not be backwards compatible with existing software.

if we had known about this shortcoming, we would probably have searched around for the older model instead of upgrading!

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
after using a "generic" tablet for 2 years i finally looked at all the name brand tablets offered. my main use of the tablet would be for reading. i am a big amazon shopper and being disabled i cannot tell you how many times they offer items that i would have to drive an hour to pick up or order from somewhere else - with no shipping ratings to know what they are like - or the cost of shipping is crazy (i am a prime customer), so the kindle already had a head start in my shopping..
back to the tablet. wow - what a difference! the new fire hd exceeded my expectations! it is so fast. the clarity of the screen is amazing. i love this tablet! of course being on a fixed income i picked it up when they were running a fabulous sale - same price as what i paid for the generic tablet a couple of years ago! were i independently wealthy i would have chosen the larger fire hdx - but i can say i am so pleased with the fire hd 7 i cannot complain. i see complaints about no sd card but to me the storage is more than enough! it has the capacity to store up to 6000 books and if that is not enough for you then you need to go to the bigger tablet. i do not sync and store any pics or my main email account on the tablet, so i do not have all that filling up my tablet - my phone has a huge sd card, plus the cloud, plus my desktop - no need to use the tablet for those reasons. i am amazed how smoothly i can bookmark a page i am reading and hit home and go to silk to look up something online. because of the ease of the internet from my fire i just had to zap over 800 emails as i have not been to my desktop in a couple weeks!
being a prime customer i can say the choices of movies and shows amazes me. so much so i am squirreling away a fund for the fire tv to take advantage of the freebies on a large screen tv.
i am glad i waited for the new release/version and got it at such a bargain price during the holidays. i was still on the fence with the ebook vs. a "real" book in my hands until i got my fire. now i am so comfortable with the tablet (and of coarse the free and nearly free reads from kindle) it no longer bothers me. i still believe in the printed book but when you are on a fixed income even goodwill and the like are more expensive than a kindle bargain!
if you are in the same situation i was and can get the kindle - do it!
and to give yourself a warm fuzzy feeling zap your old tablet back to factory settings and give it to someone who can't afford even a generic tablet that loves to read. i by chance ran into such a person and had someone else give it to them. you will have given that person who loves to read a chance to read all the free ebooks available.
one happy kindle fire owner here - it's possibilities are endless!
and - i love the fact that when i am reading a series i can see from my amazon account when and which novel in the series i last read. you do not get that option with some of the other tablets, another big point with me as i do read so much you can forget which book you last read. will not happen with your kindle.
if i sound over the moon i am - it truly exceeded my expectations.

review_body:
since i have a kindle paperwhite i thought this would be a good addition, and the price was reduced for the holidays. after about a month of using it i could say it's "okay". i have a "hand-me-down" ipad mini and i find it a better system, for me.

the reasons i think the fire is just okay is its low battery life and weight compared to the ipad mini. i would play a game on the fire for about 15 minutes at 98% battery life and after the 15 minutes the battery life would be at 80%. i would do the same on the ipad mini and the battery life is still around 90%. i also tried out the audio books. i would have it play for about 6 hours and on the fire the battery percentage went down around 15%; whereas for the same time and book on the ipad mini it only went down 5%.

and for the weight, the fire is about 1lb. 1oz. (17oz.) and the ipad mini is 13oz. i know that doesn't sound like much of a difference but when you're holding it up for awhile it slowly does make a difference. and surprisingly you can feel the difference when you pick them up.

overall it's a decent tablet for the price.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: love love love it!! why did i wait so long??
review_body:
this is my first \\"e-book\\" and i love it. it's so much more than just a reader, with all the apps that are available you can do so much with it. there are 2 things that i don't like about it, one, it takes forever to charge. i can burn up the battery in about 2 hours if i'm playing games, if i'm just reading it lasts much longer. the only other thing is that, because it's so much more than just a reader, i wish we had the ability to set a wallpaper, it seems like a trivial thing, but the black (or you can choose it to be white) background is so drab. since it has an excellent camera it would be nice to take a pic and set it as my wallpaper. perhaps in the future.
the screen and video are amazing, even with a matte finish screen protector on the images and video are bright, clear, sharp and vivid!!! sound quality is good, i have not used headphones yet so i can't vouch for the quality of sound coming from the jack.
there is a clock app on here that let's you set an alarm, if you have any issues with hearing, forget it, i literally could not hear 1/2 the tones at all and that was with the volume all the way up. they are simply to high pitched, i think only my neighbors dog could hear them!! the ones i could hear were barely audible. so when i travel i guess i will continue to use my phone as my travel alarm, but i wasn't buying an alarm clock so it doesn't really matter, just thought i'd mention it.
one last thing, i saw that some people complained about the camera, and i wonder if they are using the wrong one. there are 2 cameras on this, one on the front and one on the back. the one on the back is for taking pictures and is much better quality. the one on the front is for video calls like when using skype, so the image quality is lower so that it streams live faster!!. so if you want to take a selfie while looking at yourself, you're gonna have to go in the bathroom like everyone else!! lol but just like the alarm clock thing, you didn't buy a camera did you?
all in all tho i'm really happy with it, i thought i wasn't going to like it because i love real books so much, but this is so much easier to hold and i don't have to mess with being perfectly situated under a reading light or fumble with a book light, i can read in the dark if i want. i can change the font size and so much more!!in all tho i'm really happy with it, i thought i wasn't going to like it because i love real books so much, but this is so much easier to hold and i don't have to mess with being perfectly situated under a reading light or fumble with a book light, i can read in the dark if i want. i can change the font size and so much more!!

review_body: i'm so disappointed with this fire hd  7.  the one major selling point was the parental controls that sounded too good to be true and absolutely was to good to be true.  i registered the devices and was adding child teen accounts to both (i purchased two for my kids), adding in the time limits for reading, gaming watching videos etc... and when done i realized once i had logged into the child's account the there was absolutely nothing on the screen it was blank no content what so ever.  i expected to see the basic tablet apps such as calculators, maps, timers and calendars etc. i didn't see anything.  i wanted to hand over to my kids as a present a working tablet of their own to use.  i have a nexus 10 that i've been sharing with them which has child accounts but lacks the activity time limits and was looking forward to them having there own device.    i researched for 2-3 hours how to set up kids accounts and i opened up everything that i could via parental controls all the while thinking how could this been so hard and surely i'm doing something wrong but alas nothing worked and was forced to create adult accounts them.  so disappointed!    the child teen accounts are so limiting in that it's all or nothing... i wanted and thought i'd be getting a working tablet that i could set video, gaming and application limits but still have all the power of a tablet.

review_headline: it's very easy to get dust under the film
review_body:
my first tablet.....
i purchased two fire hd 7" for my wife and i as christmas gifts to each other. the fire tablet has performed exceptionally so far, and has exceeded my expectations.
i researched and read user comments for quite some time before i purchased these two tablets, so i believe i had my eyes wide open as to what i was buying.
i purchased the "without ads" version and opted for the 16gb model, i also bought the screen protectors for both. installing the screen protector needs to be done with care, it's very easy to get dust under the film.
i use mine mainly for reading books and am very impressed with the speed of the download for the books i've bought, if you blink, it's already downloaded...all the books that i've purchased with my fire have automatically synced to my wifes fire too!
my wife watched some weather vids from the weather chanel and the quality and speed is amazing.
there are more available apps than i'll ever need or use and seems to be more all the time, shopping for books and buying them is so easy that i'll have to control my urge to overdo it....
i'm 54yrs old and can say that finding my way around the fire has been easy and i've found instructional vids on the amazon site and there's a help button on the fire if needed.
amazon has built a great product and made using the tablet very easy, i'd highly recommend this product to anyone and especially to a fellow baby-boomer like me!

review_headline: kindle fire has less prime shopping and video functionality than other tablets
review_body:
totally bummed out with my first amazon tablet experience! the incredible irony is to get the functionality i want, i need to buy a 3rd party tablet with amazon apps (ipad, or android) and won't be able to use amazon's own ecosystem. i was very excited to test out my fist kindle fire, i spend a lot with amazon prime both personally and at the office and was concerned this could make things too easy. it won't. surely i'll never get into the vine program now... but i've got to be honest and vent my frustrations with this amazon fire tablet i bought my wife for christmas.

hear me out; my beef comes down to essentially this - my wife cannot use her own "private" amazon account to shop and gift privately with her credit cards etc and also watch the baked-in prime instant video or listen to music from my household account... because i am the primary account holder sharing my $99 a year prime with her... which only gets you the 2-day shipping.

to use this kindle fires video and music capabilities, and enjoy a private shopping/ gifting experience, it forces us into a position where we pay another $99 a year for another primary "prime user" for her. it's too bad the solution is two apps via ipad, phones, other android devices - one for shopping, one for video - all because there is no other ways to configure the fire os.

one star for the hassle of configuring then returning the fire tablet just to go back to using two+ amazon apps on a device made by someone else. (don't worry amazon, you'll get that sale too) it's a bummer the house branded fire tablet has to go back, the thing even has an option for two adult profiles, but it seems no consideration has gone into private shopping or gifting and this very issue. i know they'd love another $99 a year subscriber, but no thanks we're a household and that doesn't seem fair. a different tablet with two apps it is.

review_headline: terrible nonworking junk. truly awful refund policy.
review_body:
warning: terrible replacement policy.
i have purchased many kindle products before including previous generations of kindle fire and hd.

this unit rates zero stars. amazon's policies rate minus-5.

my wife bought me the the latest kindle 7 hd as a xmas present.

out of the box it failed to connect to 3 of my wifi routers. i spent a long time with tech support on xmas only to end up with amazon sending a replacement. later in the day it did connect intermittently to our 4th router that i hadn't tried earlier. but problems persisted: no email setups worked, etc.

the replacement arrived four days later. it had other problems.
1. it would not setup without creating a fake child to get past the freetime setup screen.
2. it rebooted every hour or two as a new unit, taking about 25 minutes to do a full setup and to reload from backup (about 15 minutes of that time with a 30 mb/s very strong wifi signal).
3. impossible to set up any emails.
never got past this stage.

more calls to amazon. no solutions other than the fake kid hack again.

the nice lady (3rd techie) told me i could either get a refund or a replacement. i asked if i could try it for another day to make up my mind. she cheerily approved my suggestion.

another hour had been wasted, but hopes were high.

in the next 5 hours there were several more problems and 3 crash/reboots.

i called amazon again after 9:00 pm. the second person, andy, then advised that amazon's policy only allows a replacement for a new unit, not for a replacement. my replacement was just in the process of being ser up when it couldn't get past the freetime screen at all. i told him about my conversation a few hours ago.

after being on hold a long time while he supposedly spoke with supervisors, he said that amazon would make a one-time exception to its policy and allow a refund. i asked him again if he was seriousinasmuch as the first unit never worked even for even a minute and the replacement would not even set up properly without crashing. he confirmed amazon's policy and my one-time exception.

that is shameful and disgusting.

he also confirmed that these units are full of problems.

beware of problems with these units. they are a waste of money and time.

more importantly, beware of amazon's refund policies when you buy amazon kindle junk.

you could spend weeks getting endless replacements and live in total frustration with constant spontaneous crashes, reboots, and 25 minute waits for backups to download only to find that if you get a replacement, you will be screwed when that piece of junk fails.

i was told that the long download times related to my extensive book collection. surprise: isn't that what kindles are for?

i will find a samsung galaxy pro iii 12.2 tomorrow (not thru amazon) and never waste another moment with kindle products.

review_headline: just a bulky tablet with ereader tendencies and no customization options.
review_body:
i wanted this to read on. nothing more. i have no intention of it being my go-to tablet, using the apps, watching tv...none of it.

i'm a book blogger who needs it to review egalleys and read her books. having the fire hd7 would fix many of the issues i had with my recently retired kobo aura, but sadly what i have found since using this, is that it's a jump back in time. the core might be faster, but it's heavy, bulky and thick! and it's not an ereader any more, it's a tablet posing as one trying to make everything but actual books the forefront of it's abilities.

- you can't make your books, or the bookstore the main focus of your reader unless you manually add the books to the home screen, one by one. this is supposed to be an ereader...right?

- the carousel is annoying, removing something from it is a 4 step process. still unsure if what's in it is just a reminder of what i have looked at lately or what's currently running in the background. if the latter, the fact it's so frustratingly complicated to remove things from, it is even worse.

- you can not customize it at all, which i find in 2014 on an item i paid $140 for to be just ludicrous. as best i can tell, it doesn't even come with background options to change it too that are amazon approved. why can't i have a picture of my kids at disney as my background amazon? why?

you can see my full review here: http://www.memyshelfandi.com/2014/12/product-review-kindle-fire-hd7so-far-so.html

basically, spend the additional $100 and get an ipad mini. all the same features, but lighter, sleeker, better camera and the ability to customize. it has the kindle app which is the same as the kindle itself...this being the newest item from kindle should have been the best and the brightest and instead i get something that can't do half of what my 1st generation nook color could when i got it in 2010. disappointing to say the very least.

review_headline: not a fan of kindle fire hd - 2 years into ownership
review_body:
the good news is that the kindle fire hd is a relatively cheap tablet and reader. it has clear graphics.

the bad news is that it locks you into amazon. you cannot use google play. the available apps are limited and often do not work as well as android apps available on google play. the kindle fire hd will also not work with free books sites. amazon uses this platform as a slave to its content.

review_headline: i used to love my kindle but decided to finally chuck amazon's kindle ...
review_body:
i can only give kindles 1 star. : i used to love my kindle but decided to finally chuck amazon's kindle products.
the fire hd 7 was my second kindle fire 7. both were problematic with the fire hd 7 being a bomb due to an amazon update. i bought the fire 7 hd 16gb (model h with the micro hdmi "out" located next to the power input) in late 2013. it had a few problems right from the start, (insertion of letters or numbers from opposite sides of the keyboard from where you tapped, etc.) which i reported to amazon. then both amazon and gmail did an update in february which became incompatible..ie. i could no longer delete email and the kindle contents could no longer be seen by my xp console. thus, i couldn't remove downloaded docs or pix or music from the kindle hd. amazon blogs showed that many other owners were having similar problems. i reported to amazon, and then followed a nightmare of hours & hours of tech phone help and 3 refurbished replacements. they told me they were sending new ones but they didn't. the problems were never solved which were caused by the update. it cost a lot of money to buy new. it only worked somewhat well for 6 months. they would not credit my hd 16gb towards purchase of a newer model (like the newer 7) where hopefully these problems didn't exist. so, although kindles are cheaper than ipad mini, kindles are not worth the costs cuz amazon doesn't fully stand by their products. i don't know if the newer models work better or if they've changed their service policies. but i can only give them one star now.

review_body:
this was a purchase to replace my failing kindle keyboard . no e-ink readers were now available with audio or tts. i made the purchase with reluctance, fearing the back lit screen would be hard on sensitive , failing eyes . surprise, because of the ability to select other screen backgrounds and brightness, this has not been a problem. as with other kindle devices , you can change the font sizes, and now i can also change the letter style. the text to speech is greatly improved in sound as well as voice selection. i have lots of audio books,and the fire has great sound, making listening a real pleasure. so far all the other features i have tried work well, but there is a lot of new ( to me) stuff to learn. having a bunch of techie smart grandchildren helps a lot.
one caution and, the only reason for 4 stars, is that mirroring,flinging to your tv and fire tv streaming device does not work on the fire hd 7. i thought i had researched this with care, and this fact is stated on the product information page, in a location that is easily missed, if you don't click on every further information box as you scroll down. if you need this feature, you will need a hdx model. my bad for not catching this, but it could have been made much clearer. i plan to sell this one and upgrade to an hdx model. overall, i love it.

review_body: while it serves my needs, i'm quite disappointed with my fire.  after seeing my friend's ipod, i decided to try the kindle fire because of price.  i have had had a kindle reader for several years and loved it.  although i do enjoy reading books on the kindle fire, i find that the battery life is no where near the 8 hours they say it has.  more like 4 or maybe 5.  the worse thing about it is i must reboot it daily and sometimes more than once a day due to it freezing or at best slowing down.  i get kicked off the web for no reason as sometimes it just blacks out.  i've returned 3 previous fires thinking it was a defect in the ones i bought.  the first was a factory refurbish and the second was new which i had the same problem with.  i returned that for a better model and still have the same problem.  in conclusion, for the money, it's a good product.  sometimes it's frustrating when it locks, but when i reboot it, it works perfectly.  i play some card games and mah jong (which i'm addicted to) and it works fine for a while. i've spoken with customer service and they're very helpful and sympathetic but can't seem to solve the problem.  so i'm resigned to the fact it's a fault with the product.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: overall, a good tablet; pleased with this purchase.
review_body:
i purchased this fire tablet to replace my 1st-generation google nexus 7 tablet, which had gradually slowed down and gotten so balky that i couldn't use it. i was leery of replacing the nexus with another nexus so decided to go with the fire tablet instead.
overall i'm quite happy with this tablet. my only basis of comparison is with my old nexus so i'll just make a few comments comparing these two:
size: the fire tablet feels bulkier and less streamlined than the nexus tablet, although not really particularly heavier. i wish it had more rounded corners.
screen: clear and crisp; one of the problems i had with the nexus tablet was that the screen became "washed out" around the edges and also started randomly dimming and brightening while in use. so far i haven't experienced anything like this with the fire.
performance: generally very good. watching videos on the fire tablet has been a smoother experience than with the nexus. i haven't had the constant freezing-up that i was getting with the nexus. my one issue has been that when i click on a link from within, say, facebook or twitter, i get taken to a blank page in the silk browser instead of to the link. if i exit silk and go back to the source and re-try, it usually works fine. no idea why this happens but it is a bit annoying.
i was a little leery about the silk browser being the default, with bing as the search engine, rather than chrome/google, but it's actually working very well. no complaints there.
i also really like the "reading view" feature in silk, which formats web pages to make them clearer and easier to read. it doesn't seem to be available for every single web page, but for the ones where i can use it, i always do.
apps: the only one i was using on the nexus 7 that i can't use here is instagram. that is somewhat annoying but not the end of the world. facebook & twitter work well.
downloads: i've tried downloading a few documents and it's workedquickly and well.
this isn't a particularly elegant-looking tablet and is a little awkward to hold compared to the nexus 7, but so far it seems to be beating the nexus on performance. i'm happy with my purchase.

review_headline: just ok as a tablet. no google play store.  freetime sucks for kids over 5-6.  i wish now that i had bought something else.
review_body:
i have mixed feelings about the kindle fire. first it is nice to be able to set separate profiles on it for my kids, myself, and my husband. it is fairly lightweight and seems sturdy. i bought it for my boys who are 5 and 9, so it's important for it to be sturdy. i have a few issues though. also, since i don't think there's a way to rate amazon freetime, i'm going to include that here also.

kindle issues so far:
internet is not very fast. my samsung galaxy iii phone has way less memory, is smaller, and is ridiculously faster than this. i expected better. it's not impossibly slow, but there's a large delay where my galaxy has none.

google play store and kindle fire are not compatible. there are tons (like thousands) of apps that amazon does not have that are available on google play and i can't access them. that bites. it's actually nearly a dealbreaker. i don't think i'll buy another kindle unless this is resolved. i would have done better buying a different tablet with android. the reason i went with the fire though is because we have amazon prime and kindle unlimited, and freetime sounded like a good idea to keep my kids from accessing things they shouldn't. i thought freetime would be more compatible with prime and unlimited.

so now here are my problems with freetime - there are a lot. i would rate it a 1 if i could rate it:
on my profile or my husbands kindle profile, amazon prime and kindle unlimited probably work fine (i haven't actually tried to read a book or watch a movie yet on the fires, but i don't anticipate a problem), however, i bought these for my kids and set them up with freetime. amazon prime and kindle unlimited do not seem to sync with freetime very well, or in the case of prime...at all. so lets say i wish to allow my kids to watch any pg movie on amazon prime. they can't do this via freetime. this is frustrating. i want them to have access to the features i have. i just want parental controls so i can make sure they're not going to accidently access dirty movies. and i don't want to have to do it all for them. i thought this would be easier for me. it is not. they can't access prime movies at all as far as i can tell.

kindle unlimited seems to have a different problem with freetime. i can work around it, but it is annoying. what you have to do is access kindle unlimited via a parents/adults profile. then get a new book. then add it to your child's freetime. then they can download it to their device. this seems like a small thing right? but i have 2 kids and one of them is a 9 year old who sometimes goes through a book an hour. he's a very avid reader. i do not want to be hounded by my kids to access unlimited every time they need a new book. basically it is compatible, but not as compatible as i would like and the only reason i have kindle unlimited is because my kids are constantly asking me to download books for them.

my next problem with freetime is that it's set up for 5 year olds. it's supposed to have 2 settings: for kids under 8 and kids 9-17. when you set up their profiles, you put in the age of your child and select which setting you want. nearly all the same books and videos and games show up for both kids, even though my nine year old has the setting for older kids. the only difference i can really see is the background color is black for my 9 year old and blue for my 5 year old, and the suggested books and games at the top are a little different. what interest is a nine year old going to have in "but not the hippopotamus" or "little critters" apps? they're not age appropriate. and the books can't be sorted by things like ar reading level, grade level, or even boy/girl. they're all mixed up in this silly thing. there's no way to sort them, and there's no way to search by reading level. they have level 1 (learn to read books) mixed right in with chapter books. and let metell you, the chapter books are seriously lacking. there's almost nothing that my 9 year old wants to read. i don't expect them to have the most popular series books available, but i do expect way more than the current offerings. as a mom, this is a big amazon fail in my book. i might keep freetime for my 5 year old, but probably not for my 9 year old. it's just not useful. i'd rather give him full access to prime and unlimited than limit him the way freetime does.

so here's what freetime needs to be for any amazon people that might view this:

for my 5 year old, it's mostly ok, but:
i want a way to allow them to access prime movies from my subscription that are rated g or pg, without me having to type in my code, add a movie/show, allow them access, and download the darn thing.
i want it to suggest books and move them to the top of the list based on the other books my child has shown interest in.
i want to be able to set a reading level/range for my kid, and i want those to be the only books that show.
i want it to filter out "girl" books about rainbows, unicorns, and fairytales. no offense, my boy is just not interested.

for my 9 year old, not ok:
mostly the same as above.
i want to set a reading level/range.
i don't want baby books showing up.
i don't want "girl" books showing up for my 9 year old boy. again, no offense. i have no problem with him reading those books, but he won't because they don't typically include farts, butts, ninjas, or vomit. he like boy books.
i want book, app, and video suggestions made based on what he's shown interest in. and i want them age appropriate. i don't want it suggesting learn to read books about trucks showing up just because he read an age appropriate chapter book about monster trucks yesterday. there's a huge difference in reading levels.
i want it to allow him access to my kindle unlimited, but since i also use unlimited, i want a way to limit which books he can return to get a new book.
i do not want to have to add the kindle unlimited books to his profile myself. i just want him to have permission, preferably based on the preset reading level/range i mentioned above and let him go. i don't want him to download erotic romance novels, but i want him to be able to download the next 6th grade ninja book...on his own.
i want him to have access to all g and pg movies available on my prime, and i do not want to have to authorize each one.

review_headline: new model has no hdmi jack and still does not have a memory card slot to add memory
review_body: the basic unit is ok, but calling it "hd" and not including an hdmi port (which is on my 7" fire hd purchased in 2012) is an outrageous downgrade by amazon to try to extract more money from its customers to provide a jack which should be part of the hd unit.  yes, they do sell an adapter (which just converts the usb port to an hdmi port, but doesn't even provide an hdmi cable to hook up to your tv), but they want $25 for it.  this is very disappointing.  in addition, there is no memory card slot, so you can't increase the unit's memory.  if you decide to purchase this unit, be sure to get the 16gb of memory, since the memory can't be expanded.  and they still don't provide the basic function that is in the basic kindle of being able to set up "collections" so you can group your books.

review_body:
i was looking for a tablet for my daughter so she wouldnt kill my battery every time i pull it off the charger. this is not a tablet. this is a digital advertisement that wants to sync with your credit card and let your child buy as much as they can click on. there is so much to complain about i will narrow down to top 3 most frustrating things with this. 1- in order to download any free or paid apps i needed to set up "one click purchasing" which means if anyone just clicked yes when asked to purchase, well then i already gave permission to charge my card. that combined with every kids app letsyou play for 3 minutes then tries to force kids into purchasing is ridiculous! 2- this device is not set up with google at all. so no gmail, and no youtube, just bing search. no youtube? what else would i be using a tablet for? (now in fairness you can browse the internet on this with some unknown browser... but i specifically didnt want my kids going onto the internet to roam free.) 3- the lock screen background is an advertisement....? you cannot change the background at all, because that's where they putyet another scheme to get your kids to click on something without really knowing whats going on.
in closing, this doesnt do anything i wanted a tablet for. the parental controls are lacking significantly because its basically all or nothing. they offer a program called "free time" or something but i didnt even get a chance to check it out before i was putting back in the box to return.

on a positive note the books are in color, audiobooks play well, the camera is decent, and there is music, apps, internet, as well. i can see the pictures in my kindle cookbooks but i'm also disappointed that there aren't more photos, but that has more to do with the cookbook than the kindle.

review_headline: very happy with the fire...great first tablet for 8 year old
review_body:
fire is exactly what i was looking for for my son for christmas. he is 8, so i struggled with getting him any electronics at all. i have had to come to the realization that this generation is a generation of electronics. i like the fire because i can control what he has access to, how long he has access to it. i love that the fire is compatible with my fire tv, and works seamlessly with other amazon products. i love that with amazon free time i can limit his app usage, or set many different parental controls. all while i, the parent, still have access to the full line of features the fire has to offer.
easy to use and super simple to set up for him.
i did spend some time downloading some apps and a couple of videos for him before i gave it to him for christmas, so when he opened it, it would be ready to go. this did not take long at all and was well worth the look on his face christmas morning when he opened it!
it is very simple for an 8 year old to use as well. we do not let our child have gaming devices or electronics--this is the first. he was able to immediately turn it on, and navigate through everything on his own by reading and intuition. easy for him to use without having to ask for parental help every time he wants to "go back to the home page" or find something else to do.
easy for my son to navigate and control to watch movies with (all which you have the option to pre-select/filter what he has access too ) or set up on netflix (if you have an account). he loves it, and so do we!
the only thing i see as a tiny (possible) issue is the slow rate at which it seems to download apps and books etc. i am using the same internet at home for my laptop and the tablet seems to go a little slow. although i have not spent much time trying to diagnose this (possible) issue, so it could be something other than the tablet.

review_headline: the fire could be friendlier to the user....
review_body: the fire could be friendlier to the user, by a lot.  the specs are good, the stereo sound is great (would be better if located in the front), the \\"plastic\\" feel casing and oversized bezel around the screen doesn't bother me much, in fact i like to hold my thumb there; however, the inability to customize the look of the user interface bugs me.  i hate the whole carousel thing....it's rather too large for me -- i feel stupid looking at/scrolling thru oversized icons. the carousel is not customizable either: things you don't want to show up, will again show up even after removing it, once you use the app again.    add 12/27/14:  i enjoy having the menu buttons on the right hand side in landscape mode.  (too bad no customization for left handed people.) definitely better than having it at the bottom, like my wife's galaxy tab.    not being able to easily use google products such as youtube app or chrome browser is annoying. (i can't say i blame them...they're competitors!) at least going to youtube.com works fine.    you cannot use widgets.  =(  i'll miss my weather widget.    i haven't found an easy way to ensure programs are not running in the background...i feel that something is going on because the battery dropped 10% while i was sleeping with the screen turned off.  maybe there's an app for that.  overall, i think the battery life could be better.    i'm going to keep it of course, it was a gift and i'm not shy with figuring out how to side load things or root the operating system all together to get what i want....it would be nice to not have to do the workarounds.    in the end however, i would not recommend this device, nor buy another amazon device product, to include the fire phone, because of the lack of personal customization.  but, i'm sure some people don't mind, good for them, but not me.

review_headline: a neat easy to use color tablet at low cost.
review_body: i bought my wife the fire hdx 7" to replace her old kindle that was not functioning properly. and i saw how she liked hers, when amazon offered the fire hd7 at a sale price on my computer, she gave it to me as a christmas gift as well. so we are a two fire family. i am in my 70's and have some trouble holding large books like ken follete's almost 1000 page fall of giants, which i have in hard cover. i also live in a small cape and our book shelves are full so the kindle seemed a practical way for us to enjoy new books without the difficulties of handling or storage. the colors are bright, the fact that i can check my e-mail and go onto the internet and do other things as if i was on my computer attracted me. as an older person, i have a little trouble with the sensitivity of the page movement and so at times i would inadvertently skip several chapters. and i would have to find my way back, so i suggest trying to be aware of what chapter your reading when you get your new device. i noticed some differences between my fire hd 7 and my wife's hdx, first my power button is too small and i think it should be colored white so it can be easily found. next my wife's device can be set to show the actual book page your on, whereas mine shows the percentage of the book that you have completed. admittedly i have not explored all its features but i do like it. it does make reading easier because it has a back light for the screen, so even if your lamps are at a distance you can read. the lighting is always perfect. i also bought a belkin chambray case for it and am pleased with the color and find it easier to hold with the case than without. this device is worth the money and it has many advantages, one being that because i have a in home computer network, i never use the data allowed on my cell phone. before having the fire, i used my smartphone for a lot of the online tasks and always used up my data allowed by verizon; thereby incurring additional charges on my phone bill. my fire will actually lower my phone bill and pay for itself within the year.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: get the 16 gb, and thank yourself for doing so perhaps even larger?
review_body:
the kindle fire 8gb is a great device. i mean it's $100. obviously they loose some money in a loss-leader strategy where amazon makes money every other year. now i personally love my device. i got it for christmas. however, i will state that this is a failed product in the memory. it says 8 gb but you really get like 5 gb to play with, and out of that you may end up with 2 gb for books, movies and all the other apps you want. which is usually going to be limited to netflix, pandora, facebook, and maybe a game or two. i have 4.

great design. 5/5
you pay for what you get. the device is ergonomic, and great for a lot of functionality

aesthetics 3/5
you pay for what you look at. although it's angle in slightly in a contour that's a bit odd from a hand held perspective.

use 5/5
if you watch a lot of cartoons like i do, it's perfect. i'm pretty old to be watching cartoons but some of them are great. from a design perspective it's how you can get some fresh ideas sometimes.

speed 3/5
this device is not build for speed, but again the price.
storage. this device's storage absolutely stinks. i'm going to be honest. i have hearthstone a fun game that i may play every now and then but am considering deleting the entire app because it takes 1.23 gb of storage. fb is also a hogg, and i'm deciding that although it's cool using this device for fb. the device has no "clear" button. so i'm starting to figure out that this device and fb is not a great idea.

cloud.. 3/5
keep in mind that whatever you download will expand dramatically in data besides whatever is the mainstream apps like books and media. this means whatever you download like final fantasy or hearthstone has the potential to suck the life out of your kindle fire. within 1 day i've already maxed out the memory twice. it stinks.

i'm not about to return the device but amazon needs to give us a little legroom here. i know they give us a lot of first party storage. but would they mind letting us pay a little extra for our third party stuff?

amazon did seem to design a device for people who need a tablet entertainment center and alsow don't mind it if it gets stolen. i mean it's only $100. yes it stinks if it get's stolen or breaks. but it's not an ipad that you can break, or get stolen and that cost at a base minimum $500 on up.
engineering insight. 1/5

while i say this is a great overall design in my first point. from a engineering standpoint why didn't you include a sd card!? without the sd card this device technically is a 'failed' product in functionality. because eventually the device will run out of flash storage, and it will not work. but the point here is that if you need to transfer things, you must use your main computer. i've done that before and that is perfectly fine and dandy for myself. the main problem with that for some people is that it's a on the go device. perhaps you're in new york and the nearest computer is 3 blocks away but through a crowd of people. perhaps you are in a college and the nearest computer is 2 miles away in the library and you can't plug in. so amazon for me to have to constantly go to my device storage and be like ok which app truly do i need, is not going to be a great selling point. unfortunately i believe this product won't be around anymore because the newer version probably is already introduced or has been will be etc.

overall review the device seems to be designed for entertainment purposes. while the device works in functional design, there's a lot to be said for how amazon catered to the audience. the device works, and it's something that can be used for school. i do not recommend writing on the device. i also do not recommend storing audio books on this device either as it's function seems to be more towards books and say movies. if you do want audiobooks please use the normal kindle. the normal kindle is a perfect design example for something that has wifi, and a week's worth of battery. so if you have several devices. use your computer for facebook, use this for your movies (it's far more powerful then the computer at streaming.) i mean my computer gets so slow streaming videos at times this thing is much more high quality in 7" and i love watching. finally, use the small kindle touch for your audiobooks, and some heavier reading. this device can do reading.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
i definitely made a very expensive mistake.
there is absolutely nothing new on this kindle fire 7 that wasn't on my original kindle fire (after less than 2 years the internal connector for charger didn't accept the charger cord anymore and amazon wasn't interested in repairing it).
this fire is definitely targeted to just a certain user audience - most people won't even use all the battery consuming bells and whistles.
the battery has such a short life that it is impossible to use it for a day without plugging in to recharge.. and - charging extra for the electric plug connector is a scam.
this thing is not worth the $$..the instructions and advice videos on the amazon web site are gross - they are absolutely no help at all.
any helpful advice comes from plowing through the messages from users.
the covers all open backwards - not like a normal book.
the cord connection is very touchy and sometimes works and sometimes needs to be played with.
my old (but still running - but getting tired) kindle keyboard machine works better than this, lasts longer, connects to the web, and has a convertible connection cord..
please bring back a simple kindle for reading, audio, and web connection for those of us who have enough other electronics with all the bells and whistles we need.
don't buy it unless you want a new plaything..

review_headline: works fast, but the battery runs down too fast
review_body:
i bought this to replace my 2011 kindle fire which has finally pretty much died. i love the blue of this, and overall it's pretty much the same as my prior one. the display layout is a bit different, but that didn't take long at all to get used to.

my biggest complaint with this is the battery life - the same usage of this compared to my older model has this battery draining way faster. i'm having to charge this daily, rather than every 3-4 days, which is really frustrating. if there's ways to change settings to improve battery life more, i can't figure out what they are.

this is faster in terms of loading and processing things, though i can't say for sure if it's really an improvement over my other kindle, or just how much that one had slowed down from being a few years old.

i like the placement of the buttons on this one, with the volume buttons on the side rather than the top. i also love having the plug for the power cord on top, as opposed to the side. it makes it easier to charge while it's also in use, and not awkward to hold like when it was on the side.

review_body: worst purchase i have every made, i should have trusted my instincts to go with an ipad mini, but i decided that i go for the cheaper alternative instead.  well while setting up this device with freetime unlimited i manage to get myself locked out by parental controls, i contact customer service and they tell me to deregister the device so that i can register the device again.  the device deregisters from my amazon.com account and my device, except now that i go to register on the device i get a \\"registration error\\" and cannot register it again.  i spend 3 hours with kindle technical support and they have no idea why the device is now in a limbo state and they say that it is not connected to wifi and that i should test it with the silk browser... except that the silk browser is blocked by parental controls that i cannot unlock.  i switch 3 wifi hotspots to prove the point that it is not a connection issue especially since i have 2 kindles and 2 other hd 7's that i am setting up which are operating fine.  as the parental code is device specific (i must have mis-typed this device over the others) there is nothing they can do except factory reset, except they can't even do that because they can't ping, they can't remote alarm, they can't even send out a remote factory reset because the device exists as if it is not even connected to wifi (which i assure you it is).  essentially i've first handedly at the instruction of amazon quarantined my device into a state of limbo.  to make matters worse?  this is 9:30 pm to 12:48 am christmas morning and 1 of 3 of my kiddos is going to be heartbroken tomorrow as to why his kindle is deregistered and has nothing on it except a parental control prompt that we can't get rid of.. amazon's solution?  yeah, there's no \\"let's send doug a new one next dat air and we'll sort out this software issue on our end\\" it's \\"you can always choose to return it, but until our development team explicitly states that it is beyond troubleshooting you will need to be patient and work with them...\\" over the next 2-5 business days, which is what, 2 weeks!??  mind you this is brand new out of the box while setting them up as christmas gifts.  absolute epic fail.  if it weren't for purchase as disposable tablets for the kids i wouldn't even bother anymore.  if you have the means steer clear of amazon hardware and invest in a apple ipad mini instead.
