review_headline: perfect for amazon addicts - great for everyone!
review_body:
i assisted my 90 year-old father in the purchase of the fire hd, and decided the price was too good to pass up so i purchased one for myself, and i love it. i work in it (35 years) and have laptops, an ipad v2, a great smart phone, and still find the fire hd 7 to be irresistible. it is almost the perfect size, perfect for its portability, but after using the ipad for several years, would appreciate a bit more screen real estate. with that said, i am perfectly happy with it, love the apps, books, music, videos, and games.

the hardware is quite exceptional, especially given the price point. more than adequate speed, and the screen and sound quality are amazing, again, especially for the price point.

the fire is super easy to setup and the "amazon" connection is fantastic. i purchase a ton from amazon and like that i can search amazon for an app, game, book, order it, and it automatically downloads to the device. this is especially helpful for me, as i administer my father's fire hd from 2,000 miles away!

my only serious gripe is i wish i could use the google play store to purchase/install apps on the fire hd. there are a ton of great android apps that are either unavailable or difficult to install on the fire hd.

my only other wish would be for an sd card port. it would be great to be able to carry more multimedia without relying on wi-fi and cloud access.

regarding accessories, i highly recommend the finite cover and the amazon stylus.

i would certainly buy it again, and recommend it to anyone without qualification.

review_headline: buy a samsung instead, the custom amazon interface has severely limited the best aspects of having an android tablet
review_body:
i'm a huge android fan and was trying to decide between this and the samsung tab for my daughter. i have a samsung note and everyone in our home has samsung galaxy s4 phones. i've also had other android tablets in the past. i picked this because it had a bit faster processor speed than the tab and the tech reviews online were glowing. however, i've found it to be an awful watered-down version of an android tablet, with many android apps and features just not available because of the dumbed down interface that forces use of amazon app store and prohibits access to the main and largest android app store, google play. it also lacks other great android features commonly found on the samsung and nexus android tablets.

what this means:

if you have bought apps in the google play store in the past (for previous tablets, phone, etc.) you will not be able to access them, download them, or use them at all on this tablet unless you root it, which then invalidates all warranties, etc. (and you also need decent tech abilities were you to want to try to root it). the interface does not allow you to download the google play store, nor can you try to get apps from it via the browser, as something about the way they've programmed the fire essentially makes it invisible to the android play store, so that the store doesn't recognize the fire tablet as being an android.

even if you've never bought anything from the google play store, it's still a bummer for you because the amazon app store has a very limited selection of apps. if you're getting this for your kid, they want to change the wall papers and personalize the tablet. there is a very limited selection of not very interesting wallpapers and it's just not optimized to enhance your experience by customizing it with apps you'd like because the selection is so very limited. i have about 30 some apps in my google play account. once owned, you can use them for any of your android products (usually) and once you login to your google account you have easy access to download them all to your new device. can't do that with the fire at all. so even if it does have some of the apps i like and use, i'd have to pay for them again, via the amazon app store in order to have them. i have a bunch of medical apps that i use and some of them are available in the amazon store, but most are not. same with the apps my daughter has and even more so with the wallpapers and other personalizations that are typically available for android products.

my daughter, when checking out this tablet and attempting to customize it, was seriously disappointed and upset with it, stating "my android phone has more capabilities and things to do with it than this tablet!". if your kid is at all tech savvy they will hate this tablet.

unfortunately it seems like amazon has taken a great little tablet but stripped it of it's great abilities in order to force-funnel all owners into buying from their limited app store, streaming only their videos and music, disallowing access to other great media and news and useful applications that are found in the google play store, thus limiting it's capabilities. there may be other sites that it limits the use of as i didn't do an exhaustive search, prohibiting google play access was enough for me to know we'd never be happy with it. i'd say the apps it comes with, already loaded are disappointing as well when compared to what comes on a real android tablet (one that lets you access the full world of apps, music, books & magazines, blogs & posts, etc. that most every other android tablet can access) it's kind of like buying a truck but blocking off the back bed area (the box area where you can put tons of stuff, the essential part of a truck that makes it so useful..) so that you can never put anything in it or use it, you can only put stuff in the front cab - why bother with a truck then?

if you want a true android with allthe capabilities of an android (and i can think of no reason that you wouldn't want that...) then you really need to buy an alternate android tablet. i'd suggest looking at the samsung tablets, such as the tab or note. i am not an apple fan at all, but i would even say to get an ipad over this tablet as it's capabilities have just been too stunted by the limits imposed by amazon's interface. it's very disappointing as in general i'm a huge amazon fan and i love my amazon fire tv and basic kindle. however, with this they've very much disappointed me. this tablet is limited to streaming video & music from amazon, downloading amazon books and light/limited internet browsing. it's true capabilities have been cut off.

summary: severely limited use as you can't access the thousands of apps and goodies on google play as the amazon interface prohibits downloading the google play app and has made the tablet unrecognizable as an android if you access google play via the browser. you'd have to root it in order to change this which will invalidate your warranty. this denied access to google play severely limits the capabilities of your tablet. if you want a real android tablet with full functionality look at the samsung tab or samsung note instead. the decision by amazon to prohibit full access to the plethora of android features and apps is very disappointing.the capabilities of an android (and i can think of no reason that you wouldn't want that...) then you really need to buy an alternate android tablet. i'd suggest looking at the samsung tablets, such as the tab or note. i am not an apple fan at all, but i would even say to get an ipad over this tablet as it's capabilities have just been too stunted by the limits imposed by amazon's interface. it's very disappointing as in general i'm a huge amazon fan and i love my amazon fire tv and basic kindle. however, with this they've very much disappointed me. this tablet is limited to streaming video & music from amazon, downloading amazon books and light/limited internet browsing. it's true capabilities have been cut off.

summary: severely limited use as you can't access the thousands of apps and goodies on google play as the amazon interface prohibits downloading the google play app and has made the tablet unrecognizable as an android if you access google play via the browser. you'd have to root it in order to change this which will invalidate your warranty. this denied access to google play severely limits the capabilities of your tablet. if you want a real android tablet with full functionality look at the samsung tab or samsung note instead. the decision by amazon to prohibit full access to the plethora of android features and apps is very disappointing.

review_headline: not even close to competing with a stock android tablet
review_body:
i am a huge fan of amazon, but they have ruined android with all their restrictions, customizations and lack of google play. i knew the device wouldn't have google play, but i was shocked to see that nothing google was actually a google app. all google apps (gmail, youtube, etc) are third party apps that, quite frankly, suck. i should have checked into that more, but trusting amazon to have a good product i failed to check further (my fault). however, the fact still remains that this is nothing like an android tablet and basically is a kindle that can browse the internet (only on the silk browser) and play games. it's not an android tablet, it's a jazzed up kindle with a terrible ui. amazon promotes this thing as an alternative to higher priced android tablets. it comes nowhere close to competing with a tablet offering android with the google play store. even apple, the most restrictive company out there, allows google apps on their devices. amazon needs to get with the program and offer a more user friendly os that doesn't exclude people from using google play. i have no doubt that google play would be on the kindle fire if amazon wanted it.

all that said, i can make the kindle fire work for me. i can root the device (yes, void the warranty) and add google play or sideload the google apps i want. it's not the end of the world, but it shouldn't have to be that way. i haven't decided yet if i'll be keeping it or returning it and going with a galaxy tab 4.

review_body: the one thing that i don't love on this is that there is no light to signal when charging is completed. every other kindle, including my other fire (lcd) shows an orange light while charging that turns green when it's ready to go. not that this is a deal breaker, there are plenty other super features to enjoy, but it does keep me from giving it five stars. why they left that off i have no idea - people will just have to guess whether the thing has been plugged in long enough. other than that, i like the color - good thing, too, because it was the only one available with the other order specs i wanted, e.g., 16gb over 8, with no special offers (after all, it is supposed to be an upgrade from my lcd, and the extra charges still brought it in under $150) except you have to watch, as you are choosing your options, that the item you think you are ordering does not change on you: for instance i had chosen blue, and as soon as i selected 16gb rather than 8, they switched my item to the 6 inch; then i had chosen pink, and when i selected no special offers, they switched me to black. another combination of choices would have gone through as requested except that the estimated shipping time suddenly jumped from right away to a week or so hence. you could assume that, once you have started your selection process, the item you want would be locked in, but this is definitely a situation where you must be paying attention and double check your shopping cart details before completing your order. other things i like about it are the slightly larger screen and slightly lighter weight from my lcd, and it still has the lightning quick response that i have grown to love. oh, and the camera - my lcd does not have a camera, and i really wanted one - the images are a bit grainy, so i won't depend on this device to take the place of anything with decent resolution.

so after i've had this for a year and a half, i would like to add to this review. i still like the tablet but there are several of issues that really irritate me and i find them totally frustrating.
first read what it includes..you cannot add a memory card to it. they did an update to this after having it a year and now all your books, files, music go onto the cloud instead of staying on your tablet. that is great if you are connected to the internet. i couldn't access anything while on the road during a trip a few months back. not even my downloaded music! not good!!

third, i've noticed that while reading or playing a game on the tablet that it gets very warm after only an hour. you have to stop, close the case and let it rest or it starts closing the programs and taking you back to the home page. if you are playing a game you lose your points and have to go back to the beginning. i noticed this started after the update.

i'm thinking maybe they did all this to get you to buy the newer version of the tablet. only problem is i am now on a very fixed income and cannot afford it. sigh!

review_body:
i love my kindle reader (the older one with the external keyboard) and was excited when amazon came out with a tablet. i was finally able to afford one and purchased the hd7. i got it home, got it all set up, and immediately set it back to factory settings and returned it. found out you can't customize it like you can other tablets and the crazy scrolling thing at the top is very confusing. not user friendly at all!! i could create folders for my books but what was the point, it didn't remove them from the scrolling thing which just kept getting longer and longer as i added books, etc. also, the placement in the scroll seems to be random so you have to go searching to find an unread book, etc. their app for computers and other tablets are setup the same way which again is annoying but at least you can control things on the tablet outside the kindle stuff better.

being bombarded with the special offers every time i turn on the tablet was very annoying, too. i guess amazon allows you to remove them for a price. i like to look at special offers but not every time i turn on the tablet! why not create an icon that the user can select to browse the special offers.

i am a big amazon fan but holy cow, they missed it on their tablets!

review_headline: basic but lacking for user friendly programming
review_body: as a basic tablet this works. i have had this device for about two weeks and find it frustrating but kindle capable.  i am not a big fan of the carousel or bar options at the top of the device main screen features as you can't tailor the contents to your personal use.  an annoying feature of the crousel feature is the filling in of books purchased when you didn't bring them into your device.  overall apps for the device are not the best, missing the basic app "settings" you have to search for it.  i have tried app searches from the app store and failed to find many that are available to basic smart phones or other tablets on the market.  not all apps on the device show up other than from the option line at the top of the main screen.  i find this annoying.  this device could be much more user friendly like other tablets available.  another issue is the screen is not outdoor or sun light friendly as it has a glare and caused me to purchase a screen cover to allow it as a better reader.  once i receive this cover, i will see what it does to video and picture views from the browser app or pictures.  the music app purchase fiction could indicate download to the fire as an option when you purchase from the first scren to make sure you are not purchasing an album or cd. yet, it does the basic functions fine and this is why i gave it 4 stars instead of 3 stars (which was my first thought). as said the device works, just needs better programming.  also, like many electronics today, the device has a terrible instruction finding option for easy research.  an overhaul of the programming could go a long way to making this much more user friendly and a five star rating.  but then again the price does probably limit functionality of the device.

review_headline: nice reader, learning what else it can do!
review_body: ok, truth in advertising time.  this is my second kindle fire hd 7.  my first froze up exactly 15 minutes after turn on and had to be sent back. amazon sent me my new one quick, quick and now i'm going to review that one.  (remember most electronic items if they are going to fail, fail within 1 hour of first turn on time, due to weak components or manufacturing defects.  i made 15 minutes.)  now my new kindle was charged upon arrival 99% so i didn't have to go through the 12 hour charge time most new items need.  i was able to find how to register and all that by following the on screen instructions.  beyond that i'm watching some you tube videos to go deeper into what this machine will do and it's very nice.  great screen resolution, fast, very fast.  book reading i needed to up the font size (due to my aging eyes i'm 59) but that is easy and worked.  downloading books, with my system at home it is very fast and easily done.  now working through the app's and what i would like to do besides reading books with this.  recommendation - buy this kindle, it is worth the money.  it is a great little tool and will be for sometime to come.  i bought the 16gb, wifi and would do it again.  next purchase a good solid case for travel.  research on amazon has many but will advise later.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: big improvement in the audio, the bluetooth works great, and the browser is fast
review_body:
i have a few older kindles but i wanted one with more memory. this one fits the bill. it runs fast and everything about it seems better, with the exception of the on/off button, which i find a bit hard to find in the dark. i'm sure i will get used to it in time, but it doesn't stick up much from the surface of the kindle at all.

the bluetooth works well, and i love the louder audio. it's nice that the volume controls are handy on the side and easy to control without having to pull the screen down.

i choose pink, because i once lost a kindle fire. turns out black is extremely hard to find in a house with a lot of books. it took me 2 years to find it tucked in the side of my magazine holder. i'd cleaned that thing out several times and still missed it - so i definitely went for the color. the magenta color is pretty and it stands out enough when it is laid down, peeking through the case.

it is delightful that movies and youtube actually work now. i got the one with offers. i have an older one that i got with offers and i found that i actually enjoy seeing them. they do not slow the device down and often they are just a quick ad that you can choose to look at further or not showing a latest movie or new product out.

i wasn't real sure about cameras so for right now i just put a bit of tape over mine on the cases. they are nice for taking a quick picture though. i did try them, there is the capability front and back.

this is a nice jump forward. i'm very pleased with this purchase.

update 4/26/2016 this is still going strong and is one of my favorite electronics. i have dropped it, knocked it off the bed, and once went to sleep reading it, it fell over and hit me in the face, and i woke up and threw it at a concrete wall before i realized what was going on. it still lives with little if any damage. it's really tough! i did put a moshi screen protector on it, and i keep it in a good case.

review_headline: device is great. parental controls miss the mark.
review_body:
the fire is great. the kids profiles need a lot of work. overall, the fire hd is a good device at this price point.

my first impression, holding it, was that it felt cheap. the back cover feels like cheap plastic over a hollow space, where my samsung galaxy tab 8 has a much more solid feel to it. but, this wasn't a device for me, it was for my 8 year old, so i wasn't hung up about that too much.

setting up profiles for kids is a pain. you can't do it on the web; you have to do it on the device. that is a headache. i should be able to do it anywhere and have it apply. i should be able to copy profiles from one child to another. i should be able to green light content in categories. i should, for example, be able to green light all g, pg, and tv-pg movies. i shouldn't have to decide each time.

when i purchase a new book, i should be able to say on amazon's site if my kids' profiles can access this title. i shouldn't have to go to the kindle, open up the parent view, open up the child settings (for each child separately) and then scroll forever to find the title i just purchased.

i wish i could specify which apps could be used with time limits. there are many apps that would fit my goal of 'educational' apps for 30 minutes, but i can't set that anywhere, so i end up opening up all apps all the time because the settings are poorly implemented.

it is ridiculous that the kids profiles can't access music or movies. at all. no matter what. you can't open that setting to your kids without leaving the protected profile. bizarre.

amazon's free time application for kids is absolute garbage for any kid over 5 years old. if your kid is under 5, then free time is maybe fine for you. however, free time is so restrictive that there is absolutely no way to do any in app purchases, even with a password, even if you already purchased the in app purchase in the adult account tied to the device. if you have a game or whatever and you make an in-app purchase, your kids in kindle free time won't be able to use the purchased content even thought the exact same app on the device in the parent profile has the purchased content.

free time has two modes: under 8 and over 8. there are exactly two differences: (1) the background color changes. (woo hoo!) and (2) in the 8+ version, they take away a 'characters' filter. so, the 8+ version has fewer features than the little kid version. they don't add anything else. no options for any kind of web browser or connection. no options for any kind of in-app purchases, even with a parent password. no options for any kind of social connections at all. nothing.

amazon's free time application is a great idea that is horribly implemented. it was the main reason i purchased the fire over competing tablets, and it is so completely lame that it is unusable for any kid over about 5 years old.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: ... really really don't understand who thought it was a good idea to replace android with a way worse custom ...
review_body:
i really really really don't understand who thought it was a good idea to replace android with a way worse custom version of android that doesn't support anything that i use android for. the amazon app store is terrible and the apps are horrendous. i have an android phone and i use maybe 10-15 apps regularly (including games). none of these work on the fire. literally zero. the google authentication and app framework aren't a part of the fire so even emailing the apps to myself and doing a ghetto installation results in a bad user experience as i can't log in to any of my apps.

they also wrote their own browser. that obviously sucks. which i'm pretty surprised about because i assume it's just a branded version of the stock android browser. but it's slower, doesn't cache my tab content when i close the browser, and has weird interface querks that just baffle me. seriously, let me freaking install chrome on this thing. oh wait, amazon made really poor decisions with this device and i can't.

it functions as well as any other tablet in terms of being an e-reader and i love that i can watch movies on it. but i could do all of those things and more on a non-butchered version of android. i use it a lot to read with, and i love that i can use it in bed without lights on. but it's heavy and every time i hit the home button and am taken back to a home page that sucks i'm angry that i wasted money on this instead of spending the extra $50 to get a real android tablet that supports the kindle app (fyi, all of them do).

overall, don't buy this. do yourself a favor and go buy an actual android tablet, install the kindle app and the audible app and rest assured that you'll be much happier than if you had bought this.

review_body: bought this thinking we'd get a tablet and a kindle which kids and adults could use. boy, were we wrong!    the kindle reader and streaming amazon/prime video and audio work, but are actually worse than using amazon apps on other android devices due to issues with the device.   anything else is so frustrating you will lose your sanity cussing at amazon.  - wifi tends to be unstable - this despite having the latest fireos. in areas where other smartphones and tablets work fine, the fire shows wifi connection with good strength but nothing (including amazon) works - need to restart the device (or turn wifi off and then back on) almost daily.  - even when wifi works, it can be slow. for example, when accessing amazon prime video upstairs (further from my wifi access point/router), i get messages saying the network is not fast enough to stream the content. in the same location and network, a nexus 7 is able to stream the same content just fine (no, the nexus 7 is not on a 5ghz wifi network).  - the silk browser is pathetically slow - if it works at all. if you switch to another app and try to come back, the browser may have crashed in the interim.  - there is no multi-tasking - at least that you can control. you can't be sure if apps you used are still running (whether you want that or not).  - think you can access youtube easily? think again. you can find some apps for this in amazon's store, but they aren't good.  - think you can get another browser? it's not going to be easy to find chrome or firefox. the silk browser won't display firefox's download site and won't allow google apps.  - like to watch videos on comedy central? you'll see an error saying they only support chrome on android. they haven't heard of fireos.  - search for other apps? you'll find a ton of junk masquerading as apps you may know/love, including porn apps.  _ today, the device unregistered itself from amazon for no apparent reason. so i ended up having to download and reinstall/reconfigure allmy apps & content again.    freetime is supported on the fire - so you can set up a kid-friendly area with daily reading goals etc. but the time doesn't sync across devices, so the time read on a kindle won't count on the fire.  also, the fire lacks some features available on the kindle paper white - such as vocabulary builder.  the kindle devices are entirely different in terms of user interface etc - so don't buy a fire because you happen to love your kindle.    amazon's customer service is great in their desire to make things right. but that doesn't mean they have good technical support - desire and ability are different things. they shipped me a replacement device. but it has much the same issues.      overall, the device promises to be a kindle reader, a device from which to consume amazon content and an androidish tablet. but it fails to live up to expectations as any of those.   if you want an ereader, get a kindle paper white. this includes freetime profiles for kids and vocabulary builder (which the fire does not).  if you want a tablet (that can access amazon content - books, prime video and music), save your sanity and buy yourself a nexus 7. you can install the kindle reader, amazon music and amazon app for books, music and video respectively, and they work better than the fire. the one thing you won't get is freetime parental controls for apps.

review_headline: initially great, but less than six months later... dead.
review_body: edit: 02/24/2015  the review below is when i originally received my kindle in december 2014. during the early part of february, my kindle stopped turning on. i first noticed this after i left it idle for about an hour, off the charger, with the battery at around 54%, so there is no possible way the battery had died. regardless, i did everything i could to try and get it to work, including amazon's recommended instructions for those with my issue. i dealt with customer service several times about this incident and was told that i would receive a new one in the mail. fine - however, i noticed that the one being sent to me was refurbished. apparently, in the warranty of the kindle, should anything go wrong, you can be sent either a new or refurbished one. while this may be okay for some, it definitely wasn't for me considering i had originally paid for a new one and had never dropped it, exposed it to liquid or used anything other than the original charger. in addition to this, the refurbished  kindle was not even sent in a properly packaged box. one cardboard box with just one plastic insulator inside and with the kindle and charger just what seems to be thrown in! i am retracting the original 5 stars to 2, as amazon's customer service was exceptional in doing their best to fix all of this. though, i think amazon's policy on *their* product is awful. perhaps i am just too picky, but i don't think i'll ever purchase a kindle again.    original review: 12/02/2014  very lightweight and reads like a dream. the apps run well without any lag. i'm really glad that i paid extra for 16gb and without the special offers, it's everything i imagined and more!

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: quicker than 2012 fire hd, excellent value, but compromised.
review_body:
the most recent incarnation of the kindle fire hd 7" (as of october 2014) is an excellent value but with some improvements and some compromises compared with the original kindle fire hd we bought in late 2012 and still use daily. it's much faster with some improvements to the os, which are enough to offset some minor compromises. and the price point is right for a very competitive market.

improvements:
*as of april 2017 the os for this older kindle fire hd was upgraded to include alexa -- just days after we'd purchased the most recent fire hd 8. good to see amazon continuing to support these devices.
*this quad core version is much, much faster than either our original kindle fire hd or the 2nd or 3rd generation fire hd our friend purchased last year when the price dropped to around $139.
*a word search in a 470 page novel that takes 2 minutes on the older fire hd takes only seconds with the quad core version - around 7 seconds to find 22 instances of a word. a bible word search that took nearly 5 minutes with the 2012 fire hd took only 10 seconds with the new 3rd generation fire hd 7".
*everything scrolls more smoothly, without hitches. the carousel, apps, facebook and web pages all scroll much more quickly and smoothly than with our 2012 fire hd.
*the overall operating system and navigation are better. from books to carousel and device management, everything is a little more sensible. many quirks of the 2012 fire hd os have been fixed.
*built-in speech-to-text for rudimentary voice entry of web searches, short emails and social media posts.
*much better accessibility options for disabled users with vision impairments, dexterity or mobility challenges.

the same - good as ever:
*the display. i'm a photographer. photos still look great, as do hd videos. in addition to my calibrated photo editing system, i'll often use the fire hd to evaluate my photos to be sure they look right for general web display and email.
*the overall interface remains familiar. we're comfortable with it, including the carousel. so no significant change is a good thing for us.

disappointments:
*built-in speech-to-text not quite intuitive and doesn't seem to respond to some normal commands used by other speech-to-text software.
*audio. the most recent fire hd 7" audio is a notch worse. the original 2012 fire hd audio was remarkably good, clear with good stereo separation through those rear firing speakers - even with a cover, or the tablet sitting in a lap or on a table. it was good enough for watching most movies, and even pleasant enough for some long term music listening. the new fire hd 7" is adequate but lacks the sparkle and clarity of the original.
*physical design. the front remains the same, other than placement of the camera - only the edges and back have changed. the new fire hd 7" feels very ... ordinary. blocky edges, with inadequate tactile quality on the rear surface to be comfortable for long term handling in one hand. the new model definitely needs a good cover. the 2012 fire hd showed more attention to detail, which gently beveled edges, and a nice tactile feel on the rear cover that made it pleasant to use one-handed even without a cover. but this compromise may have been necessary to achieve the lower price point.
*control placement - this isn't a serious drawback, and some users would consider it an improvement. the original 2012 fire hd on/off and volume controls were nearly flush and unlikely to be unintentionally pressed. but some users found them difficult to use. the most recent fire hd 7" has somewhat more prominent switches that are easily felt and seen, but also more vulnerable to accidental operation. the compromise in the 2nd or 3rd generation version my friend bought in 2013 seemed about right, but admittedly control design and placement on a device like this are very subjectiveand unlikely to please every user.
*as a photographer i doubt i'll find much use for the 2mp camera. tablet ergonomics are terrible for steady handheld photography or video. it would need stabilization, higher resolution and more interesting editing apps before i'd consider it more than a novelty. picky, sure, but samsung has really raised expectations for cameras in mobile devices.
*the os has some glitches. clicking on external web links from facebook often takes several tries, especially when multiple browser tabs are open. this wasn't a problem with our older 2012 fire hd using the silk browser. hopefully it'll be resolved soon. (january 12, 2015 update: this glitch has mostly been resolved.)

we're still big fans of the kindle fire hd and amazon universe, even though we've noticed the devices seem to have only a 2-3 year lifespan before problems develop. our kindle keyboard failed in just under 3 years. and our 2-year-old 2012 model fire hd has begun showing symptoms of overheating, with shorter battery life per charge, and taking longer than usual to recharge. however that 2012 fire hd has been used daily for two years, often several hours a day, so it's probably used more heavily than some folks would use such a device. (january 12, 2015 update: the overheating problem with our 2012 kindle fire hd was resolved by deleting the resource-hogging washington post app and doing a full reset. the otherwise excellent washington post news app works fine our the new fire hd 7".)

as prime subscribers, we're still very satisfied with amazon overall, including customer support. when my elderly mom inadvertently taps the wrong thing and makes an unwanted purchase instead of putting it on the wish list, there's never a problem cancelling the order. when our older 2012 fire hd didn't auto-update to ensure compatibility with prime music, a customer support rep online patiently guided me through the manual update process. this was much better than wading through the hundreds of useless gripes on the amazon discussion forums where most users would rather complain than actually fix a problem. deliveries are usually excellent (the very few problems have been the fault of the usps, not amazon). that sort of top notch customer service is what keeps us coming back to amazon devices, which are really good values now.mera. tablet ergonomics are terrible for steady handheld photography or video. it would need stabilization, higher resolution and more interesting editing apps before i'd consider it more than a novelty. picky, sure, but samsung has really raised expectations for cameras in mobile devices. *the os has some glitches. clicking on external web links from facebook often takes several tries, especially when multiple browser tabs are open. this wasn't a problem with our older 2012 fire hd using the silk browser. hopefully it'll be resolved soon. product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
i've got to say, having read that this thing uses a (heavily customized) android os, i had thought that this would be a lot more like the nexus 7 than it turned out to be. i am fairly disappointed.

the hardware specs and performance are quite nice, but it's essentially a fancy kindle. it's a real champ for reading books on a tiny screen, if that's what you want to do. but if you expected to be able to use the google play app ecosystem or treat the device like any other android device, you'll be very frustrated. amazon has a competing app marketplace, but the offerings are very limited in some areas that are important to me. i think that was very shortsighted of amazon, and is a missed opportunity in my opinion.

i'm not at all impressed with the silk browser, and am rather annoyed that i'd have to root the device to use any other browser. at least my nexus 7 can use chrome, which is not only a better browser but helps keep all of my devices (except this dressed-up kindle) synchronized.

and i've just got to say... amazon requiring you pay extra if you do *not* want the kindle fire hd to show advertisements on the lock screen is just cheesy. wow.

i'm honestly considering sending this back.

review_headline: very limited fire os, do not buy if you want performance and customization.
review_body:
the tablet build quality is good, but i don't care for the fire os and how restricted it is. there is almost zero ways to customize the tablet, and you're locked into the limited amazon app store. you cannot get or use any google apps, so no gmail, youtube, or google maps!!!

additionally, while the hardware specs are comperable to most higher end tablets the actual performance or running the os and using the web browser are quite poor.

the os is clunky and i even had a software bug to where i was locked out of the tablet completely and the tablet would not reset itself as it should have, and i had to sit on the phone with 4 different amazon techs for ~3-4 hours total until they finally sent me a replacement device.

i would only recommend this for kids or grandparents since it is so restricted. but honestly the samsung or google nexus tables are a way better way to go for anyone.

review_body: i presently own the 2013 kindle fire hd, it is my first tablet. it has opened my eyes to the world of amazon. the device is excellent for reading or listening to audio or video. the kindle fires were created for amazon users in mind. i believe that for the price it really is an excellent deal.  first, the device comes loaded with many features that are useful, l like the silk browser but i also downloaded another browser to compliment it. it is also possible to download and store e-books, audiobooks, digital music, videos or games on the kindle. the variety is incredible as long as you have internet.  no one offers so much for free like amazon.com. i have received a few great offers on music deals and books. i have also obtained free e-books and have found apps or websites that offer free books from amazon for the kindles.  each day a new app is offered on the app store, a free app of the day. the kindle offers two choices for storage: the cloud or the device. i would recommend backing up anything that is not pertinent to the cloud if possible, it frees up space on the device and may easily be reinstalled when needed.  i also recommend joining amazon prime, if you enjoy watching videos. it has a thirty-day free trial that upgrades to ninety-nine dollars a year. the prime time offers unlimited music streaming without ads, unlimited movies or tv shows to watch on various devices that stream videos. amazon also offers free unlimited photo storage; which works great on the 2014 kindle that has two cameras, front and back.  recently, amazon updated the kindle fire with new and better features and visual improvements that enlarged the font and type size. they also offered a paid app of \\"the washington post\\" for six months to try for free. i also discovered another great improvement called immersion reading. this allows the reader to buy a kindle book, then adds narration and highlights; so that one can read and listen at the same time. amazon offers the users to try a classic book with narration for less than a dollar.  my negatives are few, the device needs more than 8 gb for storage space and app usage. the system apps are really great, but some features are unnecessary and by default can't be removed. even if you don't have any need for an alarm clock or calculator these apps may not be removed.  for the price, i believe the new kindle fire with double cameras is a wonderful deal and the 16 gb is definitely better. i highly recommend this device and have thoroughly enjoyed using my kindle daily. i greatly appreciate amazon.com for the many great features and offers made to their loyal customers, and i only discovered them by using the kindle fire.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: fast, great speakers, meets my needs
review_body:
i really spent a lot of time researching before buying this kindle. it's my 3rd and my last kindle fire previous gen is only 2 years old and having issues of being unable to stay on sites ( keeps saying it needs to reload), extremely slow, and making me very frustrated. i've set it back to factory settings and even tried to see if i could turn it into an android without success. i love my android phone, but it doesn't have a front facing camera and i really wanted to get something that had a camera so that i could skype without sitting at my desktop.
anyway, the advantages of buying an android tablet is that you can indeed access all your amazon books, movies and music plus you can access all of googles services. i own an apple desktop, and don't want another apple product, so that wasn't even in the equation ( plus the price) . i almost went for the nexus9, but then decided that i really didn't want to spend that much money on a product that may need to be replaced in a few years. the kindle takes care of all my needs. i like having the cloud ( so long as amazon stays in business) to store all my music and books, and now it also stores pictures. since all my digital music and books are from amazon this isn't an issue for me. pcmag rates tablets and they gave the fire a pretty good review. right now there are a lot of androids around the same price or even cheaper, but many of them seem to have issues like poor speakers, no front camera, etc. the speakers and camera were important to me. i like being able to listen to audiobooks without earphones, or to music.
the camera has a panoramic feature unlike any i have ever seen. you set the camera for panoramic push the button, it takes a pic and then it tells you to slide your phone over, you do and push the button again. the picture has a bit of a curve look to it, but it's still quite cool. you can then easily share picture by email, facebook etc. amazon will store pictures for you now, althoughit is limited unless you are a prime member. i don't know if they will make it hard to send pictures to places like shutterbug (like my apple computer does) or not. the kindle works really fast, it's very easy and has great speakers ( unlike my old fire) it works on a different operating system for web browsing. i know because i have used both my new fire hd7 and my previous fire (1st gen) at the same time and the display is quite different. i do wish they would update the operating system in the previous gen fire.
so the drawback is that you can't access some of google's apps, like google maps, you can get facebook and most apps that people want. you can check if the app you want is assessable before purchasing by going to the apps page on amazon. you can go online and use google maps like you would on the computer. it also doesn't have expandable memory, but with the cloud that's not as important, although it would be nice. the outside of the box said something about being able to show your screen onto your tv, but it's not quite so easy. there is no hdmi port, and after reading how to do this, it only works through either a playstation or xbox ( i can't remember) which we have- but they are set up downstairs and the room we would like to use it is upstairs. it would seem it could be done some other way, as many people don't have those machines. i would like to display my skype screen on the tv so my mom could see her great grandkids while we talk and she is not going down a flight of stairs to do that. i do have the apple tv ( as well as roku) and the apple tv allows this from my mac computer. the kindle also had a fantastic price, i paid $99 for the 16 gb ( black friday sale). oh, it also now has family share, which allows you to share with one person all your books, audiobooks and apps - but not movies.
my one wish and actual recommendation to amazon is that they open up their system to the android apps. by closing their system they are actually closing out a large population of the market they are looking for. it's rather like the difference between the appletv and the roku. on the roku i can go to so many more places than on the appletv, so i only use the appletv to transmit the image from my computer to my tv, while i use the roku all the time. that said, my kindle fits my needs perfectly, works quickly without any problems and was at a price that was fantastic.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: amazon prime is not always 2-day shipping...
review_body: sooooo...i am sure this is a very nice kindle.  it will be my family's 5th kindle purchase.  this one was to replace my husband's old 1st generation one that is acting up.  i ordered it on the 3rd as part of an amazon prime order, which should be 2 day shipping.  when i first ordered it, it gave me a delivery date as the 8th.  i called and asked why i was paying for amazon prime 2-day shipping when this wasn't going to arrive for 5 days?  the rep said that was wrong, that it would be delivered on friday the 5th.  i said that's great, because my husband's kindle is not working well at all.  i got the other 2 items in that same order on friday, but no kindle.  i checked the tracking and it said the kindle had been delivered at 10:28 a.m. friday morning!!  i called cs again, and was told, \\"ohhhh, the usps delivered that.  sometimes they mark items as shipped even when they haven't been.  you'll probably get it tomorrow.  if you don't get it by monday, call back and we'll refund your money or replace it.\\"  i said, \\"i don't want my money refunded...this is a replacement for a non-functioning kindle...\\"  i was assured it would be here on time, as i pay $$ for amazon prime's 2-day shipping.  the girl said, \\"well, i can't really do anything right now...but i am sure you'll get it by monday.\\"  so there.  now, in spite of being reassured that it would be the 2-day shipping which should be guaranteed by my amazon prime membership, it is back to 5 (or more!!??) days.  update:  no kindle was delivered on monday.  called and was told i would be given priority, one-day shipping.  no kindle on tuesday.  called and was told that \\"one day shipping\\" really takes 3 days to be delivered.  now i \\"should\\" get it on the 11th.  i pay for amazon prime's 2 day shipping, and now, if it even shows up on the 11th as promised, it has taken 8 days.  fyi, i am upgrading the review to a 4, since i do like the product...as a couple of complainers here have noted, this is not really a product review,which it should be so, let me tell you, i have the same kindle myself, and i love it.  however, i am not a gamer, nor do i use it for anything other than reading books, and maybe my emails now and then.  the product is fine from my perspective.  just don't expect it to be delivered by the promised date.  maybe there's a huge run on them because they're $25 off now?  update 2:  finally received on the 11th.  item was as specified...husband is very pleased with his upgraded kindle.  i 'ignored' the comments from the posters who said this is not a device review, but is a service review...ummmm...amazon's whole business is built on service.  if they didn't provide service, good service, to their customers, they wouldn't have a business at all.  i buy a lot of stuff from amazon, and their service is the reason.  i could buy almost everything, include e-readers, from a variety of other online retailers or stores.  if an online company can't adhere to their delivery promises, that is part of the service they have offered their customers, and future customers should know that this part of their 'package' deal may not be accurate.  fortunately, in my experience, this delivery glitch rarely happens with amazon; out of my last 1,000+ orders, this is maybe the 3rd time.  they've got a great track record, and this only proves they are not perfect.  in spite of this delivery delay, my 2015 amazon orders will not decline, but will, more likely, as in previous years, equal or exceed its predecessors.  go amazon!!

those users can only open the very limited apps you can assign them. my teenagers immediately started freaking out because a bunch of the "standard" apps for them were not available through the amazon app downloader. you cannot use google play.

it worked great, and i was really wanting to love it... but we sent it back the next day when we realized how many limitations and restrictions the tablet has.

if you are not going to share this tablet. if you don't play games. if you only want to use the tablet for amazon related things, then you may enjoy the fire.

however if you want to be able to download regular apps like youtube or instagram, then don't buy this.

review_headline: love my kindle, but lifespan kills it for me. :-(
review_body:
very frustrated! i love my kindle, my hubby loves his, & my kids love to use mine. that alone would give them 5 stars in my book - i use it all the time. but in the last 2 yrs, i've purchased 2 kindles. first one began to die weeks before the 1 yr warranty expired. at first it would only work while plugged in, but then it would try to boot up, die, then reboot, die, etc. continuous cycle. after an unsuccessful hard reboot & factory re-set, amazon replaced it with a refurbished one. now the 2nd brand new kindle we bought has begun doing the exact same thing at just over a year (so past warranty). when i called support i was offered to purchase a refurbished one at a "discount". however, i could have purchased a brand new one over the past black fri weekend for less than the refurbished discount.

i really like amazon & have wanted to love my kindle. in fact i was planning to buy my son the kid's version for christmas. but i refuse to buy a new one every single year. that is ridiculous & the technology is obviously sorely lacking with amazon if that is the average life span. of course they do now offer an extended warranty up to 3 yrs, but this was either not an option when i purchased mine, or it was not readily offered, because this is the first time i've seen it.

i suppose i will now go look at ipad minis, but i'm very frustrated at all the lost content i've purchased from amazon. if you don't want apple to rule the world, you need to step it up & put out a better product. and yes, i know, i can read my books from the kindle app on my phone & laptop, but seriously, who wants to read a 700+ page book on your phone...or with a big ole' laptop balanced on you? so i will finish reading my unread kindle books on my laptop, & then amazon will not be getting anymore digital purchases from me. and i have very little reason to renew my amazon prime membership this year (especially now that it has increased to $99).

way to turn away acompletely loyal, continued repeat customer, amazon. guess i've gotta look elsewhere. :-(

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
how do i hate thee? let me count the ways:

my main complaint is that is has a proprietary browser that doesn't act like any tablet or computer. being used to using a samsung tablet and various laptops and computers, i find this thing to be counter-intuitive and hard to figure out where things live (where it downloads things to, where control panels are, where programs are, etc.).

it reminds me of windows 8, which is maybe where microsoft got the stupid idea for windows 8, which is the worst os i've yet to run across. maybe even worse than this one.

it's a bit heavier than my samsung tab 4 pro as well even though my samsung is bigger, has an sd card to expand the memory and i can connect it to my computer to add up to 128gigs of files with a 128gig sd card.

the camera isn't as good as the samsung, the chip isn't as good, and it doesn't offer as many apps as the samsung.

you say that's not a fair comparison? well it's kindle itself that is making the comparison to a samsung tablet - it just popped up as i was looking at the specs on the fire hd 7. it says it's a better deal because the samsung is $199 and the fire is now only $139 (i paid $199 for the fire hd 7, but that was a year ago and the samsung cost more then as well.

at this time the samsung tab 4 pro 8\\" tablet is $200 and the fire hd 7 is $139. for the extra $60 you get a lot more (as i mentioned above) with the samsung. bigger screen, lighter weight, sd card, ability to add files to via usb, and - most importantly - you can use chrome or ie with it so it acts like a real computer, and also it stores things in a file system very similar to a computer so it's easy to figure out how to use, whereas the fire hd is easy to use for most purposes but sometimes it's hard to figure out how it is designed, what the architecture is for filing files, programs etc.

so the bottom line for me is i don't like the fire hd, i do like the samsung tablets, and i would not recommend anyone buy this fire hd.

review_body:
i've been a long time kindle user. this is my sixth one. this new one has a lot of great features; unfortunately, i have something better to compare it to - my last kindle.

there were just several moderate to small issues with this new one that led to a comparatively unpleasant user experience. the most irritating of these was screen freezing. several other users mentioned this in their reviews, which i found today when searching to see if anyone else had the same problem.

for me, it happened 3 times in less than an hour while i was trying to listen to an audio book and play a simple connect three game at the same time. this was never an issue on my old kindle and this is a frequent activity for me.

then the screen froze again later while i was trying to watch a tv show. each of these freezes required turning the device completely off, giving it a minute and restarting it. another review mentioned it freezing while searching the web. since listening to audio books, playing games and browsing the web are what i primarily use this device for, i'm afraid i just don't trust it to perform.

the other small issues are that the battery seems to drain more rapidly and the download speed of apps and audio books seems a little reduced. on the plus side, my email experience was better and the brief amount of web browsing that i did was much improved with the new hd screen and it did seem a little faster.

overall, even though i still think this is good tablet, potentially great if they fix the screen freezing, i just prefer my old one. i told my husband i'm taking it back from him, and he gets the new one instead.

review_headline: no display mirroring on this model
review_body: i really like the look, feel and sound of this device. but i primarily bought it for display mirroring, which the amazon site clearly says is available. i looked at all the amazon help sections, read the owner's manual, and have contacted amazon about this \\"missing\\" feature. i feel like this was sort of a \\"bait and switch\\" kind of deal--i got the device during the cyber sales and thought i was getting a fully-featured device. but it doesn't look like it. instead it looks like key features are missing. it's not as if i don't know how to set up device mirroring. i've done it effectively with my kindle fire hdx and with apple products. this just appears to promise something it doesn't deliver. however, if the mirroring isn't important, the performance on this device is excellent. everything loads quickly, even the special offers aren't that annoying. but i really am missing the display mirroring and probably will have to send this back. )-:    update: the amazon help response was sort of odd. i asked several questions, but only one of those questions was really answered in the first round (what kindles actually have display mirroring.) however, i did find out that you can \\"hardwire\\" your hd7 to create mirroring display using amazon hdmi adapter for fire tablets (4th generation) and an hdmi port--if you have one--on your tv. [be careful with older kindles, the adapter doesn't work!] i am still testing to see how using the adapter affects the battery life of the fire. with the hdx and wireless mirroring, you can have the power cord attached so that you're not running the battery down while mirroring. i'm not sure that an hdmi connection, like a usb connection to a power source with other computer devices, will also power the kindle. i doubt it, but if the kindle will run for a decent length of time on battery, this may not be an issue. amazon could be much more helpful in describing how mirroring works with each device and what accessories are needed for each.

review_body:
this is the review for android users. if you have owned or own any other android devices and are looking for even a semblance of that usability, this is not the tablet for you.

tl;dr: if you use real android devices and want that functionality, move along. if want the best access to amazon entertainment sources give this thing a try.
i'm coming to the fire line from a nexus 7 2012 model that my son shattered the screen on. pointing out the obvious, fire devices run a heavily skinned "android" os that is dubbed fire os. fire os at its best is clunky and awkward, and lacks any real customizations. in the app store a lot of great apps are omitted to force use of amazon's proprietary apps. not that there aren't alternate ways to get certain apps to replace amazon's but don't expect the tablet to just adapt to your preferences. for example, i got swiftkey keyboard loaded onto the fire and was elated when it seemed that it was going to work, only to disappointed later when the my swiftkey was replaced again by the fire keyboard after a few minutes of non-use. oddly enough, the time i had with swiftkey on this device showed me just how poor the fire keyboard is. swiftkey was far more responsive and gave additional customizations, such as my favorite feature of adding a number row to the keyboard. another poorly done aspect of the fire line of apps is silk browser, which does not operate so smoothly as the name may lead you to believe. my biggest gripe with the silk browser is that it does not open links from outside sources very well. i would have to exit the browser multiple times and re-click links to get the browser to load them. fortunately, you can get dolphin browser or another browser to replace silk browser and it will maintain its default status. finally, the lack of a recent apps construct is probably one of the most frustrating downfalls of fire os. to switch between apps you literally have to go back to the home screen and select the app you're trying to switch, essentially multitasking is impossible on this tablet.

now, the good. if you're a prime subscriber and heavily invested in amazon's entertainment selection, then that aspect of this tablet will work great for you. having access to the kindle owner's library is a huge plus. the prime video functionality is nice, as i can download prime video to the tablet so i can keep up with shows i'm watching even when i'm not connected. prime music just added stations that genre/sub-genre focused. for amazon entertainment services, this thing is great but that's about all it's good for.p you're trying to switch, essentially multitasking is impossible on this tablet.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: fire hd 7 has clear audio advantages  over fire hd 6
review_body: for those of you trying to decide between the fire hd 7 vs. fire hd 6, this may help.    all i cared about between the two was the screen clarity and the sound clarity (and volume).    regarding the difference in the screen clarity, there is just a hair's advantage to the 6. not much in it at all, though. the extra pixels per square inch make a difference on the fire hd6, but not enough in my eyes to pick it over the hd 7.    regarding sound, i think the 7 has three advantages. because it has two speakers, and the 6 has but one, it gets noticeably louder. the 7 also has clearer sound to my ears (though the difference in volume between the two units is much greater than the sound clarity). perhaps most importantly, the fire hd 7 it has a speaker design advantage over the 6.    the fire hd7 speakers, when the unit is turned landscape, are located on either the top of the unit or the bottom of the unit, depending on which end you hold up toward the sky. in either case, your hand will not block the speaker (assuming you are holding it on the left and right edges, and not the top and the bottom edges).    the fire hd6, when turned in landscape mode, has the one speaker centered on either the left edge or the right edge, again, depending on which end is facing up. bottom line: when you hold the fire hd6 in landscape mode, with one hand on the left edge and one hand on the right edge, you will cover the speaker with one finger or more. it doesn't have that much of an impact on the volume or clarity of the sound, but it does have some.    if you plan to listen to the unit largely with headphones or earbuds, no big deal, as both units sound the same. the audio advantage of the hd7 really only comes into play when listening through the onboard speakers.    is it worth spending the extra money to get the better audio on the fire hd7?  i think it is. particularly if you plan to use it a fair amount without earbuds or headphones.

review_headline: detailed review of the fire hd 7 - a great entry-level tablet at a great price!
review_body:
the fire hd 7 is a great entry-level fire tablet that includes a 7\\" 1200x800 216 ppi pixel density display. pixel density wise, this is the lowest off all the fire tablets but is still decent enough where you're going to get a nice picture on the display. it's by no means an \\"ipad killer\\" or \\"galaxy tab killer\\" and you really shouldn't purchase it for that purpose. this particular model is really tailored to reading kindle books, streaming video, browsing the web, checking email, and so forth. bottom line, it's a great deal at $139. i'm going to compare the features of the hd 7 with the features of the other fire tablets to help you make an informed decision on which model to go with:

*** display ***

the display is a 7\\" 1200x800 resolution display with a 216 ppi pixel density which is not great, but not horrible either. it is the lowest pixel density of all the fire tablets with the fire hd 6 coming in at 252 ppi, the fire hdx coming in at 323 ppi, and the fire hdx 8.9 coming in at 339 ppi. the human eye really can't distinguish individual pixels beyond a density of about 300 ppi so you're not going to be getting a noticeably pixelated display by any means. all in all, this is a nice display.

*** processor, gpu, and on-board storage ***

the fire hd 7 comes with a respectable 1.5 ghz quad-core processor with enough power to run almost all of your content with ease, including smooth video playback. it comes with a mediocre 1 gb of ram which really is not sufficient in my opinion but it is what it is. this is not an ipad or galaxy tab killer by any means, but it gives you just enough power to use the essential amazon services you need.

the hd 7 is substantially less powerful than the snapdragon 2.2 ghz and 2.5 ghz quad-core processors that come with 2 gb or ram and come with the higher end fire tablets, but at the same time, those tablets cost quite a bit more ($179 for the hdx and $379 for the hdx 8.9) so you're getting what you pay for.

onboard storage is available in either 8gb (4.5gb actually available to use) or 16gb (11.6gb actually available to use.) there shouldn't even be an 8gb version in my opinion as 4.5gb of usable storage is pretty pathetic, even with cloud storage availability. i'd recommend the 16gb over the 8gb version in a heartbeat.

*** battery life ***

i say this in all my reviews, i swear, there should be a penalty for under-delivering on battery life claims. while amazon claims the fire hd 7's battery lasts about 8 hours with mixed usage, i experienced about 6 hours which included video streaming, web browsing, and downloading via wifi.

*** wi-fi and 3g service***

the fire hd 7 comes with a single band, single antenna wifi as opposed to the dual band, dual antenna mimo (multiple input multiple output) wifi that you get with the hdx and hdx 8.9. mimo technology lets you download and upload simultaneously while still allowing you to be productive on the tablet by multitasking, watching movies, etc. it is certainly a better wifi and takes advantage of the 802.11a/c wifi which is blazingly fast, but for the average consumer needs, the single band, single antenna wifi is still sufficient for downloading content, browsing the internet, and streaming video content.

neither the fire hd 7 or fire hd 6 come in a 3g version so you are limited to using wifi. honestly, i don't really see the point in needing 3g anyway as you can download content, browse the web, check email, etc. from any place with a wifi hotspot which is basically every starbucks, mcdonalds, and countless other establishments, not to mention your home wifi network.

*** camera and audio ***

the hd 7 comes with a mediocre 2 megapixel rear-facing camera which is kind of pathetic in my opinion. although you can record in 1080p, with only 2 megapixels, don't expect much in terms of picture quality. i got better pictures with a 4 year old smartphone than what the hd 7 produces. even the hdx 8.9 has an average 8 megapixel rear-facing camera so you're not missing out on much there.

audio is standard dolby audio so nothing special but it's still decent in terms of sound quality. the fire hdx 8.9 comes standard with dolby atmos sound technology which is simply amazing! you really have to hear it to appreciate it. if you simply need a standard audio experience, the dolby audio on the hd 7 is more than adequate and is by no means \\"crappy audio.\\" a good pair of headphones makes all the difference in this department.

*** weight and build quality ***

weighing in at nearly 11.9 ounces, the hd 7 does have a nice heft to it that gives it a nice, durable feel. to give you a comparison of weight, the ipad mini which is basically the same size of the hd 7, weighs in at 11.7 ounces, virtually identical in weight to the hd 7

build quality feels solid, as is the experience you'll get with the entire fire tablet lineup. none of them feel \\"cheap\\" by any means.

*** app availability ***

fire os is a forked android operating system, meaning it's a heavily modified android os so some standard android apps will work on the fire hd 7 but keep in mind, since amazon is in such a fierce competition with google and apple in terms of their app stores and music sales, fire os will not allow you to install or run any of the core google apps such as google drive, calendar, docs, slides, and so forth... even youtube, which is owned by google is banned, as is the starbucks and foursquare apps. there are nearly 250,000 apps available on the amazon app store which is pretty impressive given how young the fire os is, so you're likely to find alternative apps to satisfy your needs in this tablet.

*** conclusion ***

as is the case with any of amazon's devices including the fire tablets, fire phone, fire tv, and even the various kindle models, the more of them you buy into, the more immersed into the amazon ecosystem you become which can be good and bad. i can say, having fire tv along with a fire tablet and a fire phone, combined with an amazon prime membership is going to give you a great experience as all of the devices work together to bring all of amazon's services right to your fingertips (and television!) with a simple flick of your finger on the hd 7 or fire phone, you can send the video you're watching straight to your fire tv to continue watching it.

you can also stream all of your free video and music content across the various devices, and with the free cloud storage for all your amazon content, everything from your music, photos, videos, and documents are safely stored and available 24/7 in the amazon cloud.

all in all, this is a nice tablet but unless you're on a tight budget and need to stick to this price range, i'd really recommend jumping right up to the hdx 8.9 as it offers so much more and can legitimately replace an ipad or galaxy tab with ease, and for around the same price point. if your budget limits you to this device, you won't be disappointed with it, but it isn't going to compete with the ipad or the galaxy tab.

all in all, this is a nice tablet but unless you're on a tight budget and need to stick to this price range, i'd really recommend jumping right up to the hdx 8.9 as it offers so much more and can legitimately replace an ipad or galaxy tab with ease, and for around the same price point. if your budget limits you to this device, you won't be disappointed with it, but it isn't going to compete with the ipad or the galaxy tab.

1 star for an otherwise awesome piece of hardware? in this review, you will find out things that should keep you away from purchasing this device. i have in my household, an asus transformer, a nook, 3 hd7 2012 versions, and the 2013 hd7. the only one i'd like to throw through the wall is the new version. here's why:

1. restriction of applications to profiles is really hard to manage, and frankly doesn't work. archived applications still show up, and the interface is not intuitive. i had thought you couldn't see what was accessible, but each profile image shows up next to the applications. the archiving doesn't seem to do anything to any of the lists or access from a kindle, so removing them their was a waste of time. i happen to get several apps that after research are sketchy with hidden applications. i don't want to remove because developers fix this kind of thing all the time.

3. interface. it's somewhat intuitive, but it forces plenty of things at you from the get go, and the control of the carousel and other features is clunky compared to the simplicity of the standard android interface.

4. alternate installation of applications. i have alot of other apps which i need to load in outside of amazon. first, that process is not as easy as it could be, and they do not show up in the family profile either.

if you can get past these limitations and actually like the interface and other benefits (books & prime) that the kindle gets you, go for it. for me, i've rooted and installed kitkat on the other three devices. just waiting for a root for the new fire to get this one straightened out.

- that turns on when you press the "on" button, every time

- that lasts more than a year

- allows me to add books of any file format without jumping through hoops for 1 hour, wifi, login,upload, download, send to etc

how many people are on their 3rd, 4th or 5th version or replacement? one person wrote they are on their 8th. has the company president owned 8 kindles?

review_headline: love, love, love it... but one annoying problem
review_body: i've had my kindle for almost a year, my wonderful wife got me one for christmas 2013, and i absolutely love it.  maybe the best gift i've ever gotten, i use it every day for many things, practically a laptop substitute.  games, videos, email, social media, it does it all!  all i need is wifi, and with a hotspot on my mobile phone, i have that practically anywhere.  i have one and only one complaint.  it randomly reboots itself, on average almost every day.  it either shuts itself off, sometimes while i'm looking at it, or it requires a hard reset to power on.  this requires holding the power button down for at least 30 seconds, and it's very annoying when you're trying to just take a quick peek at email and it has to reboot (another 30-60 seconds).  but other than that, it's amazing.  small enough to fit in my inside suit pocket, but large enough to watch an episode of game of thrones.  the kindle version of some apps is a little clunky, but for the most part it does everything i want it to do and in the palm of my hand.  the "special offers" are really not that annoying, basically just a splash screen and a few notifications.  getting rid of them is cheap enough, but i really don't think they're a big deal.  the 8gb version is fine for me, but i only run about 30 apps, and some of the fancier games take up a lot of memory, so consider that when choosing which version you want.  and get an inexpensive clear screen protector, the screen gets a lot of fingerprints and abuse.  i highly recommend the device!

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: ... recollect seeing that there were 2 usb ports but disappointed that there is only one in the actual product
review_body:
when i checked the specs i recollect seeing that there were 2 usb ports but disappointed that there is only one in the actual product. the problem with only one usb port is that it is used for recharging the battery and it wears out from the continuous use. i bought two fire hdx 7 for my grandkids two years ago and although the tablet itself is of very good quality and survived the abuse, the usb port wore out in a little over one year and replacement of them is a very troubled operation that requires the technician to work under a microscope and using specialized tools generally not available in a hobbyist shop.
the usb port itself is mechanically impaired by the customization to surface mount it to the pc board. standard usb ports are mounted on pc boards via through holes which give them mechanical robustness and integrity. the kindle usb is customized to eliminate the through holes pins and is only soldered to copper traces on the board surface only which serve the dual function of providing electrical connection and mechanical strenght. this reduces both the mechanical soundness and electrical integrity of the interface. being that there is only one usb port, the dual use of it for interfacing to other pcs and to recharge the batteries which is most frequent and repeated on a daily basis, greatly reduce the product's useful life. the mechanical force required to insert and extract the charging socket into the usb port and the reduced mechanical capabilities result in early failure. therefore the otherwise very good quality of the kindle fire is greatly diminished by this simple but crucial weakness. after all a chain is only as strong as its weakest link and adding a second usb port would at least double the product's life. being that this problem was well exposed and documented in the earlier version of this tablet, shame on amazon and its engineers for not at least adding a second port to this newest version if not restore the mechanical robustness of through hole mounting. i am an ee myself so i know what i'm talking about and i also know that unanticipated weaknesses sometime do not become obvious until real life use. however once they are discovered, they must be remediated in future generations. to not do so is engineering malpractice and should be punishable by law. since that is not yet the law of the land until then my only recourse will be to not buy any more versions of this product and be negatively disposed towards any additional amazon products.
