review_headline: liked it okay before the upgrade, have had all models of the kindle fire, on the 4th gen now
review_body: adding to an old review  i am on my fourth kindle fire. i have the 4th generation now and gave my 3rd generation to my son. for some reason the battery drains extremely fast on the 4th gen. i mean as in you can pretty much watch it go. my 3rd gen does pretty well on battery life and i like that. i have turned off a lot of features, tried to turn off some other things but amazon doesn't seem to want me to get rid of them. the camera is no good but i really didn't purchase it for the camera anyhow. i have another camera. if you are purchasing this for the camera, i would go with something else. for the price, the kindle fire is decent enough. nothing fancy but it does enough. love how i can use it to pick movies and then send it to my fire stick. that's a neat feature. do not and never have liked the keyboard and really hate how it tries to guess words because it's almost always wrong. the space bar is whacked and too small. i always end up putting periods when i don't want to because of it. web browsing is a bit slow and frustrating. i wouldn't like it if a kindle fire was my only source for web browsing or email, but i have a laptop so that isn't a problem. love reading and purchasing books and watching movies with it. those are it's two best features to me. games, okay, email, okay, web browsing, not so okay but it does browse. battery life, do not like. camera, do not like. wish there were more options for parental controls. i like the idea of adding a kid profile but it's too restricted and i could not figure out a way to grant more access to things so i ended up just going with parental controls. i don't want my son to have access to my books or some of the rated r movies i own but you can't restrict that without creating a kids profile and like i said, the profile limits it too much. but the profile would be great for really young children! i would also like to be able to remove some things like firefly and the maps. i don't need or want those on my kindle andfeel like they might be part of the reason the battery drains so fast. and i do mean fast. even asleep it drains.    kindle 3rd generation: liked it okay before the upgrade. it's like going to sleep at night and waking up to find someone has completely rearranged your room. i stick with a device because i get used to using them. this new upgrade freezes and hangs so much it makes me want to throw the kindle across the room. and it makes a noise when you plug and unplug it from the charger so no more quietly using it while my husband is asleep. i have looked everywhere trying to find a way to turn that feature off. i liked my kindle for reading and light web browsing. now emails are worse than ever, the web just sits there with a black screen, some links go to nowhere. i liked it the way it was but now i have no choice but to stick with this awful forced upgrade. and i have always hated the keyboard. it makes up words and tosses them in at random. i call it kindlease.  it still stinks, too!

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: the device has a clean look and the glass appears to be sturdy and tougher than the one on previous models
review_body: this tablet has met all my expectations.    it's very light and i can hold it for long periods of time without my hands and arms getting sore.  the device has a clean look and the glass appears to be sturdy and tougher than the one on previous models. the outside plastic shell kind of provides a strange sense of hollowness when holding it, quite different to the past kindle devices. even though it feels fragile to the touch, i believe it also provides a second protection layer without the use of a case.    regardless of being used to an older, bigger-sized tablet, this 7\\" kindle display is easy on my eyes and provides an incredible high resolution. i am used to reading on a kindle e-ink device, but i must say reading on the new tablet doesn't cause as much eye strain as my other tablet. of course, for long time readings, you should choose a paperwhite instead (i had problems with two paperwhite devices but the third one worked out great and i'm now happy with it).    very fast with the newest apps and games, the little device hasn't let me down either when it comes to lagging.    movies play smoothly and there are no \\"hiccups\\" on the maximum resolution available.    speakers are louder than on previous models and work quite effectively, since they are also located on different spots now. you can get an stereo feeling even without the use of headphones. i was surprised about this.    screen touch works great, very responsive.    the firmware is always being updated and correcting possible bugs. any reported bugs are usually fixed in a timely manner.    battery life is great and lasts as advertised or longer.    one thing i miss is the ability to connect the tablet to a tv through the use of an hdmi. older kindle tablets had this feature and i believe it should be re-implemented.    overall, i'm very happy with it and i'm sure it will provide me with hours and hours of fun.    oh, and don't forget to check the special offers feature, as you will find good deals everynow and then.

the quality control of the display on this unit is apparently not very good. the first fire hd 7 that i received had was dim along the right side of the screen and especially in the bottom right corner. the replacement unit that i was shipped had the same problem but on both sides of the screen, and the backlight was inferior (dimmer, warmer toned).

the fire hd is perhaps not a bad idea if the fire user is going to be undiscerning - perhaps for children, the elderly, or other casual users. but if you want a tablet with high production standards, skip this and put some extra cash toward an ipad or something. you might even try the hdx, but i personally i would hold off on amazon tablets until they get their quality control figured out.

review_headline: great value, but parental controls are frustrating
review_body: this product has great screen resolution, connectivity to the internet, and has the ability to quickly switch between user profiles, and is far less expensive than many tablets.  the major drawbacks, however, are twofold:  first, the device's software is not as intuitive as some other e-readers.  second, the parental control options, while good, are not as flexible as they should be.  for example, the owner has to create and enter a pin code if they want to set up a children's profile.  this is problematic if you want to let your child use the device, but don't want to re-enter a pin every time the tablet is turned off or goes to sleep.  little annoyances such as these could be big problems if you are in the market to buy an e-reader that is family friendly and easy to navigate.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: not all that and a bag of chips...do your homework
review_body:
i was unaware of what "special offers" consisted of when ordering the new kindle fire. it consists of heavy marketing from the time you open it until it is closed. i open my kindle to an ad, then under each icon is a variety of apps "suggested", then in the games more ads (typically something i've recently looked up). frankly i would have paid more to not have the "special offers" had i known. i am already marketed to by every tom, dick & harry on tv & the internet...last thing i want is to be marketed to further when i am sitting down to relax with a book or game.

also, i am already a prime member so apparently i did not get the 30 day prime that was supposed to come with it. in addition to this, i have less control over my email than i had with my previous fire. you can set it to "manual", but i have yet to find out how that works exactly...there's no icon for it. i have to wait for it to refresh in 15 minutes. the quick icon for amazon is no longer there either, you have to search the internet for it. i do like the "silk"...very smooth to use. i don't have as many security pop ups as before (with my earlier fire), but then again i don't have the choices in settings i once had either.

my last complaint is that it is difficult to purchase accessories for my new kindle due to "generation" issues. this generation cover doesn't fit that generation kindle, screen protectors, replacement chargers, etc. too complicated! find a style and stick with it!

i've always liked amazon's products, service and quality....but they are getting a little sloppy on products and shipping in lieu of marketing. if the customer service goes, so will i.

overall, if i had it to do over, i would have purchased one without the special offers, and would have done more research and asked more questions about its format. other notebooks may cost a little more, but may also "have" a little more. justmy opinion.

review_headline: big improvement over the first generation fire
review_body:
i have owned a kindle fire first gen since they came out and while it still works great, more and more amazon features need a newer model to work. so i jumped on the 30 day free trial for this one.

so far i am happy with it and i am glad i went for the 16g version (since only 11g are actually available).

while there are many improvements like speed and such, the biggest plus for me is having the ability to download prime movies/shows to the device for later viewing (something you could not do with the original fire).

the biggest negative is that there are so many changes from the original fire that it takes quite a while to find things. plus amazon has so many different versions of the fire (even the 7"), that it's hard to find info on a specific model/version.

i only gave it 4 stars because there is still room for improvement in the ui. for example, on this model there is no stop button for music (only pause) and it leaves the last song/album you were playing above the notification bar (on the drop down on the home screen). not a huge deal, but perhaps people don't want others to see what the last thing they listened to.

i also failed to get flash working despite following directions posted on the net. some sites work with flash manually installed and dolphin browser, but most do not. the same sites work with the same version of flash (11.1) and dolphin on my first gen fire.

at this point i plan to keep it, as the pros far outweigh the cons. but i will also be keeping my first gen fire until it dies.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: this item could really be good, but falls short without storage and can't use android market for apps
review_body:
i did the 30 day free risk-free trial (more on that in a minute).

the unit might be nice for someone for whom this is their first 'tablet' but not if you've even had experience with even the most basic generic android tablets (i.e., less than $79 or so). the big failing of this unit is that it has no means of inserting an sd card for storage. it gives you either 8gb or 16gb (depending on which option you pick) and the o/s and other installed apps take most of the memory for the unit with 8gb, leaves you about 3gb. to give you a comparison i have a generic agptek android tablet which has nearly all the functionality of this device (less bluetooth) it cost nearly half as much, takes microsd cards for storage.

the other drawback is that you can't use google play for android apps, one is limited to the comparatively limited options of the amazon app store.

what pushed me to return it (only used it a couple of days before making the decision) is that for the price i am getting so much less - had it even had the option of an sd card i would have kept it, even though i thought the unit a tad pricey for its limitations.

if you are looking for a truly functional tablet that can store locally as well as access a cloud drive,,, this is not the unit you want.

i wanted to like this thing, but as i already said; it paled by comparison to basic android tablets in terms of options and functionality.

wanted to add that despite the 30 day free trial 'risk-free', amazon had me pay (although only $2.95) to return the unit - to me that isn't a 'risk-free' trial since i had to pay to return it.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: the only real negative is it isn't an apple ios device
review_body:
loses the first star because it isn't an ios device (see review). loses the second star because of the cheaper feel of the backing material and a not-as-pretty-or-intuitive interface.

this is a fantastic product. the display is great. the available apps are plenty useful and powerful. this is a great first-time tablet for someone who has never used an ipad/iphone. it feels solid and sturdy, even if the backing plastic does feel "cheap."

i am heavily invested in amazon prime content. i use the cloud drive for my photos (free as prime member, don't need to pay for extra storage like i do eventually with apple). i love the addition of music to prime. i read kindle ebooks. i use prime instant video. those features are great and built in. easy to use and is a great content-using device.

quite simply, the only reason i am returning this device (a potential five-star device for the right user) is because it isn't an ios device. my wife. my brother. my in-laws and the majority of my friends and family all use apple devices. we can share photo albums easily of our children. we facetime. we imessage. we play games against each other on our devices.

when using this fire device, i can't do any of those things with all of the people that i would want to do those things with.

make no mistake, this is a great product, especially for that price. it just can't be the device for me, because i've invested (and so have the people i interact with on phones/tablets) in ios devices.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
the device seems well built and not "cheap" as one might suspect given it's sub $200 price point. i purchased the device for my 8 year old daughter who is in the 3rd grade, and my only complaint is more software related than hardware.
to utilize the full features of the device such as web browsing and the camera, you must be signed in as an "adult," i will explain the problem this presents. so it has this system where you have a user profile on the device. they have two "clearance" levels for access to features on the device, one designed for adults, the other for children. the parents have significant control over content and features available to the children on their profile and this is a very useful feature. additionally, you can set time limits for different types of activities the child might engage in on the device such as: reading, watching videos, using apps. in addition to being able to set overall daily usage limits for the kindle, you can break it down even further and require the child to read for a certain amount of time before the games unlock. this is great!
however as i eluded to, my gripes with the device are related to the same child profile system that works very well in some ways, but falls short in others. specifically, the child cannot take pictures with the camera or access the internet in any capacity. my daughter has some homework assignments that have online components to them and i really hoped that she could do them on her new kindle, but this is not the case. why not just let her use the adult profile?
because adult profiles are linked in and connected to your amazon account with all types of easy ways to purchase content and products. this is no problem as an adult who can pick and choose what i would like to purchase... however, were my 8 year old daughter to be presented with 1-click shopping opportunities, my credit card would be maxed out before i even realized she had begun to makepurchases!!
consequently, in conclusion, the hardware is great for the money with a sturdy gorilla glass front and sufficient hardware "muscle" to handle all of the activities commonly associated with modern android devices. but, as with many great things, there is an achilles heel; the software package is both its greatest strength and weakness. it is fine for adults with readily accessible content and great parental controls, but the lack of online accessibility in the child's profile really makes it unsuitable for much more than elementary age kids. here's to hoping they can fix it with an update!

there goes everything.

be prepared for this when you buy a kindle fire. eventually something will happen and you are going to be forced to reset your kindle fire to factory defaults. for me it was after the latest update when all of a sudden my kindle had a new password that i didn't know. the only way to get a new password for your kindle, by the way, is to reset the device to factory defaults. now restoring your device is supposed to be relatively painless, everything is supposed to be backed up on the cloud.

it isn't.

in fact, surprisingly little is actually backed up. now, i could deal with being locked into the amazon app store, which has about 10% of the play store. i could deal with having to side load chrome onto an android device. i could even deal with many of the apps for my kids not working in freetime. but on a device that can be remotely deactivated, that has offers pushed remotely to it, that has so many of it's features based off of remote access, to have the only way to reset the password be to nuke it, that is untenable.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
to clarify: my mother purchased two of the hd 7's for her and myself this past christmas. hers is white and mine is cobalt. both were purchased without the special offers.

we both use protective cases with bluetooth keyboards as well screan protectors on our devices. that being said. lets move on with the review.

i will specifically be reviewing my personal cobalt hd 7.

i have had my hd 7 for 10 months now. i mostly use the hd 7 for my classes. i take notes on it, using a notetaking app and a bluetooth keyboard. i absolutely love the fact that it has bluetooth and that i can use a bluetooth keyboard with it. the keyboard that is actually on the tablet is not to my liking. however, i do not like keyboards on any devices except andriod phone's, as i am a bit picky. the keyboard on the hd 7 is probably fine for most. it is just a personal preference.

my hd 7 gets moderate to heavy usage. i throw it (inside a portfolio case) into my purse or backpack and carry it with me to classes, and outings such as shopping or dinner with friends. i also use it at night to watch tv shows on netflix when i don't want to use my laptop.

durability: i will start my review with the physcial tablet and its durability. i tripped one time down two steps while holding the tablet, and the tablet (inside a portfolio case) went flying across a tile floor. i was very worried, but when i picked it up it had zero cracks and zero scratches. i was extremely impressed. it was still as good as new after the incident. i have not dropped the tablet, or had any falls since. durability wise, i give the hd 7 an a +.

sound: the sound on the hd 7 is amazing. it is better than my hp laptop, and my phone. i actually have to turn the volume on my tablet down when watching movies without headphones due to it being a bit loud. overall the sound is very impressive. not only is the sound loud, but it is very crisp and does not sound garbled or warped. it's like watching a tv. sound gets an a +.

camera: this is where the review goes downhill a bit. the front facing camera is very grainy. stick to your cell phone for your selfies. however the back facing camera takes moderate to high quality photos, depending on the lighting, and the patience of the photogropher. overall, the camera on the hd 7 gets a solid c.

video quality: the quality of videos (youtube, netflix, hulu, amazon prime, and whatever else you amy use), assuming you chose the high quality button on the website you are using, the video quality is super! it is like watching any hd show on any laptop. much better than watching videos on a cell phone. video gets an a +.

speed: this one is a bit tricky. some days my hd 7 is very speedy, even faster than my phone or laptop. other days, it can be so slow that i want to throw it. i might depend on the app im using, or the wifi im using, but i have not paid enough attention to say for sure. so over all,
i'd give speed a solid b.

memory: i have the 16g version of the hd7 and i love it. i have documents, books, movies (like frozen), and many apps on my tablet. i will say that sometimes will using evernote or facebook i will get a "low memory" warning, but apparently this has something to do with the apps themselves, not the tablet (?). the "low memory" warning has never been anything more than a warning, so i've stopped paying attention to it. it is more annoying than anything. memory gets a b +!

final comments: the only problem i have is with the amazon app store. i am used to the google play and apple app stores which have a large variety of applications to choose from. having to use the amazon app store on my hd 7 severly limits my app choices, as some of my favorite apps are not available in the amazon app store. hopefully that will change in the future. as for music, books, tv shows, and movies. amazon has me covered!

final grade? a solid b! its the perfect tablet for me and my lifestyle. if you are somone who plays a lot of games or apps this may not be for you. but if you like videos, tv, and using a tablet for schoolwork instead of lugging around a heavy laptop, then this tablet is a top pick! it is cheaper than most other competeing tablets, but works a high grade level!. having used both andriod and apple products, makeing the switch to the amazon os was a bit strange, but once you get the hang of it, you will love it! it is well worth the buy!

review_headline: i thought the kindle apps on my android/windows tablets were good enough, boy was i wrong
review_body:
i've been resisting buying a kindle fire because the kindle app on my android/windows devices does a great job (or so i thought). but the price was too low to resist, so i decided to buy it. boy am i glad i did. fantastic sound, good / fast camera, and the reading experience is just better--where better = faster and more features. for example, i bought a guitar tab book several months ago and the sound simply didn't play on the kindle app on my android/windows tablets. however, it plays just fine on my kindle fire. couldn't believe i was missing out on the sound track and the backing track. wow. and the contrast between the text and background is much much crisper on the fire than on the kindle apps. playing music is fantastic. loud with a nice bass. much better than my nvidia tegra 7 tablet, which is supposedly the ultimate gaming tablet. haven't played any games yet, but i'll update this when i do. music and videos are crisp despite the 1280x800 display. i thought not having 1080p would be a problem, but somehow amazon has the contrast and colors to make the extra resolution not worth the $100+ you have to pay for the next level of the fire.

bottom line, buy it. you won't be disappointed. and if you're a prime member you get all those free movies and music!

also, i bought the \\"built scatter dot slim sleeve case\\" which i so prefer over all those plastic folding things, hate um! fits the hd7 nicely!

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
i believe it should be mentioned if not emphasized that the kindle fire can not function without an initial wi-fi connection to "register" it. i am still wondering what the "special offers" are as it is part of the description. the kindle fire came with a charger/ usb adapter. it should be noted that the charger portion that connects to the outlet gets very warm/hot. the cord is approximately 40 inches, so be ready to use an extension cord or be sold an accessory. the home page has many icons linking to services such as music, newsstand, goodreads, that cannot be removed so the portion of storage that is used by these things cannot be freed up. i believe the storage available for the consumer to utilize as they choose should be the advertised storage space. i put a child's profile in and put on a screen unlock password, now i cannot remove the password feature which is extremely frustrating when trying to quickly use the camera in order to not miss a shot. in the game apps store, the browsing is incredibly frustrating because once you've read a description and try to return to browsing, the apps order is changed so that you're likely to re-browse apps and/or miss some because the order is shuffled slightly every time. it also bears mentioning that the apps you enjoy on your phone may not be available for the kindle fire. additionally you may have apps that require updating, but if they aren't listed in the update section allotted you cannot update them period. while i appreciate the notification bar for email, facebook, and games i continually receive notifications that aren't described. for example, i'll have a circled 1 in the bar and when i pull down the shade it is blank. i am left wondering what triggered the notification; is there a system problem, an update, or is it a programming glitch? i may never know.
i believe the kindle fire is well constructed. the smoothness of operation and versatility of this machine is remarkable. i love thatmy phone calendar is synchronized with my kindle fire, my contacts are as well- in case of phone loss or accidental factory reset. the cloud space provided is adequate for my purposes and more is available for purchase. after i had internet installed, i have logged over a hundred hours on my device and it has frozen only once. it has provided: a portal to the world that i did not have before, entertainment, relaxation and supplemental educational activities for my son. other than the abovementioned concerns this is a fabulous device.

review_headline: what to expect? ...you really get what you pay for
review_body: i thought it was a good buy based on the specs comparison between the galaxy tab 4 and fire hd 7, the reality is that the os is sluggish, hard to get familiar with. the unit feels rather heavy, and overall  it feels cheap (specially the back of the unit, like low quality plastic). there are a couple of things that i liked: the speakers sound really loud and clear and the fact that you can download "some" videos for free to watch when no wifi is available, unfortunately the (very) limited selection of videos available at amazon to download for free does not justify the $180 (after tax with no special offers). another disappointment is the camera, believe me i'm not expecting a ultra hd camera for a $180 tablet, but the camera quality is really really awful. another annoying thing is the fact that it doesn't have a home button, so if you want to "awake" the tablet you have to actually press the power button that is rather small, its not that hard to find it, it's just that it goes against of what people are used to. and the last but not least disappointment is the fact that is not expandable as the galaxy tab, now days 8gb are nothing if you rent/download 2 hd movies you will run out of space, so no space for music or anything else....needless to say this fire its on its way back for refund.

review_body: update    i just upgraded my kindle fire from the original fire to the new kindle fire 4. i actually got the blue kindle fire 4, didn't realize i wrote this under the black product name but i'll assume the color has nothing with how it works. i'm still working my way through this new device and although it may not sound like it i do like my new kindle i'm just trying get used to the difference between what i've had for so long.    for those of you considering the new kindle fire (4th generation). here are my observations. -warning this is pretty lengthy.    1. i've seen and handled both the 6\\" and the 7\\", in my opinion that extra inch does matter. the 6\\" can be compare to the samsung note 4 roughly in size for a tablet. the 7\\" is (i'll assume) the same size as the 3rd generation 7\\", in comparison to the original fire it is lighter, and much thinner. the color is brighter and the icons on the carousal appear larger to me.    2. the new features include, front and rear cameras, bluetooth ability (i assume that generation 3 has that), it claims a faster processor, which i guess is relative depending on your wifi connection. i don't notice much of a speed difference between this and the original, but i do notice a battery issue (i'll discuss that later), it comes in 5 different colors (black, white, yellow(citron) , navy blue (cobalt), pink-(magenta- at least it looks like that to me). i can't remember if the original fire came in a 16 gb or if it had \\"special offers\\" but this one does (i'll discuss that later), volume controls on the outside, five new drop down menus,-shop, a games drop down menu (don't know why i have a games drop down menu and an apps drop down menu), audiobooks (i'll discuss later), photos and offers. you can also adjust the font size for the homepage-not something i remember being able to do on the original. they also have a free time for the kids and a quiet time i guess for the adults. the family share feature i'm not quite sure the purpose for it. i've not tried the feature that let's you watch a movie by \\"flinging\\" it to your tv. sounds interesting but i'm thinking i need some accessory to make that happen.    3. now for my concerns with the new kindle-battery life-it almost non-existent if you use the wifi alot. i called amazon about this issue because i thought my device was defective. with my original i never had to worry about my battery going down while i was in wifi mode (i also didn't have an airport mode either, so maybe that's why) all i do know is that inorder to save battery life you have to constantly flip between airport mode on/off, on your device to save the battery life and for it to charge completely. a real hassle considering what all you have to do to get to the airport mode to turn it off and on. it doesn't matter if you keep you devise plugged in while in wifi mode because it still won't charge completely unless you have the airport mode on (wifi off). also just a ticky issue for me-i miss my charging light, with original fire when you plugged it in if the light was orange then you knew it was charging and once the light turned green you knew you device was close to being fully charged. now with the new kindle fire you have to look for this very tiny, battery icon and look on it for an even smaller lighting bolt to determine if the device is charging (not good for people with sight issues) as you can see, this is a major issue for me.    4. as discussed earlier my issues with the \\"special offers'. the advertising makes it seem as if you only see these ads when your device powers down and are like screen savors, what they don't tell you is that the ads are everywhere. i did not know that i would get \\"recommendations\\" for every icon on my carousal (not something on the original-but then i didn't have \\"special offers\\" on my first kindle), unless you again go into the settings and hide the recommendations. i also, consider it over kill to have both a shop and offers drop down menu (a petpeeve of mine), with the help of a very helpful amazon rep, i was able to \\"hide\\" the recommendations for every icon on my carousal i was so bothered by the \\"special offers\\" and \\"recommendations\\" i considered sending the device back and paying the extra $20 just so i don't have deal that, who knows i may still do that, it might also improve my battery life.    5. audiobooks drop down menu-helpful, no longer need to download audio app to listen to audiobooks, that said i am having a difficult time closing out of my audiobooks. you can't just close the book you have remove it from your device (not a issue with the original fire). you can stop the recording but it doesn't close the book, an it drains the battery because you can't close the book.    6. apps. i'm also discovering that not all my old apps work on the new device. i'm not looking forward to purchasing the same apps over. i guess it's a good thing that i only gave the old one to my son so i can use that app again if i want to. another ticy issue of mine-i'm not a fan of the layout where you go to shop for apps and it doesn't matter which one you go under- games or app drop down. it used to be left side pay apps, right side free apps, now they're all mixed up and everywhere, more annoying than anything for me.    7. camera-from what i can tell, it takes a nice enough picture. i just don't know how hard it will be to make \\"hard\\" copies or possibly download the pictures to a computer. i was surprised that you can take pictures without wifi, so that's a plus.    so for now that's all i've observed. i'll update as i continue to find new things with my new device.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body: this is my second kindle fire hd 7, my first was the 3rd generation (this one is the 4th gen). my last one was stolen, otherwise i would never have thought of replacing it because it was fantastic! the only complaint i had about my other fire hd was that it was the 8gb version, which fell short on memory. my new fire is the 16gb version and for what i am using it for it is plenty. i have loaded 3 different versions of the game gta on it, about 25 apps and still have about 4 gb free. on the old one, i could only load one version of the game along with a few small apps and it was full. my point is for the extra few dollars it is well worth the extra 8 gb of ram.    i absolutely fell in love with my first kindle despite the memory limitation complaint. i had it for about a year and experienced nothing but solid performance and good value from it. as far as this new hd7 goes, it kicks butt! it has a much faster and smoother processor/gpu and includes both front and rear-facing cameras with 1080p video capability on the rear one. the previous generation lacked both cameras and had no mic, making this a welcome addition.    the lcd screen on the new generation is beutiful, clear and very bright! the audio quality is simply amazing. you can play music at full volume and it is clear, rich and quite loud; to be honest it is surprising any tablet could sound so good, especially a budget model.    battery life is excellent. i seem to get between 7-9 hours on a charge but not so if the screen brightness is at maximum which isn't necessary because full-bright is almost too bright. it takes a while to charge with the included ac adapter. if you don't mind waiting 5-6 hours for a full charge the included charger is fine, but i do mind so i will be purchasing a higher capacity charger which should cut that time in half.    if you are looking for a lot of bang for your buck, in my opinion this tablet wins over all the others hands down. the build quality is excellent and the interface and included feautures are well done. yes, there are better tablets out there but not until you start getting into the $300 range. you won't be disappointed with this model - i am glad the other one got ripped off! :)

review_headline: great android tablet for the money.
review_body:
i wanted a tablet for the following:
1. wifi-enabled, no need for 3g or anything like that
2. web-browsing
3. movie-watching when on-the-go
4. facebook
5. miscellaneous hobby apps
6. not too pricey
7. quality construction backed by a company that will be around in a year's time

the kindle fire hd 7" appeared to fit the bill. and sure enough, it does. the only tiny pain point i had with it was connectivity to windows xp (yeah, i know - old school). i could not get my windows xp system to recognize it as a valid portable device. until, that is, i realized i needed to disable adb (the android debugger) in the kindle. and with this model, it is not intuitive and not obvious from any of the menus. what you need to do is tap seven times on the software version number, then the additional developer's menu will become visible. and from there you can disable adb (which comes enabled by default in this model). after i did that, my windows xp system immediately recognized it. this was not an issue with windows 7.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
i wanted to wait a while to write my review because i wanted to make sure that i became completely familiar with it. i can understand why people don't see the power adapter right away. my wife got into mine before i got my chance at it. she thought it was missing too. it looked like part of the packing.

the only real problem i had was when a game took control of it and wouldn't let it go. i finally turned it completely off and turned it back on. i removed the game from the device but was not able to remove it from my cloud storage, maybe my ignorance. i'm still that familiar with cloud operations,

certainly everything else is on the positive side. i was afraid that the 8gb might not be enough, but it is very adequate. then again, i don't store a lot of movies and audio on it. the screen is very clear and crisp, though some of the pseudo buttons are a bit small for my big digits. size adjustments, such as print, is simple and intuitive.

i purchased the original kindle years ago and i used the text-to-speech to listen to books during the 30 minute trips to and from work. so i was a little concerned if i would have the same convenience with the new one. not only is the text-to-speech still there, but the voice is much nicer and smoother.

i guess i do have one more complaint. i'm not a game fanatic. there are thousands available, but all i wanted was the old standard of solitaire and chess. the card game i loaded was a nightmare. it seemed i was assaulted by ads every few seconds so i deleted it, though not completely. the chess will be the last game i load.

review_headline: battery life is bad, kindle is awesome!
review_body:
recently my kindle broke for some unexpected reason. no physical damage or liquid was applied to it but it turned black and would not turn on. i panicked, called amazon, and explained to them my situation. in the end they decided to give me a free refurbished kindle because of one year warranty that comes with the purchase.

the first thing i noticed was the color; very vibrant. it took 5 seconds to turn on, and it set me up very fast (connected me to the wifi, registering me to my amazon account, time, date, etc.) when i turned it on, the battery was at 73%. without connecting to the wifi, you cannot download apps, pend your books, or upgrade your kindle. this is a good device for people just beginning with apps. i'm quite disappointed in their appstore; doesn't have many popular apps.
about the battery life, even if it is in low brightness, it still takes around ten minutes for it to go down 5-10%. the camera is decent quality for a tablet. you can't take fast-moving objects' or high quality pictures with it. i can kind of fit this kindle on my hand, and it's really handy because it can fit in all of my purses and bags. there is good quality sound, the speakers are loud, and it is excellent for listening to music with your headphones.
what i loved was that you can create, download, and view a word, powerpoint, and/or excel document with this. you can save them to your files on the kindle. it is very convenient that you can download anything (from ur pc) to this kindle: pictures, documents, etc
also, you get one month of amazon prime for free and when you immediately get 500 amazon coins to spend on apps, books, and other stuff. (500 amazon coins= 5 dollars)
overall, awesome buy!!.....for the price ;)

review_headline: you get what you pay for!
review_body: i was in the market for a tablet, and when i came across the fire hd i was amazed at how cheap it is.  i decided to give it a try and was very disappointed.  for someone who has an android phone and have used an ipad in the past, i maybe had high expectations.  when i got the device i thought it was very cute, and was excited to use it.  once i got the thing running i was surprised to find how limited it is compared to other tablets in the market.  there was no option to stream it to my apple tv.  you had to find an app that allows you to do this and even then it was completely limited.  i couldn't believe that there was no option to use chrome as your browser! i even tried to download the app and they didn't have it in the store. you are basically forced to use the built in browser, which was very annoying since i have all my bookmarks in chrome. i am a huge fan of kindle/amazon as i only use my kindle to read my books, but my current kindle is the touch which doesn't have a color screen.  as a kindle book reader this device would be great, but i don't recommend you buy this as a tablet. the interface itself is not easy to use.  i hate that you can't customize the device.  maybe i made the mistake of not paying extra for the ad free version, but i like to feel like my device is personal by being able to pick my own photo for the lock screen and background screen and there was no option for this. i had to return it and will likely be buying a samsung tablet instead.

review_body:
so far so good! this is my first time purchasing a kindle or a tablet for that matter. i think the biggest thing to acknowledge is understanding what your needs are prior to purchasing. i wanted something to primarily read books with the option to surf the net, check some emails and maybe watch a few videos and not as the go to tablet. it has been really great to use so far. reading on it is not bad at all and i can everything that i need.

i'm not giving it an absolute 5 because it does crash every once in a while so there are clearly a few more kinks to work out but other than that, it fits my needs thus far. i think if i want to get more functionality with a variety of apps, i will look into getting an ipad or something else. this tablet is not meant to be the end all be all for tablets which is why amazon offers two more higher quality and more expensive options so i think the comparisons and unrealistic requests aren't fair for this model. it seems more research is needed in those cases.

overall, it is a good tablet that allows you to do the primary things on a tablet like reading, web surfing (you can bookmark your popular pages), video streaming and core/basic apps. i have yet to explore in detail the music because i use a different format there but i have gotten everything else that i needed with work needs, reading documents,etc. good choice for a first tablet.

review_body: got this just three minutes ago. fully charged, but plugged it in. the first thing i checked after downloading netflix was the sound. very low sound compared to the previous kindle fire hd. i compared the sound with my old one and my old one overpowered it. to be sure it wasn't just a weird version of netflix, i decided to download one of my songs from the cloud. it paused over and over as it struggled to play. remember - i literally just got this device. typing as i am going through the options. so far, my bought videos and tv shows don't show - it only leads me to the amazon store with no option to download my previous purchases. finally found three tiny lines on the left side with options - my videos are hidden in there (thanks for making it so user-friendly). the battery dropped from 99 to 87% within nine-ten minutes. not sure what's eating up the battery this fast, but okay. attempting to download one of my film purchases and the d/l speed is really, really slow. fire hd 2013 was super fast. this tablet is a lot thicker than the 2013 model, smaller speakers though. the camera takes grainy photos. well, this is pretty disappointing. i wanted to upgrade, but it appears i've downgraded. nothing i play on youtube or from my song library plays without major pausing/skipping. anyone else experience this?

review_headline: design flaw - gave me a shock
review_body:
i got my kindle as a gift. i wasn't sure i wanted one, but now i'm a fan. i am enjoying its lightweight portability for reading books, browsing the web and playing a few games. it was very handy during a recent trip.
however, i it has a serious design flaw that gave me a shock. when i pick it up and turn it on, i have to wait a bit for it to fire up. during this time, the very shiny black screen makes a fairly good mirror. looking downward into a mirror held at chest height, a 50-ish-year-old woman suddenly becomes aware that she has somehow acquired an old lady neck. imagine my shock! this is surely an optical illusion because i never noticed this before in any of my regular mirrors. amazon should consider adding a warning screen advising users hold the kindle slightly above chin level in the standard "selfie" position during power up, to avoid a nasty shock like the one i got.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body: i loved this product until it stopped working correctly.  i am now on kindle #3,  my original and two reconditioned.  on all three the screen would go black, come back on, go black again, and the come on - usually at a different place place on whatever site i was on than before the screen going black.  this latest one goes one better.  after going black twice i end up on a totally different site.  i am so tired of calling repeatedly, always having to explain everything from the start, that i will just suffer with it till i can get a different product.  it was only about 7 months old when all this started.  now, almost a year, it's still not fixed.  part of the problem is the kindle, and part is customer service.  i can speculate that my reconditioned kindle had the same problem, but since it doesn't show up on a schedule, they were deemed in good condition, and sent out a gain.  so disappointed with the whole experience.

review_headline: great device, but why aren't my old kindle games compatible?
review_body: after just a few hours with my newest generation kindle fire 7 hd (16 gb).  i will tell you it's fast, easy to set up and beautiful.  if you've had other versions of the kindle you will be able to jump right in rather quickly and feel right at home.  the main reason i'm even writing this review is to warn customers of the current lack of app support.  yes there are "thousands" of apps out there, but many of my old kindle apps are not compatible with the new fire, specifically games.  stranger still is many would seem to benefit from the more powerful tablet.  games such as asphalt, duke nukem 3d and nba2k15 (among many others) are not compatible!  new games to show off the device are not out there as of this writing (granted it's the day it came out).  i have no doubt things will improve with time.  but if you're someone like me who was anxious to show off the new device, you'll probably be disappointed  if your a gamer.  otherwise, i believe you'll love it.

review_body: a few days ago i was faced with a problem that i didn't know how to solve. the kindle fire i ordered had supposedly been delivered to a local lockbox. however, i was never sent the code to open the box. i didn't know what to do. the \\"where's my stuff?\\" menu didn't deal with my issue. i posted a negative review here, hoping to get somebody's attention.    it worked. i want to thank everyone who suggested i contact amazon customer service. the issue was quickly resolved once i got on a chatline with a representative. she was excellent. she discovered that ups had made a mistake and delivered the package to the wrong address. it had been scanned incorrectly, which was why i received a delivery notice but no lockbox code. she guaranteed that my package would be delivered within 24 hours. as it turned out, i received the delivery notice and the lockbox code within two hours. i have the fire. my son-in-law-has his birthday present. i'm very pleased.    thanks again to those of you who offered suggestions and support.    i changed my 1 star to 4 stars. it would have been a 5, except for another issue. customer service is great--if you know how to find and access it. right now it's tucked away at the bottom of the webpage. you can got through several menus and still not find what you need. i think the \\"where's my stuff?\\" menu should offer a link that takes you directly to customer service. that would have saved me time and several panicked moments.    all told, a little rough at the beginning, but amazon made everything right in the end. i'm completely satisfied.

as for the tablet uses, it does fairly well on the web, but at times its' 1gb ram does show its' limits. since i will use it mostly for reading, web surfing, some multimedia content and some undemanding games, i can live with the very low storage space, without microsd card compatibility, little ram and decent processor.

i'm just getting started with this thing. i love the camera(s) feature, the video feature, and the various apps that are available. i don't really use the email feature ... i barely check my email on my laptop!

review_headline: finally, a tablet that i can leave my ipad behind for
review_body:
i am absolutely stunned.

let me give you a little background history.

i am an apple guy. i am talking about imacs, macbooks, mac minis, ipads, and definitely iphones (owning the recently released iphone 6).

as a person obsessed with new tech, i always want to try something new. the major disadvantage of the ipad is the close ecosystem (i.e. it's apple's way or the highway). now i've tried every kindle version that has come out....i have always quickly returned them due to their clunky \\"gutted\\" versions of android os (a great idea for phones, especially with the open system, but between the choppy video, os freezes, etc, i returned the 10 or so android tablets i've had as well) and the fact that imo they simply didn't measure up to the ipad's i've owned.

until now.

the kindle hd 7 4th generation...amazon may have finally gotten it right.

now, i've only had it for 72 hours. but the 3 prior versions of this tablet, it was usually packed up and back on its way to amazon due to the \\"clunky\\" execution i explained earlier.

but with their \\"sangria\\" os (the gutted version of kit kat), as well as the quad core processor they put in this thing....this is truly the best android-esque tablet i've ever used.

and the first one i will actually keep and use.

once it boots up, it simply runs...smooth. i can't describe it any other way. games are crisp and fun to play and view. video playback on websites (a major point with me; i felt that android tablets/kindle tablets couldn't hang with ipads) is so vastly improved, i actually used the tablet more this weekend than i did on my macbook or my iphone 6. this thing simply worked quite well out of the box. its as if amazon went through the first 3 gens as test runs, and may have finally built a 7 inch tablet that apple users might say \\"hey, perhaps i don't have to drop $400 and up on a portable link to the world.\\"

the build quality is much better than the previous gens. now yes, as this is a \\"non\\" apple product, the resale value ain't gonna hold. but i don't feel that things won't fall apart if i spend several hours on this thing.

sitting in a dark room, the picture (especially with video) is nice, without much in terms of the famous \\"light bleed.\\" it is a solid product, doing what it is supposed to do without the bells and whistles.

about the only bad thing is that due to it's build materials, it is a big time fingerprint magnet. that can be rectified with a cover, however.

i am so impressed, i may actually look to upgrade up to the fire hdx 8.9 when it comes out later this month, giving this tablet to my boy.

kudos, amazon. well done.ple product, the resale value ain't gonna hold. but i don't feel that things won't fall apart if i spend several hours on this thing. sitting in a dark room, the picture (especially with video) is nice, without much in terms of the famous \\"light bleed.\\" it is a solid product, doing what it is supposed to do without the bells and whistles. about the only bad thing is that due to it's build materials, it is a big time fingerprint magnet. that can be rectified with a cover, however. i am so impressed, i may actually look to upgrade up to the fire hdx 8.9 when it comes out later this month, giving this tablet to my boy. kudos, amazon. well done.

review_headline: it’s a shame because i really like the hardware
review_body:
i picked up an amazon fire hd 7 on a whim and i just figured it was an android tablet with their ui and such on it, along with the average level of lockdown. i didn’t realize they actually ship a fork of android with every bit of google infrastructure removed and go above and beyond to keep the device locked down.

it’s a shame because i really like the hardware. it’s a bit heavy but feels sturdy. the os runs smoothly and under the expected use, i imagine it would continue to do well.

it’s just that, there’s plenty i have on google’s cloud that i’d like to be available for a given tablet to be most useful. not having calendar and contacts i can sync with my phone (note it’s not a fire phone), is core competency as far as i’m concerned. not all play apps are on amazon app store, and while i can sideload some, a lot of functionality is broken without google services framework on the system.

and while i’m sure the device will eventually be cracked somehow, i don’t think it’s worth it to worry about blocking updates, keeping it cracked/rooted, and maintaining a patchset or entirely new rom on it just to keep basic apps running.

i get that they sell them at a loss and want to lock buyers into the amazon ecosystem in order to recoup that, but i’d have bought media from amazon whether i was locked in or not, so for me the broken os is such a deterrent they’ve entirely lost my potential purchases from having a device i carry with convenient amazon integration. it's just not well suited to a user like me.

review_headline: a great upgrade for me from an older kindle fire!
review_body:
[[videoid:mop3b6gs5rl8ly]]i purchased the original kindle fire in 2011 and the second generation kindle fire in 2012. i gave my original one to my grandson and he is still using it for apps and reading. i liked both of them and i have to tell you that they have held up very well. one is over 3 years old and the other is 2 years old and i have not had any issues with them. since i have not upgraded in 2 years i thought i would get a new one with a larger memory and a faster cpu and a higher resolution display. there are many improvements beyond even those features.

i have to tell you that overall i am impressed with this new one. i didn't feel the need to purchase a kindle fire every year and when i purchased the next one i wanted it to be a definite upgrade step to what i had. i stayed with the 7 inch size as i like to portability and weight for long term reading. i alternate between the kindle paperwhite for reading in the daytime and at night sometimes and i use the kindle fire for reading in the evening and at night plus browsing the internet and getting email. this new kindle fire hd 2014 version is very fast and easy to use. setting it up for the internet and downloading my apps and books was a breeze. i like the fact that the larger memory allows me to carry more apps and books. the higher resolution of the screen is helpful in reading books as the text is clearer and easier on my eyes than the older kindle fires we own. the screen is better for playing apps and watching videos and movies and it is worth the upgrade from the older kindle fires.

i like that this version has both a front and rear facing camera. i use the camera a lot on all of my tablets and i own many apple ipads, apple iphone and android tablets. the camera is just handy for that spontaneous photo or video and i take a lot of them.

i also like the fact that the stereo sound output has been improved as i listen to a lot of books. i use the text to speech feature a lot and i also use the audible book feature a lot. when amazon sells the audible version of the book at a good price when i buy the kindle version of the book i usually get both. i like to use bluetooth to stream the audio book to my car's stereo system and listen to the book while i drive, especially on a long trip. my wife and i enjoy listening to books together. this hd tablet pairs with my car and i can now use it instead of using my ipad or using my iphone. this feature keeps track of where i am in the book regardless of whether i am reading the book or listening to it with audible. the better speakers and louder volume is also nice when watching movies.

the unit works well handling my emails and it makes it nice that i can switch from browsing, to emails to reading or playing an app on the same tablet. i also have amazon prime so i can watch tv shows or movies. this is a good tablet with a lot of flexibility. i am still not a fan of the push ads but i am so used to them now i just ignore them.

i won't discuss all of the specifications but i did include a table comparing the original kindle fire to the first kindle hd 2013and now the kindle hd 2014. for me it was a quantum leap to go from a kindle fire first or second generation and i am glad i made the jump. this tablet is a good buy for the money as the specs are very good. the table below shows the differences between the different versions and you can see the progress that has been made in just a few years. i am buying this new kindle with confidence as my last two kindle fires have performed very well and i expect the same out of this one.

one word of caution is that if you are buying this for a child then make sure to pay attention to the parental controls. turn off the ability to make in app purchases (iaps) and i also turn off 1 touch buying. it is so easy for a child to make in app purchases and some of them can be as much as $99.99 on one item. children are used to playing games with fake money and they cannot tell the difference and you will be surprised when you get the massive credit card bill. a few minutes of proper set up of the tablet for use by a child can save you a lot of headaches in the future.

there are a couple of features that i do wish were in this product that i miss. i own and have tested many tablets and i love the ability of android tablets to accept a micro sd card memory addition. i even have some tablets that i use 128 gig sd cards in and this is a great feature. a very good micro sd card only cost $100 and if amazon would add this feature this very good tablet would be a great tablet. the second feature is the ability to easily use apps from the google play store. most of the office and game apps are on the amazon play store and i really do like the amazon play store the best. there are though some powerful tools on the google play store that will not work on the kindle fire operating system and that is a shame. this limits the customer from being able to use the best available software available. this kindle fire hd 2014 is a wonderful top notch product but it would be a superior product if these features were included.

if you are upgrading from a first or second generation kindle fire then this is a great move. for someone that has the 2013 kindle fire hd this is a smaller leap in technology so you may have to really want one of the new features to upgrade. i like my new unit and i am glad that i got it. i am also glad that it came with the ac wall charger in the box. i rated it at 5 stars and recommend it based on the results i have seen so far. if you have any questions please send me a comment and i will try to answer you.

review_body:
i'm writing this review with the benefit of being an experienced kindle fire user vs. someone brand new to the kindle family. in summary, for $139 you are getting a good deal on a tablet computer - especially if you compare it to the $500 or more you can spend on a wi-fi version of the ipad. overall, if you consider the price and the functionality i think this is a great tool / toy if you watch a lot of video or play a lot of games on your device: the video quality is outstanding and you can really tell a difference between this and last year's fire. if you are a first-time tablet buyer, where price vs. value is a key consideration, or if you are looking for an affordable tablet for the kids, i'd recommend this \\"regular\\" fire hd vs. a more expensive version. if you're comparing last year's hd model to this version and it is operating fine, i'd say save your money and continue to get your money's worth out of that one.

my review below compares a lot of the features of this version of the fire to last year's fire hd but also some of the features for a first-time user.

consistent with my experience with setup of previous models of the fire, setup took a while: despite being a brand new product, the fire attempted to download and install several operating software updates. you just need to be patient while it downloads and installs.

screen display / video playback:

this version of the fire has a great screen display and looking at the technical specs amazon made some major changes in the display / resolution, and the picture appears more crisp: i compared the viewing experience watching an episode of the lost ship. the display on this fire was one heck of a lot better in terms of sharpness than last year's model. that may be a combination of some better technology as well as a new vs. year-old screen.

wi-fi connectivity:

after the final operating software update i mentioned above, it was fairly easy to connect to the internet via wi-fi. my standard test for trying out new gadgets is to see how fast they run side-by-side with a known piece of equipment doing the same test at the best place of wi-fi in my house and the worst place where it drags. in this comparison, i had this version of the fire sitting next to last year's version of the hd fire, as well as last year's 8.9\\" hdx fire, and my ipad air (yes, the kindle guy uses an ipad for work), all just using a wi-fi connection vs. cellular connectivity.

my \\"normal\\" website test is to hit the mobile websites of foxnews, cnn, my personalized yahoo page, google, and the houston chronicle. the ones that were usually slow on the other devices were just as slow, and for the other sites i couldn't tell a difference in speed in comparison to this model. downloading the lost ship mentioned above from the amazon site, strangely, tool a lot longer than any of the other fires in my comparison - about ten extra minutes.

sound / music playback:

the two speakers are located in the back of the fire in two not-noticeable ports: both of them are on the right (or maybe it's on the top, depending upon your screen orientation) side of the kindle. my test of this feature was cranking up van halen's panama to maximum volume (i always want to see if it could really play the guitar licks), and i would alternate covering one speaker up over the other: you have true stereo sound with no degradation of the sound that makes you think you are about to blow the speaker. the dolby speakers sound nice but \\"cranking\\" is misleading as it's really not that loud: you do get to hear the bass if you install and use an equalizer app and adjust until it sounds \\"just right\\" to you. mixing the sound with an equalizer app, and using good headphones, it really the way i want to listen to music on the fire as you not only have a better sound experience but you're also not disturbing others in the room. the x-ray feature ispretty neat as it displays the lyrics on the screen if you are so inclined; if you are not, it is as simple as the tap of an icon to make the lyric feature go away.

email setup:

consistent with previous versions of the fire, email setup was very easy for my main gmail account, both with the software came with the fire but my primary use of an existing app called enhanced email i purchased here in the amazon app store. i did setup the email app that came with the program with no problem - it took about a minute to set it up. amazon made more enhancements to their email product, so i have deleted the third-party app and am happy with amazon's email client.

new tabs and screen layout:

in addition to the normal tabs amazon has continued to make tweaks with the look and feel to the overall display such as more things to scroll through to find what you are looking for in an easier manner. consistent with my experiences with last year's model of the fire hd, i purchased the one with special offers and i don't feel overwhelmed with ads. in fact, i don't even notice them.

reading books:

turning pages is pretty darn easy - just tap the side of the screen to go to the next page or back a page, or you can swipe your finger across the screen to do the same. you do have the feature to see the book's description for books on your device like they have with the e-ink kindle which is a plus as i can't remember what each book in my digital to-be-read pile is about; getting to the book description, requires several taps on the screen to eventually get to where you want to be. if there is an easier way to do it, i can't find it.

camera:

there is a camera on this model - one facing the back and one facing the front or toward the user / reader. focusing and taking a picture is pretty easy, and amazon will by default store your pictures in the cloud. i'm not much of a picture taker with my tablet, so i can't really comment on the quality.

charger:

unlike previous models of the fire, this one does include a charger! if you're scratching your head with that comment, in previous models you had to purchase a charger separately for $20 which always seemed kind of silly for amazon to do.

if you've never owned a tablet before, or are looking to upgrade from an earlier model fire, i would recommend this one if video and apps are your thing - but make sure you purchase the higher memory one vs. the minimum 8 gb if you can afford the extra dollars as you will see better performance. if you're comparing last year's hd model to this version and it is operating fine, or looking for a tablet for your younger children, i'd say save your money and continue to get your money's worth out of it.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_headline: even grandma has it figured out!
review_body: i purchased this kindle for my grandma, because i wanted a simple way to video chat with her. our old process was pretty complicated: first, she had to turn her computer on, sign into skype, call me to let me know that she would like to skype and that she was online, then answer my incomming request. since she is retired and has lots of time, this was okay for her, but didn't work well for me, since i was often unavailable when she wanted to skype.    she now has a kindle that she keeps in the living room, and i can send her a skype request directly to the device. this works great for me, because she's always online, which means we can video chat during my breaks at work. i recently moved to utah, and broke grandma's heart, but she feels closer to me now that we can see eachother face to face.    in addition to how easy it was to get this setup (which i walked her through over the phone), she has fallen in love with the games she now has access to. if my 80 year old grandma can figure this out, then i think most people will find it pretty simple to use.    pros:  -easy to setup (even for an 80 year old)  -functional layout and design  -syncs with amazon account for and easy way to purcahse apps. i can purchase an app for my grandma from my computer, and it will show up right on her kindle.  -unlimited cloud storage for photos (my grandma is no longer afraid she is going to lose precious pictures of her kids)  -bright screen and great for reading    cons:  limited storage space (16gb is great for most people, but will fill up fast if you take a lot of video)    ***update: i updated my review. i ordered this for my grandma who told me that there was no power adapter included. turns out she left it in the box. so far so good.

product_title: Fire HD 7, 7" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB
review_body:
i bought my tablet fire hd 7 at best buy on the day it came out. i hadn't planned on it, but the amazon rep was there and it was during their tablet trade i promotion. i had a couple old tablets i traded in and he was dropping off the new fire hds. i played with a demo and was impressed, so i got it.

screen - my work tablet is a samsung galaxy tab s 10.5, which has the most beautiful screen i have ever seen. that being said, the brightness, contrast and color on the 7" fire screen is really good for the money. streaming hd video from amazon and netflix looks great and the text on books is crisp and clear.

hardware and build quality - everything works just as i would expect. it is fast enough that i never feel limited, the 16 gig model has just enough storage, 1 gig of ram is adequate for the size and software, the cameras are useable, especially for video, the speakers are loud and have good mid - range tone, it's build quality is robust and it is very utilitarian in design and battery life is perfect at around 8 hours with a 90% charge in around 2 hours when plugged in.

the only reason i gave 4 stars is that the play store has more apps than the amazon app store, but not detrimentally so. also some of the games are glitchy, but that is most likely due to the new hardware not being optimized in the software yet.

i call this the accord of tablets because for the price it does everything very well. it isn't the fastest, sexiest or most feature rich, but for the money, there is nothing better.
